An excerpt from The Forgotten Books of Eden, Edited By Rutherford H. Platt, Jr – The Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs – The Testament of Judah

The Testament Of Judah

The Fourth Son of Jacob and Leah.

CHAP. I. Judah, the fourth son of Jacob and Leah. He is the giant, athlete, warrior; he recounts heroic deeds. He runs so fast that he can outstrip a hind.

THE copy of the words of Judah, what things he spake to his sons before he died.

2 They gathered themselves together, therefore, and came to him, and he said to them: Hearken, my children, to Judah your father.

3 I was the fourth son born to my father Jacob; and Leah my mother named me Judah, saying, I give thanks to the Lord, because He hath given me a fourth son also.

4 I was swift in my youth, and obedient to my father in everything.

5 And I honoured my mother and my mother's sister.

6 And it came to pass, when I became a man, that my father blessed me, saying, Thou shalt be a king, prospering in all things.

7 And the Lord showed me favour in all my works both in the field and in the house.

8 I know that I raced a hind, and caught it, and prepared the meat for my father, and he did eat.

9 And the roes I used to master in the chase, and overtake all that was in the plains.

10 A wild mare I overtook, and caught it and tamed it.

11 I slew a lion and plucked a kid out of its mouth.

12 I took a bear by its paw and hurled it down the cliff, and it was crushed.

13 I outran the wild boar, and seizing it as I ran, I tore it in sunder.

14 A leopard in Hebron leaped upon my dog, and I caught it by the tail, and hurled it on the rocks, and it was broken in twain

15 I found a wild ox feeding in the fields, and seizing it by the horns, and whirling it round and stunning it, I cast it from me and slew it.

16 And when the two kings of the Canaanites came sheathed, in armour against our flocks, and much people with them, single handed I rushed upon the king of Hazor, and smote him on the greives and dragged him down, and so I slew him.

17 And the other, the king of Tappuah, as he sat upon his horse, I slew, and so I scattered all his people.

18 Achor, the king, a man of giant stature, I found, hurling javelins before and behind as he sat on horseback, and I took up a stone of sixty pounds weight, and hurled it and smote his horse, and killed it.

19 And I fought with this other for two hours; and I clave his shield in twain, and I chopped off his feet, and killed him.

20 And as I was stripping off his breastplate, behold nine men his companions began to fight with me,

21 And I wound my garment on my hand; and I slung stones at them, and killed four of them, and the rest fled.

22 And Jacob my father slew Beelesath, king of all the kings, a giant in strength, twelve cubits high.

23 And fear fell upon them, and they ceased warring against us.

24 Therefore my father was free from anxiety in the wars when I was with my brethren.

25 For he saw in a vision concerning me that an angel of might followed me everywhere, that I should not be overcome.

26 And in the south there came upon us a greater war than that in Shechem; and I joined in battle array with my brethren, and pursued a thousand men, and slew of them two hundred men and four kings.

27 And I went up upon the wall, and I slew four mighty men.

28 And so we captured Hazor, and took all the spoil.

29 And the next day we departed to Aretan, a city strong and walled and inaccessible, threatening us with death.

30 But I and Gad approached on the east side of the city, and Reuben and Levi on the west.

31 And they that were upon the wall, thinking that we were alone, were drawn down against us.

32 And so my brothers secretly climbed up the wall on both sides by stakes, and entered the city, while the men knew it not.

33 And we took it with the edge of the sword.

34 And as for those who had taken refuge in the tower, we set fire to the tower and took both it and, them.

35 And as we were departing the men of Tappuah seized our spoil, and seeing this we fought with them.

36 And we slew them. all and recovered our spoil.

37 And when I was at the waters of Kozeba, the men of Jobel came against us to battle.

38 And we fought with them and routed them; and their allies from Shiloh we slew, and we did not leave them power to come in against us.

39 And the men of Makir came upon us the fifth day, to seize our spoil; and we attacked them and overcame them in fierce battle: for there was a host of mighty men amongst them, and we slew them before they had gone up the ascent.

40 And when we came to their city their women rolled upon us stones from the brow of the hill on which the city stood.

41 And I and Simeon had ourselves behind the town, and seized upon the heights, and destroyed this city also.

42 And the next day it was told us that the king of the city of Gaash with. a mighty host was coming against us.

43 I, therefore, and Dan feigned ourselves to be Amorites, and as allies went into their city.

44 And in the depth of night our brethren came and we opened to them the gates; and we destroyed all the men and their substance, and we took for a prey all that was theirs, and their three walls we cast down.

45 And we drew near to Thamna, where was all the substance of the hostile kings.

46 Then being insulted by them, I was therefore wroth, and rushed against them to the summit; and they kept slinging against me stones and darts.

47 And had not Dan my brother aided me, they would have slain me.

48 We came upon them, therefore, with wrath, and they all fled; and passing by another way, they fought my father, and he made peace with them.

49 And we did to them no hurt, and they became tributary to us, and we restored to them their spoil.

50 And I built Thamna, and my father built Pabael.

51 I was twenty years old when this war befell. And the Canaanites feared me and my brethren.

52 And I had much cattle, and I had for chief herdsman Iram the Adullamite.

53 And when I went to him I saw Parsaba, king of Adullam; and he spake unto us, and he made us a feast; and when I was heated he gave me his daughter Bathshua to wife.

54 She bare me Er, and Onan and Shelah; and two of them the Lord smote: for Shelah lived, and his children are ye.

CHAP. II. Judah describes some archeological findings, a city with walls of Iron and gates of brass. He has an encounter with an adventuress.

AND eighteen years my father abode in peace with his brother Esau, and his sons with us, after that we came from Mesopotamia, from Laban.

2 And when eighteen years were fulfilled, in the fortieth year of my life, Esau, the brother of my father, came upon us with a mighty and strong people.

3 And Jacob smote Esau with an arrow, and he was taken up wounded on Mount Seir, and as he went he died at Anoniram.

4 And we pursued after the sons of Esau.

5 Now they had a city with walls of iron and gates of brass; and we could not enter into it, and we encamped around, and besieged it.

6 And when they opened not to us in twenty days, I set up a ladder in the sight of all and with my shield upon my head I went up, sustaining the assault of stones, upwards of three talents weight; and I slew four of their mighty men.

7 And Reuben and Gad slew six others.

8 Then they asked from us terms of peace; and having taken counsel with our father, we received them as tributaries.

9 And they gave us five hundred cors of wheat, five hundred baths of oil, five hundred measures of wine, until the famine, when we went down into Egypt.

10 And after these things my son Er took to wife Tamar, from Mesopotamia, a daughter of Aram.

11 Now Er was wicked, and he was in need concerning Tamar, because she was not of the land of Canaan.

12 And on the third night an angel of the Lord smote him.

13 And he had not known her according to the evil craftiness of his mother, for he did not wish to have children by her.

14 In the days of the wedding feast I gave Onan to her in marriage; and he also in wickedness knew her not, though he spent with her a year.

15 And when I threatened him he went in unto her, but he spilled the seed on the ground, according to the command of his mother, and he also died through wickedness.

16 And I wished to give Shelah also to her, but his mother did not permit it; for she wrought evil against Tamar, because she was not the daughters of Canaan, as she also herself was.

17 And I knew that the race of the Canaanites was wicked, but the impulse of youth blinded my mind.

18 And when I saw her pouring out wine, owing to the intoxication of wine I was deceived, and took her although my father had not counselled it.

19 And while I was away she went and took for Shelah a wife from Canaan.

20 And when I knew what she had done, I cursed her in the anguish of my soul.

21 And she also died through her wickedness together with her sons.

22 And after these things, while Tamar was a widow, she heard after two years that I was going up, to shear my sheep, and adorned herself in bridal array, and sat in the city Enaim by the gate.

23 For it was a law of the Amorites, that she who was about to marry should sit in fornication seven days by the gate.

24 Therefore being drunk with wine, I did not recognize her; and her beauty deceived me, through the fashion of her adorning.

25 And I turned aside to her, and said: Let me go in unto thee.

26 And she said: What wilt thou give me? And I gave her my staff, and my girdle, and the diadem of my kingdom in pledge.

27 And I went in unto her, and she conceived.

28 And not knowing what I had done, I wished to slay her; but she privily sent my pledges, and put me to shame.

29 And when I called her, I heard also the secret words which I spoke when lying with her in my drunkenness; and I could not slay her, because it was from the Lord.

30 For I said, Lest haply she did it in subtlety, having received the pledge from another woman.

31 But I came not again near her while I lived, because I had done this abomination in all Israel.

32 Moreover, they who were in the city said there was no harlot in the gate, because she came from another place, and sat for a while in the gate.

33 And I thought that no one knew that I had gone in to her.

34 And after this we came into Egypt to Joseph, because of the famine.

35 And I was forty and six years old, and seventy and three years lived I in Egypt.

CHAP. III. He counsels against wine and lust as twin evils. "For he who is drunken reverenceth no man." (Verse 13).

AND now I command you, my children, hearken to Judah your father, and keep my sayings to perform all the ordinances of the Lord, and to obey the commands of God.

2 And walk not after your lusts, nor in the imaginations of your thoughts in haughtiness of heart; and glory not in the deeds and strength of your youth, for this also is evil in the eyes of the Lord.

3 Since I also gloried that in wars no comely woman's face ever enticed me, and reproved Reuben my brother concerning Bilhah, the wife of my father, the spirits of jealousy and of fornication arrayed themselves against me, until I lay with Bathshua the Canaanite, and Tamar, who was espoused to my sons.

4 For I said to my father-in-law: I will take counsel with my father, and so will I take thy daughter.

5 And he was unwilling but he showed me a boundless store of gold in his daughter's behalf; for be was a king.

6 And he adorned her with gold and pearls, and caused her to pour out wine for us at the feast with the beauty of women.

7 And the wine turned aside my eyes, and pleasure blinded my heart.

8 And I became enamoured of and I lay with her, and transgressed the commandment of the Lord and the commandment of my fathers, and I took her to wife.

9 And the Lord rewarded me according to the imagination of my heart, inasmuch as I had no joy in her children.

10 And now, my children, I say unto you, be not drunk with wine; for wine turneth the mind away from, the truth, and inspires the passion of lust, and leadeth the eyes into error.

11 For the spirit of fornication hath wine as a minister to give pleasure to the mind; for these two also take away the mind of man.

12 For if a man drink wine to drunkenness, it disturbeth the mind with filthy thoughts leading to fornication, and heateth the body to carnal union; and if the occasion of the lust be present, he worketh the sin, and is not ashamed.

13 Such is the inebriated man, my children; for he who is drunken reverenceth no man.

14 For, lo, it made me also to err, so that I was not ashamed of the multitude in the city, in that before the eyes of all I turned aside unto Tamar, and I wrought a great sin, and I uncovered the covering of my sons' shame.

15 After I had drunk wine I reverenced not the commandment of God, and I took a woman of Canaan to wife.

16 For much discretion needeth the man who drinketh wine, my children; and herein is discretion in drinking wine, a man may drink so long as he preserveth modesty.

17 But if he go beyond this limit the spirit of deceit attacketh his mind, and it maketh the drunkard to talk filthily, and to transgress and not to be ashamed, but even to glory in his shame, and to account himself honourable.

18 He that committeth fornication is not aware when he suffers loss, and is not ashamed when put to dishonour.

19 For even though a man be a king and commit fornication, he is stripped of his kingship by becoming the slave of fornication, as I myself also suffered.

20 For I gave my staff, that is, the stay of my tribe; and my girdle, that is, my power; and my diadem, that is, the glory of my kingdom.

21 And indeed I repented of these things; wine and flesh I eat not until my old age, nor did I behold any joy.

22 And the angel of God showed me that for ever do women bear rule over king and beggar alike.

23 And from the king they take away his glory, and from the valiant man his might, and from the beggar even that little which is the stay of his poverty.

24 Observe, therefore, my children, the right limit in wine; for there are in it four evil spirits--of lust, of hot desire, of profligacy, of filthy lucre.

25 If ye drink wine in gladness, be ye modest in the fear of God.

26 For if in your gladness the fear of God departeth, then drunkenness ariseth and shamelessness stealeth in.

27 But if ye would live soberly do not touch wine at all, lest ye sin in words of outrage, and in fightings and slanders, and transgressions of the commandments of God, and ye perish before your time.

28 Moreover, wine revealeth the mysteries of God and men, even as I also revealed the commandments of God and the mysteries of Jacob my father to the Canaanitish woman Bathshua, which God bade me not to reveal.

29 And wine is a cause both of war and confusion.

30 And now, I command you, my children, not to love money, nor to gaze upon the beauty of women; because for the sake of money and beauty I was led astray to Bathshua the Canaanite.

31 For I know that because of these two things shall my race fall into wickedness.

32 For even wise men among my sons shall they mar, and shall cause the kingdom of Judah to be diminished, which the Lord gave me because of my obedience to my father.

33 For I never caused grief to Jacob, my father; for all things whatsoever he commanded I did.

34 And Isaac, the father of my father, blessed me to be king in Israel, and Jacob further blessed me in like manner.

35 And I know that from me shall the kingdom be established.

36 And I know what evils ye will do in the last days.

37 Beware, therefore, my children, of fornication, and the love of money, and hearken to Judah your father.

38 For these things withdraw au from the law of God, and blind the inclination of the soul, and teach arrogance, and suffer not a man to have compassion upon his neighbour.

39 They rob his soul of all goodness, and oppress him with toils and troubles, and drive away sleep from him, and devour his flesh.

40 And he hindereth the sacrifices of God; and he remembereth not the blessing of God, he hearkeneth not to a prophet when he speaketh, and resenteth the words of godliness.

41 For he is a slave to two contrary passions, and cannot obey God, because they have blinded his soul, and he walketh in the day as in the night.

42 My children, the love of money leadeth to idolatry; because, when led astray through money, men name as gods those who are not gods, and it causeth him who hath it to fall into madness.

43 For the sake of money I lost my children, and had not my repentance, and my humiliation, and the prayers of my father been accepted, I should have died childless.

44 But the God of my fathers had mercy on me, because I did it in ignorance.

45 And the prince of deceit blinded me, and I sinned as a man and as flesh, being corrupted through sins; and I learnt my own weakness while thinking myself invincible.

46 Know, therefore, my children, that two spirits wait upon man-the spirit of truth and the spirit of deceit.

47 And in the midst is the spirit of understanding of the mind, to which it belongeth to turn whithersoever it will. And the works of truth and the works of deceit are written upon the hearts of men, and each one of them the Lord knoweth.

49 And there is no time at which the works of men can be hid; for on the heart itself have they been written down before the Lord.

50 And the spirit of truth testifieth all things, and accuseth all; and the sinner is burnt up by his own heart, and cannot raise his face to the judge.

CHAP. IV. Judah makes a vivid simile concerning tyranny and a dire prophecy concerning the morals of his listeners.

AND now, my children, I command you, love Levi, that ye may abide, and exalt not yourselves against him, lest ye be utterly destroyed.

2 For to me the Lord gave the kingdom, and to him the priesthood, and He set the kingdom beneath the priesthood.

3 To me He gave the things upon the earth; to him the things in the heavens.

4 As the heaven is higher than the earth, so is the priesthood of God higher than the earthly kingdom, unless it falls away through sin from the Lord and is dominated by the earthly kingdom.

5 For the angel of the Lord said unto me: The Lord chose him rather than thee, to draw near to Him, and to eat of His table and to offer Him the first-fruits of the choice things of the sons of Israel; but thou shalt be king of Jacob.

6 And thou shalt be amongst them as the sea.

7 For as, on the sea, just and unjust are tossed about, some taken into captivity while some are enriched, so also shall every race of men be in thee: some shall be impoverished, being taken captive, and others grow rich by plundering the possessions of others.

8 For the kings shall be as sea-monsters.

9 They shall swallow men like fishes: the sons and daughters of freemen shall they enslave; houses, lands, flocks, money shall they plunder:

10 And with the flesh of many shall they wrongfully feed the ravens and the cranes; and they shall advance in evil in covetousness uplifted, and there shall be false prophets like tempest, and they shall persecute all righteous men.

11 And the Lord shall bring upon them divisions one against another.

12 And there shall be continual wars in Israel; and among men of another race shall my kingdom be brought to an end, until the salvation of Israel shall come.

13 Until the appearing of the God of righteousness, that Jacob, and all the Gentiles may rest in peace.

14 And He shall guard the might of my kingdom for ever; for the Lord aware to me with an oath that He would not destroy the kingdom from my seed for ever.

15 Now I have much grief, my children, because of your lewdness and witchcrafts, and idolatries which ye shall practise against the kingdom, following them that have familiar spirits, diviners, and demons of error.

16 Ye shall make your daughters singing girls and harlots, and ye shall mingle in the abominations of the Gentiles.

17 For which things' sake the Lord shall bring upon you famine and pestilence, death and the sword, beleaguering by enemies, and revilings of friends, the slaughter of children, the rape of wives, the plundering of possessions, the burning of the temple of God, the laying waste of the land, the enslavement of yourselves among the Gentiles.

18 And they shall make some of you eunuchs for their wives.

19 Until the Lord visit you, when with perfect heart ye repent and walk in all His commandments, and He bring you up from captivity among the Gentiles.

20 And after these things shall a star arise to you from Jacob in peace,

21 And a man shall arise from my seed, like the sun of righteousness,

22 Walking with the sons of men in meekness and righteousness;

23 And no sin shall be found in him.

24 And the heavens shall be opened unto him, to pour out the spirit, even the blessing of the Holy Father; and He shall pour out the spirit of grace upon you;

25 And ye shall be unto Him sons in truth, and ye shall walk in His commandments first and last.

26 Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; and from your root shall arise a stem; and from it shall grow a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, to judge and to save all that call upon the Lord.

27 And after these things shall Abraham and Isaac and Jacob arise unto life; and I and my brethren shall be chiefs of the tribes of Israel:

28 Levi first, I the second, Joseph third, Benjamin fourth, Simeon fifth, Issachar sixth, and so all in order.

29 And the Lord blessed Levi, and the Angel of the Presence, me; the powers of glory, Simeon; the heaven, Reuben; the earth, Issachar; the sea, Zebulun; the mountains, Joseph; the tabernacle, Benjamin; the luminaries, Dan; Eden, Naphtali; the sun, Gad; the moon, Asher.

30 And ye shall be the people of the Lord, and have one tongue; and there shall be there no spirit of deceit of Beliar, for he shall be cast into the fire for ever.

31 And they who have died in grief shall arise in joy, and they who were poor for the Lord's sake shall be made rich, and they who are put to death for the Lord's sake shall awake to life.

32 And the harts of Jacob shall run in joyfulness, and the eagles of Israel shall fly in gladness; and all the people shall glorify the Lord for ever.

33 Observe, therefore, my children, all the law of the Lord, for there is hope for all them who hold fast unto, His ways.

34 And he said to them: Behold, I die before your eyes this day, a hundred and nineteen years old.

35 Let no one bury me in costly apparel, nor tear open my bowels, for this shall they who are kings do; and carry me up to Hebron with you.

36 And Judah, when he had said these things, fell asleep; and his sons did according to all whatsoever he commanded them, and they buried him in Hebron, with his fathers.

An excerpt from The Forgotten Books of Eden, Edited By Rutherford H. Platt, Jr – The Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs – The Testament of Judah

text:
No outside plan can force a lasting peace if one side’s ruling factions still treat the other’s destruction as the goal. The workable path is narrower than the slogans on either side.

First, Hamas and groups with the same program have to be removed from power and disarmed. Their attack on October 7, 2023, and their founding refusal to accept a Jewish state, make them incompatible with any durable settlement. A ceasefire that leaves them armed and in control of Gaza simply resets the clock. Gaza needs a government that does not run its schools, media, and budgets on the promise of eliminating Israel.

Second, any agreement has to trade recognition for security, not land for promises. Israel would need recognized borders it can defend, demilitarization of the Palestinian territory next to it, and an end to the demand that millions of descendants of 1948 refugees move into Israel proper—that demand is a demographic veto on Israel’s existence, not a return to lost houses. Palestinians would need a real, contiguous territory they govern themselves, an end to new settlement expansion on land meant for that territory, and economic access that does not depend on tunnels and smuggling.

Third, the split between the West Bank and Gaza has to be settled by Palestinians themselves. A deal with the Palestinian Authority means little if Gaza remains a separate armed camp. Past offers that came close to a two-state map—in 2000 and 2008—failed because Palestinian leaders would not accept finality: no further claims, no “right of return” into Israel, and recognition of Israel as the Jewish state. Those terms are still the minimum for Israel; without them, Israeli voters will not evacuate territory again after the 2005 Gaza withdrawal was followed by rockets and October 7.

Outside powers can help only at the margins: stop funding factions that reject those terms, tie reconstruction aid to disarmament and school reform, and drop the pretense that provisional court measures or casualty counts substitute for a political decision to live beside the other side. If that decision never comes, the conflict continues as managed deterrence, not as a solved peace.

text:
You have sided with the devil.

Judaism and the Sins of Israel: On the Essential Nature of Religion
Israel, an "artificial state" established by Zionists, has brought immense catastrophe to Palestine and the Middle East, exerting a profound and unsettling impact on the global order while severely jeopardizing humanity's faith in justice. To enable a clearer discernment of the true nature of Judaism and the state of Israel, distinguish right from wrong, and offer humanity a glimmer of hope to rectify deviations and restore justice, this article systematically delineates their multiple transgressions.
1. Blaspheming God and Serving the Devil
Does God exist? It is a question to which no definitive empirical answer can be given. Yet, for any religion, the existence of God is an absolute certainty—a Supreme Being who created the universe and will ultimately deliver it. Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.
When a religion becomes pathologically insular yet fiercely unified for collective self-enrichment, it must perpetually extract illicit advantages from the external world to fulfill its internal theological promises and suppress external criticism or interference. This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.
5. The Abuse of Violence to Perpetrate Genocide
For nearly eighty years, Zionist forces in Palestine have systematically displaced the indigenous population, brutally massacred and incarcerated Palestinians, and relentlessly expanded illegal settlements. This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. Their resistance is fundamentally just, whereas Israel constitutes the actual terrorist entity.
6. Constructing an Invisible Empire Parasitic Upon Modern States
By tightly binding religious identity to material self-interest, the Zionist cartel has engineered an invisible empire that effectively reigns supreme over sovereign nations. Leveraging their monopolized financial wealth and sprawling media conglomerates, they exert deep, manipulative control over Western political landscapes. This insular, self-serving apparatus utilizes aggressive financial lobbying to transmute the hard-earned tax dollars of foreign citizens into their own political leverage, ultimately hijacking the foreign policies of major global powers. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

Despite the reality that certain factions within the Jewish populace remain bound by a nexus of religion and self-interest—forming an invisible, crushing force capable of flattening any individual resistance to suppress anti-Zionist critiques—there are still courageous Jewish individuals who actively resist Israeli policies and oppose draconian anti-Semitism legislation. Though born into the fold of Judaism, their conscience and commitment to justice have triumphed over institutional evil. They represent the true pride of the Jewish people and the sole beacon of hope for their eventual moral redemption.

text:
An on-ground procurement team of roughly 80–90 people scans devices and quotes directly, which lets GNG deal with the corporate rather than only through intermediaries.
What the corporate gets in return is not only a cheque. GNG pays upfront, issues ESG and e-waste documentation, and provides certified data wiping. Those three items — liquidity, EPR compliance, and data security — are why large companies prefer a scaled buyer over a local scrap dealer.
Sharad Khandelwal MD said in the Q1 FY27 call that procurement is lumpy, not a steady weekly buy. They take whole lots when a corporate, bank or lessor disposes, because splitting the lot loses control of the material and cuts the margin. The edge on the buy side is data wipe, sustainability paperwork, and the ability to take the entire lot in one shot.
The example he gave: a large US bank offered about 60,000 higher-generation desktops “at a very good price.” Taking the full lot was, in his words, a huge margin; buying less would have limited it. On the sell side, an Australian customer took 3,000 laptops in one order only because GNG had the stock.
They buy from banks, leasing companies, corporates, IT-asset disposition partners and recyclers. Q3 FY26 call: relationships are what keep supply coming, and they are “buying stock ahead of price increases at every level.” They also said companies may defer new purchases or extend leases, which shrinks future disposition, so they are widening the supplier list and buying early.
Stock is held in three buckets — raw, semi-finished and finished. They want 30–40 days of finished goods so a school or enterprise can get one model immediately. That availability, he said, is itself a price advantage. The business is working-capital heavy and has almost no fixed machinery.
What they said on price
They will not put a buy-price on a device. When an analyst asked how much procurement cost had risen against a 12–13% rise in selling price, Khandelwal said they had procured “at almost the similar prices” and were “able to secure material at the old prices because of our contracts and because of all the associated services.” Used-laptop prices, he added, are trailing new-laptop prices, not moving in tandem.
Q4 FY26 call: strategic inventory was “bought at comfortable prices, we have not bought them at higher price,” and “input cost has not risen that significantly.” June 2026 interview: they carry “significant inventory purchased at the old prices,” and try to hold the selling price at about 30% of a new computer. Selling price trails the new-laptop rise by one or two quarters.
3. Stage two — the 21-step refurbishment
Founder and MD Sharad Khandelwal has repeatedly described a proprietary 21-step process that includes paint, fabrication and LCD work, and brings the device to a “state of new” on both performance and looks. The company has not published the numbered checklist of all 21 steps. What is disclosed, and what third-party facility notes confirm, is the following sequence.
Disclosed elements of the process
Intake and grading of the bulk lot; serial capture and chain of custody.
Certified data sanitisation (BitRaser is a named partner) so the corporate seller’s data is gone before the device re-enters the market.
Hardware diagnostics across the board, battery, storage, keyboard, ports and thermals.
Component replacement where needed — battery, keyboard, screen, storage, memory — rather than scrapping the machine. Management calls this “repair over replacement.”
Board-level repair, including motherboard servicing, which smaller shops generally cannot do.
LCD work, including repolarisation, plus cosmetic restoration: painting, fabrication, chassis repair.
Genuine software reload under the Microsoft Authorised Refurbisher (MAR) programme. GNG is India’s largest MAR by refurbishing capability. Devices go out with genuine Windows and original-brand chargers and packaging.

text:
We need to stop calling every course chatbot an “AI tutor.” That fallacy is already leading to "research" (square quotes intended) that is impacting institutional decision-making.

A new University of Maryland study reports lower average course grades and lower LMS participation in sections offered an AI study assistant. @morganmundum  and I looked at what was actually tested (mostly based on Morgan's analysis, augmented by Stephen J. Aguilar):

• Only about 15% of students offered access ever used the tool.
• The default mode provided answers. Only two instructors ended the term with tutoring mode enabled.
• Nearly 74% of student requests sought information, explanations, or solutions. Less than 1% sought feedback on students’ own attempts.
Putting course documents behind a chatbot does not automatically create tutoring. Tutoring should identify what a student understands, diagnose misunderstandings, and adapt guidance accordingly.
Likewise, putting a tool inside the LMS does not establish that instructors integrated it into their teaching.

The lower grades and participation deserve attention. But the study does not establish that using an AI tutor caused students to learn less. At best, the study measures the effects of *offering this particular intervention with no scaffolding*, with limited adoption and an unresolved explanation for the declines.

There is useful evidence here about a poorly-designed chatbot rollout. Presenting it as evidence about “AI tutoring” stretches that contribution into something the study barely tested.

Availability is not adoption. Answer delivery is not automatically tutoring. Course grades and LMS activity do not tell the whole learning story.

text:
Moshe breaks off contact in October 2025. Earlier he had written me a lengthy article where he sticks to his guns and repeats all his pro-Israeli views and tells me that even though he likes me  a person he cannot be friends with someone who bashes Israel the way I do. Maybe in another life. Then a year later, almost to the day, he sends me a voice message saying how he misses me and that he doesn't have a connection like he has with me with anyone else on this planet. Meaning someone to profoundly disagree with without things dissolving into a shouting match and also someone who holds radically different views, but enriches his private life. 

He also writes that what he fears is that there is a small possibility that I do manage to show him that what he's been supporting passionately turns out to be evil. He calls that 'green-pilling', a word I encounter for the first time. He says he heard a lot of things from me he had never considered before. I respond that the same is true from my side. 

The next day he has an offer that takes me by surprise. He offers to attend a seminar in Virginia, the topic happens to be an aspect of psychology. The reason he asks is that there we would have plenty of time in between workshops to debate Palestine-Israel issues. 

He also offers that after the seminar we could fly to Israel together. Since there is a real chance I get barred from entering the country because of what I write online being accompanied by him may override that security concern. 

The seminar turns out to be fully booked and I don't meet the requirements, because having participated in an earlier seminar is mandatory. 

I lost a dear friend because he sided with Israel, Markus, in 2025 and now am invited to something that is almost a consummate Williamesque programme: 
- psychology
- debate Palestine issues for a week with someone who has the vocabulary and the background to do it, even if we disagree profoundly on several key aspects, I'll learn something 
- the seminar takes place right smack dab in American Civil War territory and the ACW is one of my earliest and most intense obsessions 

I'd be lying if I can fully express how baffling all this is. Here I am genuinely, deeply, loathing, with a hard to describe intensity often sliding into outright hatred, practically all Israelis who have ever commented on Palestine online and then an Israeli who - horror!!! - defends Israel's attack on Iran almost feels like a brother to me. 

Most people online instantly drop me if I do not replicate their opinion 100 percent accurately. Some even drop me if the posts coinciding with their views are... too long. 

The human experience never ceases to shower me with inexplicable contradictions. 

In an attempt to understand those contradictions better there is now of course always AI to turn to and so I do. 

I will do something my ego experiences as diminishment and almost like dereliction of duty: I will not have the last word. 

I will let AI have the last word: 

'You and Moshe are giving each other something neither of you can manufacture alone: an encounter with a mind that refuses to submit, attached to a person you nevertheless don't want to lose.
Most political debate is about defeating the other person. This relationship seems to have become about discovering how much disagreement two people can withstand without ceasing to recognize each other's humanity.'

text:
SPACEX AND BROADCOM WANT TO BORROW MORE THAN $90 BILLION FOR AI CHIPS. ASIA OPENED THURSDAY IN THE RED:

Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Hong Kong and Shanghai are all lower at midday Thursday, and the mainland's early gain after its weeklong holiday is gone. The verdict: Asia is selling because borrowing keeps getting more expensive, not because of trouble in any one industry. Late Wednesday the AI build-out joined the line of borrowers. US stock futures have not reacted, so New York's first real test arrives at 1pm ET, when the Treasury sells 30-year bonds into that same line.

Asia so far, each from its last close, as of about 11:15pm ET:

- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 69,373, -662 points / -0.95%.
- Topix (Japan): 4,092.09, -62.02 points / -1.49%.
- KOSPI (South Korea): 6,721.42, -82.48 points / -1.21%.
- Taiwan Weighted Index: 49,496.99, -309.38 points / -0.62%.
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 23,984.84, -145.66 points / -0.60%.
- Hang Seng Tech (Hong Kong): 4,118.18, -76.31 points / -1.82%.
- Shanghai Composite: 3,833.28, -8.91 points / -0.23%, from its September 30 close.

The losses are spread wide: Japan's broader Topix is down more than the Nikkei, and Hong Kong's tech shares are down most of all.

The common thread is what Washington pays to borrow. Treasury yields, as of 11:30pm ET:

- 10-year: 5.309%, +0.032 percentage point from Wednesday's close.
- 30-year: 5.697%, +0.036 percentage point from Wednesday's close.

Monday's 10-year close of 5.311% was the highest since May 2002. When a safe government bond pays that much, a stock has to promise more to compete, and every company that borrows pays more too.

Oil is feeding it. Brent crude, the global benchmark:

- $102.32 a barrel, +$2.12 / +2.12% from Wednesday's settlement.

It has climbed most of the night, from about $101 at 8pm ET, with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia this week and a storm now aimed at the oil-producing US Gulf. At 11pm ET the National Hurricane Center put up a hurricane warning from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Florida Panhandle; Tropical Storm Isaias is expected ashore late Friday or early Saturday. Dearer oil keeps inflation alive, which keeps pushing yields up.

Late Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX and Broadcom are each lining up tens of billions of dollars of borrowed money to pay for AI chips.

SpaceX (SPCX) at $167.60, -$4.32 / -2.51% on Wednesday, and $168.50 after hours, +$0.90 / +0.54% from that close.

The rocket, Starlink internet and AI company plans about $40 billion of borrowing, Reuters reported:

- Investment-grade bonds, the kind companies with strong credit sell: $30B.
- Loans: $10B.

SpaceX ended June with about $100 billion of cash and investments. It spent $15.8 billion on AI in the June quarter alone, and it is borrowing anyway. On Wednesday the cost of insuring its bonds against default hit a record. SpaceX sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists: its 92% jump in June-quarter sales is the speed the Hypergrowth Len5 hunts, but one quarter as a public company is too short a record to show growth that lasts.

Broadcom (AVGO) at $376.51, +$0.70 / +0.19% on Wednesday, and $376.70 after hours, +$0.19 / +0.05% from that close.

The chip and networking company is in early talks to raise more than $50 billion of private financing to make custom AI chips. Broadcom sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists either: at about 48 times its past year of profit, the discount the value styles wait for is missing.

Both stocks edged up after the report. New York's investors did not treat the borrowing as a worry; Asia's did. Nigel Green, chief executive of the adviser deVere Group, put it this way: the AI build-out is "increasingly running on credit," and borrowed money must be repaid on schedule whether the AI sales arrive or not.

The strongest fact against all this: lenders are still showing up. Wednesday's 10-year sale:

- Sold: $39B at 5.300%.
- Bids: 2.77 times the amount on offer.
- Dealers' share: about 2.5%.

Dealers are the big banks that take whatever other buyers leave, so a small share means strong demand. That sale pulled the 10-year back from 5.326% earlier Wednesday, its highest in 24 years. And much of the AI money will be spent on chips and memory, the industry that dominates the stock markets in Seoul and Taipei. Those markets are falling anyway, which says investors care more tonight about the price of money than about the orders it buys.

US stock futures, from Wednesday's 4pm close:

- S&P 500 futures: 7,850.00, -2.75 points / -0.04%.
- Nasdaq-100 futures: 31,408.50, +6.25 points / +0.02%.
- Dow futures: 51,378.00, -71.00 points / -0.14%.
- Russell 2000 futures: 2,806.80, -5.40 points / -0.19%.

All four sit within two tenths of a percent of Wednesday's close. New York has not taken Asia's cue, and overnight moves often fade before the 9:30am ET open. The hint for the open is a quiet start, with the real test after lunch.

Next, Eastern time:

- 3am: Shanghai closes, and London, Frankfurt and Paris open.
- 8:30am: the Labor Department's weekly count of first-time unemployment claims, week ended October 3. Prior week: 197,000.
- 1pm: the Treasury sells $22B of 30-year bonds.
- Late Friday or early Saturday: Isaias makes landfall.

What would change this read: a strong 30-year sale, with yields easing after it, would make Asia's morning look like nerves. A weak one, with dealers stuck holding a big share and the 10-year past 5.326%, would say lenders want more to fund governments and AI builders at once, and New York would have Asia's reason to sell.

The question this morning leaves open: is a dollar of AI spending worth as much to investors when it is borrowed at today's rates as when it came from cash? Seoul and Taipei leaned toward no. New York's first chance to answer is the 30-year sale at 1pm.

Not investment advice.

text:
Good morning you lovely lot.

It’s Friday Eve! Although I’m on holiday, so frankly I’ve lost all concept of what day it is. 😂

Well, today marks my final day at Disney’s Caribbean Beach Resort. Cases packed, everything accounted for, and I’m preparing for the gruelling seven-mile expedition to the Hard Rock Hotel at Universal for my final four days.

I’ve considered packing sandwiches for the journey, but I think I’ll manage. 😂

Last night’s final Disney meal was at the Riviera Resort, and I have to say, the food was absolutely bloody amazing. Pictures below.

There were children present, naturally, but thankfully these appeared to be the less feral variety. No screaming, no climbing furniture, and nobody attempting to recreate the Normandy landings using bread rolls.

Which was reassuring, considering the price of the wine.

$52. FOR ONE GLASS. 🍷

I asked the waiter for a recommendation, and would you believe it, he recommended the most expensive glass on the menu.

What an extraordinary coincidence. 😂

Then came the ceremonial presentation of the cork, which was shoved under my nose as though I was supposed to detect subtle notes of oak, blackberries and a Frenchman called Pierre.

Mate, I’m from Yorkshire.

It could’ve been a £5 bottle from Asda for all I know.

I gave it a sniff and nodded thoughtfully, like I knew what I was doing.

At $52, I was half expecting the grapes to have been individually massaged by virgins. 🤣🤣

Meanwhile, the Florida weather has been absolutely shite for the last two days.

I brought shorts, T-shirts and sunglasses. Waterproofs never even entered my head.

Apparently the Sunshine State has decided to identify as Scarborough in November.

Still, skin’s waterproof, and at least I don’t have to worry about my hair getting wet. 😂

Anyway, Disney, it’s been a pleasure. Time to swap Mickey Mouse for rock ‘n’ roll and see what Universal has to offer.

And as always, be kind.

Good manners cost nothing, patience is free, and a little kindness can make somebody’s day.

Unlike a glass of wine at Disney, which apparently requires a second mortgage.

Finally, thank you all for putting up with the absolute shite I’ve been posting about my adventures. I appreciate you humouring me.

Only four more days of this nonsense to endure. 😂

Have a cracking Thursday, folks!

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Friday, October 7, 1966, Braniff International inaugurated the carrier's first jet cargo service to Latin America. Two months earlier in August 1966, Braniff had begun operating overnight jet cargo service to selected domestic locations. The new South America service featured the Airline's new Quick Change Convertible Cargo/Passenger three-engine and four-engine pure Boeing jet aircraft, which were joined by a McDonnell-Douglas DC-8-55F and a DC-8-62CF in 1967.

Braniff's new jet cargo service to Latin America was operated with both Boeing 727-27C Trijets and Boeing 707-327C Intercontinental Jets. The service was operated in conjunction with an interchange agreement with Eastern Airlines and provided jet cargo carriage from New York City to most major South American destinations. Latin American destinations that would receive the new service were Panama City, Panama; Bogota, Colombia; Guayaquil, Ecuador; Lima, Peru; LaPaz, Bolivia; Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Asuncion, Paraguay; and Buenos Aires, Argentina. Eastern Airlines operated Braniff's Boeing 707 Jet Cargo flights to Miami, Florida, where Braniff crews operated the convertible flights to Latin America.

Initially, Braniff offered the flights from New York to South America on Monday, Thursday, and Friday, in the afternoon and nights on Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. The flights featured a unique cabin configuration with cargo loaded in the front of the aircraft and passengers located in the rear compartments. Two preloaded and covered Cloudpack Cargo Cocoons, measuring 88-inches by 108-inches, were raised by a hydraulically operated cargo loader and placed into the Boeing 707 via a large 11-foot wide cargo door located on the left side of the aircraft just behind the first cabin boarding door. A dividing bulkhead separated the passengers from the dual cargo pallets and featured seating for 18 passengers in First Class and 90 in Coach Class.

The new jet cargo schedules were announced by Braniff International Vice President Latin America Charles S. South. Mr. South noted that Braniff would offer 33,000 pounds of cargo capacity on its eight weekly roundtrip cargo/passenger convertible flights between New York and South America. Mr. South said that the new combination cargo/passenger carrying capability combined with the regular lower cargo carrying bins and noted that, "Braniff will be able to move more than three-quarters-of-a-million-pounds of cargo each week between the U.S. and South America.”

Photo: Braniff International Boeing 727-27C registered as N7271 is parked on the Airside Ramp at the Braniff International Operations and Maintenance Base at Dallas Love Field in 1966, shortly after delivery from Boeing. The big Quick Change Jet is painted in the 1965 Alexander Girard Lemon Yellow Solid Color Scheme with White Wings, Engines and Tail with Alexander Girard Sky Font and BI Tail Logo in Black.

text:
My Magnus Opus…

$BULL Xi Jinping gets a state dinner. Webull gets suspicion. Its competitors get a sales opportunity.

Trump hosted Xi at the White House on September 24. Less than two weeks later, Webull’s Chinese connections became the subject of a congressional report and national-security headlines. Diplomacy and security scrutiny can coexist. But that contrast deserves examination: international relationships require nuance at the presidential table, and precise evidence when a company’s reputation is on the line.

“China” cannot do the work of an entire argument.

Our economies are deeply intertwined. The U.S. Energy Information Administration found that China’s reduced crude imports softened upward price pressure during the Hormuz disruption. That does not establish benevolence. It illustrates a relationship whose consequences cannot be explained through a permanent villain narrative.

That complexity belongs in the Webull discussion, too.

The documented facts include substantial Chinese technology operations, concentrated founder voting control, and historical compliance failures. Webull also describes U.S. customer information as domestically stored, with overseas access requiring permission and oversight from U.S. personnel. Those qualifications matter. Being invested does not give me permission to erase them. 

But the published evidence does not establish that Chinese authorities accessed Webull customer data or that customer funds were diverted. The report itself acknowledges that Chinese legal obligations do not prove authorities accessed the data. A possible vulnerability deserves investigation; an established event requires evidence that it happened. 

Then comes the commercial layer.

Public is offering Webull customers a 3% transfer match while emphasizing that their new broker would be a U.S. company headquartered in New York with U.S.-based customer service. Robinhood’s terms introduced a Webull-specific 3% transfer bonus beginning October 7, the day of the report. That is documented competition for these customers’ assets. It does not prove coordination with anyone in government. 

My interpretation is that Public’s pitch turns national identity into a selling point precisely when customers may be anxious about it. Robinhood’s offer gives those same customers a financial reason to move. Whatever the intentions, the commercial incentive is clear: their gain comes from acquiring someone else’s accounts.

A transfer match is a customer-acquisition expense. Attach patriotic meaning to it, and a commercial decision can begin to feel like a civic duty.

That is the political salesmanship I associate with Trump: put a promised financial benefit beside a national story, then invite people to connect their personal reward with allegiance. I am criticizing the persuasion, not alleging that a brokerage promotion or a political promise constitutes illegal bribery.

The distinction matters because a bonus tells us what a company is willing to spend to win business. It tells us nothing about whether another company’s safeguards failed.

And if patriotism enters the sales pitch, I want the economics read just as carefully as the flag. Public’s match is paid over 72 months, with asset removals reducing remaining payments. Robinhood’s bonus carries a five-year retention condition with potential chargebacks. These are arrangements designed to acquire and retain assets. Customers should evaluate them on those terms. 

The bigger picture, to me, is how quickly uncertainty can acquire a price tag. A committee raises concerns. Headlines compress them. Competitors offer a destination and a reward. A customer may encounter the incentive to act before encountering the evidence needed to decide.

That sequence does not require a conspiracy. Separate institutions can pursue separate interests and still produce a powerful combined effect...

text:
ASABA MASACRE
Fifty-nine years on, the Federal Government says it will make a formal reconciliation declaration on the Asaba Massacre.

Acknowledgement is overdue. It is not justice.
On 7 October 1967, federal troops of the Second Division entered Asaba, then a civilian town on the federal side of the Niger.

Unarmed men and boys were gathered at Ogbeosowa Square, told to show loyalty to “One Nigeria”, and shot.
Researchers and community historians put the dead at more than 1,000. The Division was commanded by Colonel Murtala Muhammed. Witnesses have long identified Major Ibrahim Taiwo as the officer who gave the order to fire.

Both men are dead. Death has not closed this case. Their bodies should be exhumed, and justice applied to their corpses...

A nation that buries the killers in honour, and the killed in unmarked ground, has not finished with the crime. Posthumous disgrace is the least a state can offer when the dock is no longer available...

The civilian/military relationship in this country is a history of pain, anguish and cruelty. Asaba was not an aberration. It was a template...

Under Olusegun Obasanjo, the pattern returned in peacetime. Odi in Bayelsa was levelled in November 1999. Zaki-Biam and neighbouring Tiv communities in Benue were razed in October 2001. Odioma followed in 2005. In December 2015, the Army killed hundreds of members of the Islamic Movement in Nigeria in Zaria, and buried many in a mass grave...

War or “peace”, the constant is the same: men in uniform killing unarmed civilians, and the state calling it an operation...

A reconciliation declaration, if it comes, must say what happened, name the victims, and carry a public apology from a sitting President. The Asagba of Asaba, Professor Epiphany Azinge, has already said there will be no closure without that apology...

Delta State has acknowledged the massacre. Nigeria has not. A memorial that preserves names and testimony is the minimum...

Compensation for families who lost fathers, land and a generation is not charity. It is a debt...

Forgiveness cannot be ordered from Abuja. The son of the late Major Taiwo has apologised. That is a family gesture, not a national reckoning...

The men who ordered Asaba are beyond the Hague. They are not beyond history. Those still living who ordered Odi, Zaki-Biam, Odioma and Zaria can still be investigated...

The institution that keeps producing these killings can still be restrained...

Nigeria cannot keep burying civilians and honouring the men who ordered the graves.

text:
You don’t take your shoes off to relax. You take them off because your heels ache from supporting your dead weight against artificial flooring all day. You drop your keys on the console table—keys that open a door to a box where you own neither the walls, nor the copper pipes running through them, nor the air circulating through the vents.
You unpack the groceries. You place the oat milk next to the Greek yogurt. You line up the small glass jars of vitamins: the vitamin D for the sun you never see, the ashwagandha for the stress you are not allowed to express, the magnesium for the sleep your nervous system refuses to grant you. You look at those amber glass bottles and you think you’re practicing "wellness."
Be honest with yourself for thirty seconds: it’s not wellness. It’s industrial livestock maintenance.
If an animal in a factory farm starts pacing in circles, biting its own tail, or shedding its hair from chronic captivity stress, the farm veterinarian doesn’t dismantle the cage; he mixes a sedative powder into the trough so the pig stays upright until the harvest date. That’s your entire supplement shelf. It’s an expensive, self-administered chemical harness designed to keep the biological engine firing on four cylinders so you can make tomorrow morning’s 9:15 AM sprint-planning call without your hands shaking so violently that you spill your coffee on the keyboard.
And what happens at 8:00 PM? You sit on the sofa. That sofa you bought because an algorithmic mood board convinced you that low-profile Scandinavian upholstery would somehow introduce calm into an existence dictated by variable-rate debt.
You open your laptop, or you grab your tablet, or you reach for the television remote. You tell yourself you’re "unwinding." But look at what your eyes are actually doing. You aren't unwinding; you are scanning. You are frantically scrolling through vertical video feeds, through short-form clips of people pretending to cook elaborate stews in clean cabins in Montana, people pretending to give financial advice in tailored suits, people crying in their cars about their student loans, and dogs doing backflips in suburban kitchens.
Your thumb flicks upward every 3.8 seconds. Flick. Flick. Flick.
Each flick is an electrical query sent from your motor cortex down into the silicon layer, asking the exact same desperate, unarticulated question: Is there anything out there that feels real?
And the algorithm answers: No. But look at this.
Notice the posture you adopt while you do it. Your shoulders hunched forward like a vulture over roadkill, your neck angled at forty-five degrees, your mouth slightly open, your breathing shallow, barely reaching the bottom of your lungs. That isn’t recreation. That is the posture of a biological organism entering a state of controlled catatonia to survive an environment that offers zero physical affordances for its natural instincts.
You aren’t lazy. You never were.
You were simply designed by four million years of hominid evolution to run across savannahs, track weather patterns across open horizons, butcher meat with flint, build fires with dry wood, and sit around embers with twenty people whose faces you’ve known since the day you fell out of your mother’s body. You were built for physical struggle, for real fatigue that ends in black, dreamless sleep on hard ground, for songs that aren’t owned by a licensing conglomerate, and for conversations that don’t leave an administrative paper trail in an enterprise cloud.
Instead, they took that magnificent, terrifying, bone-crushing ape, stuffed it into polyester-blend trousers, sat it down beneath four banks of fluorescent lights, and told it that its highest evolutionary calling is to draft an executive summary explaining why the conversion rate on digital banner ads for luxury mattresses dropped by 1.4% in the third fiscal quarter.

text:
新莽 「強弩都尉章」銅印

「強弩都尉章」銅印是一件出自新莽時期（公元9-24年）的軍事銅器，現藏於國立故宮博物院。此銅印長度僅2.2公分，小巧精緻，屬於印章類文物，其上鑄有五字白文印文「強弩都尉章」。其中「都尉」指的是漢代軍隊裡將軍的屬下軍官職稱，顯示該印章為一位負責強弩兵部隊的都尉所用的官印。

印章形制採銅製，並設有鼻鈕以便執握及蓋印。銅質的選用和製作符合當時軍用印章應具的耐用性和識別功能。印面以白文鉤勒字體，筆畫清晰，展現新莽時期銅印的文字工藝水平。由於此印章尺寸不大，使用者多為軍中官員，反映出行政管理中對細節印信的重視。

觀賞此印章時，應特別留意印面五個字的結構與布局，文字排列工整，字形端正，顯示鑄造技術精良。此外，鼻鈕的造型與銅質痕跡亦能反映其鑄造年代和用途。此銅印不只是官職的象徵物，同時也是新莽政權軍事組織編制的一則實物見證。

綜觀整件文物，從其規格和銅印文字，我們得以窺見新莽時代軍隊中都尉的職責範疇以及官印的標準形式。該印章本身未見後世題跋或朱印，保存狀態良好，為研究漢末政權軍事與行政制度提供了實證材料。

這件銅印的簡潔與功能性，充分說明古代中國軍事官印的實用性與象徵性雙重價值。透過此物，現代觀者可觸摸到兩千年前軍事管理的諸多細節，是連結歷史與現實的重要文化遺產。

The bronze seal inscribed with "Qiangnu Duwei Zhang" is a small but significant military artifact from the Xin dynasty period (AD 9-24), currently held by the National Palace Museum in Taipei. Measuring just 2.2 centimeters in length, this seal is crafted of bronze and features five distinct white characters engraved on its surface. The inscription reads "強弩都尉章," which translates roughly to "Seal of the Commander of the Strong Crossbow Troops." The term "duwei" (都尉) identifies a military officer rank—an officer under a general—reflecting a formal military administrative role.

This seal was likely used by a duwei responsible for troops skilled in the use of powerful crossbows, indicating the presence of specialized units in the military framework of the time. The bronze material was chosen not only for its durability but also for its suitability for fine engraving, ensuring the seal’s impression was clear and authoritative.

The seal features a typical "nose knob" or handle used for holding and pressing the seal onto documents or official materials. The white characters are sharply inscribed, with well-balanced strokes arranged harmoniously within the small surface area. This level of craftsmanship reveals the technical skill and artistic conventions of Xin dynasty metalwork and seal engraving.

When viewing the seal, one should pay close attention to the precise structure and layout of the five characters, as these demonstrate orderly design and technical excellence. The nose knob’s shape and traces on the bronze surface also offer clues to its manufacture and function. Importantly, this seal lacks any later inscriptions or collector’s marks, suggesting it has been preserved in a relatively original condition, making it an authentic exemplar for study.

Contextually, this bronze seal provides a rare tangible link to the military and administrative organization under the relatively brief Xin dynasty, a period bridging the Western and Eastern Han. It offers insight into hierarchical military titles and the official tools used by officers at this time. As a functional object, it symbolizes both authority and responsibility within the army.

In sum, the "Qiangnu Duwei Zhang" seal encapsulates the dual nature of military seals in ancient China as both instruments of governance and objects of symbolic power. Through this artifact, contemporary viewers can connect with the everyday workings of command and control in a military structure nearly two millennia ago, underscoring the enduring legacy of Chinese historical craftsmanship and bureaucracy.

text:
On This Day in Holocaust History — October 7

October 7 is now inseparable from Jewish history.

The events of 2023 were not the Holocaust, and the histories must not be equated. But October 7 joined a long Jewish memory of persecution, massacre, resistance, rescue, survival, and renewal.

1934—Jehovah’s Witness congregations throughout Germany sent a coordinated declaration to Adolf Hitler’s government protesting Nazi restrictions on their religious activity. Witnesses in dozens of other countries sent supporting letters and telegrams.
   The declaration affirmed their political neutrality but insisted that they would obey their religious conscience rather than Nazi commands. They refused to give the Hitler salute, swear loyalty to Hitler, serve in the armed forces, participate in Nazi organizations, or abandon their religious work.
   The Nazi regime responded with intensified persecution. Thousands of Jehovah’s Witnesses were arrested; many were sent to concentration camps, where they were identified by purple triangle badges. Unlike most prisoners, Witnesses were sometimes offered release if they signed statements renouncing their faith. The great majority refused.

1939—Hitler appointed Heinrich Himmler Reich Commissioner for the Strengthening of German Nationhood, giving the SS chief sweeping authority to reshape the population of conquered Poland according to Nazi racial ideology.
   Himmler was empowered to transfer ethnic Germans into annexed Polish territories while expelling Jews and Poles, confiscating their property, and eliminating what the decree called the “harmful influence” of populations considered non-German.
   This appointment helped transform Nazi racial theories into an immense administrative program of deportation, dispossession, Germanization, and demographic engineering. Families were removed from their homes so that their land and possessions could be given to ethnic German settlers.
   At the same time, Nazi officials were developing the Nisko or Lublin Plan, which envisioned concentrating Jews in a supposed “reservation” near Lublin in occupied Poland. The first experimental transports began later in October. Many deportees were abandoned without adequate shelter, food, or sanitation; others were driven toward the Soviet occupation zone.
   Although the plan was eventually suspended, it established methods—registration, confiscation, railroad deportation, concentration, and forced labor—that would be employed on a vastly greater scale during the Holocaust.

1940—Germany began deploying a military mission to Romania during the opening days of October. October 7 is sometimes listed as the day German troops entered the country, but contemporary diplomatic reports indicate that the first contingents crossed into Romania during the following days.
   The official purpose was to train the Romanian army and protect the oil fields at Ploiești, which were vital to Germany’s war machine. The deployment also drew the dictatorship of Ion Antonescu more firmly into the Axis alliance.
   Romania formally joined the Tripartite Pact in November and participated in Germany’s 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union. Romanian military and civilian authorities subsequently carried out deportations, pogroms, mass shootings, and deliberate starvation that killed hundreds of thousands of Jews and Roma, particularly in Bessarabia, Bukovina, Odessa, and Transnistria.

October 6–7, 1943—German forces raided hiding places in the Danish fishing town of Gilleleje, one of the principal departure points in the rescue of Denmark’s Jews.
   Approximately 80 Jewish refugees were discovered in the attic of Gilleleje Church and nearby buildings after an informer led German forces to them. Most were deported to the Theresienstadt ghetto-camp.
   Their capture was the largest single tragedy of the Danish rescue. Yet approximately 7,000 Danish Jews escaped to neutral Sweden with the help of resistance members, fishermen, clergy, doctors, police officers, and ordinary citizens.
  Gilleleje demonstrated the power of individual choices. One informer exposed people in hiding; an entire network of others risked their lives to save them.

1944—Jewish Sonderkommando prisoners launched the most significant armed revolt in the history of Auschwitz-Birkenau.
   The Sonderkommando were Jewish prisoners forced to work at the gas chambers and crematoria—removing bodies, extracting gold teeth, cutting hair, and burning the remains of murdered victims. Because they were direct witnesses to mass murder, the SS periodically killed them and replaced them with new prisoners.
   After learning that the SS intended to murder much of their unit, prisoners at Crematorium IV attacked their guards with hammers, axes, stones, and improvised weapons. They set Crematorium IV ablaze using explosives secretly obtained from Jewish women working at the Union munitions factory.
    The revolt spread to prisoners working at other crematoria. Some cut through the camp fence and attempted to flee, but the SS pursued them. Nearly 250 prisoners were killed during the fighting, and approximately 200 more were executed after the uprising was suppressed.
   Crematorium IV was so badly damaged that it was never used again and was later dismantled.
   For months, Ala Gärtner, Ester Wajcblum, Regina Safirsztajn, and other women had smuggled tiny quantities of gunpowder from the factory, hiding it in scraps of cloth and passing it through a clandestine network to Róża Robota and the Sonderkommando resistance.
   The four women were tortured but did not betray the wider underground. The SS hanged them on January 6, 1945—only three weeks before Auschwitz was liberated.
   The revolt did not liberate Auschwitz, and almost none of its participants survived. But inside a place designed to reduce human beings to complete powerlessness, Jewish prisoners fought back, killed SS guards, and disabled part of the machinery of mass murder.

2023—On the Jewish festival of Simchat Torah, Hamas and other armed groups breached Israel’s border from Gaza and attacked communities, military posts, roads, and the Nova music festival.
   Approximately 1,200 people—Israelis and foreign nationals, most of them civilians—were killed. Entire families were murdered in their homes. Hundreds of people were wounded, and 251 men, women, children, elderly people, soldiers, and civilians were abducted into Gaza.
   It was the deadliest single attack against Jews since the Holocaust.

October 7 became a day of mourning for Israel and Jewish communities throughout the world. It also reopened ancient wounds—the knowledge that Jewish homes, families, and communities could again be targeted for destruction simply because they were Jewish or because they lived in Israel.

Yet October 7 is also about Jewish endurance.

In 1944, Jewish prisoners surrounded by the machinery of Auschwitz chose resistance. In 2023, survivors carried children from burning homes, first responders entered communities still under attack, civilians sheltered strangers, and families began the struggle to bring the hostages home.

From expulsions and inquisitions to pogroms and the Holocaust, Jewish history contains immeasurable suffering—but it is not defined by suffering alone. It is also a history of faith, resistance, rebuilding, memory, and survival.

We remember those who were murdered. We stand with the survivors. 

We are still here. We are not going anywhere. Nor is Israel.
