Funny to hear about "terrorist groups" when talking about the army of a country that built its own empire entirely through colonial conquests, crushing uprisings, and concentration camps (fun fact: the British were the first in the world to widely use concentration camps during the Anglo-Boer War).
Let's break down these alleged "claims" through the lens of the British Empire's own actions:
 On being "formed from terrorist groups": The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) were established by a decree of the provisional government in May 1948 by merging Jewish underground militias (Hagana, Irgun, and Lehi) that fought against the colonial British Mandate for the Jewish people's right to their own state. In the exact same way, the British labeled the independence leaders in India, Ireland (IRA), or Cyprus (EOKA) as "terrorists," only to sit down at the negotiating table with them once they won.
 On the lynching of British soldiers: This 1947 incident (the hanging of two Irgun sergeants in retaliation for the British execution of Jewish underground fighters) was a harsh act of retribution under guerrilla warfare conditions. But let's remind the world how many thousands of people the British Crown hanged, shot, and tortured across the globe—from Ireland and Kenya to Palestine itself—enforcing state terror and public executions.
 The rest of the far-fetched conspiracy theories about "explosions in Mexico" or "London 1994" are a standard set of fake claims from tabloid feeds with zero official or historical backing. As for the USS Liberty incident in 1967, it was recognized by both sides as a tragic friendly-fire accident amid the fog of the Six-Day War, for which Israel offered official apologies and paid reparations.
Before pointing fingers at the history of Israel's founding, it wouldn't hurt to recall the methods used to build and maintain the "Pax Britannica"—there's enough blood on the British Crown's hands to fill a dozen history textbooks.

The bishop of Durham at one time bought of a bookseller who was a friend of Tyndale, his whole stock of Bibles, for the purpose of destroying them, supposing that this would greatly hinder the work. But, on the contrary, the money thus furnished, purchased material for a new and better edition, which, but for this, could not have been published. 

When Tyndale was afterward made a prisoner, his liberty was offered him on condition that he would reveal the names of those who had helped him meet the expense of printing his Bibles. He replied that the bishop of Durham had done more than any other person; for by paying a large price for the books left on hand, he had enabled him to go on with good courage.

Interesting how God worked through Tyndale

text:
Approximately 55% of investment in AI companies comes from other AI companies. Among the 1,246 AI companies tracked between 2021 and 2025, 28.7% of their outward investments went to other AI companies, while 55.2% of the capital flowing into AI companies originated from other AI companies.

The precise scale of circular financing
Share of "explicitly circular" transactions. The BIS defines these as transactions where the investor also maintains a commercial supply relationship with the investee. By transaction count, such "explicitly circular" deals account for only 16.1% of AI-to-AI transactions; however, by transaction value, they represent 46.4%. This implies that larger transactions are more likely to involve both equity investment and supply contracts.

Investors acting as suppliers. In 64% of these circular relationships, the investor also serves as a supplier of products or services to the investee. This pattern is particularly concentrated within the AI ​​industry: 73% of circular investment relationships originate from companies in the computing power or infrastructure layers.

In February 2026, Nvidia invested $30 billion in OpenAI and subsequently provided a residual value guarantee of up to $105 billion for OpenAI’s data center project in Ohio. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress acknowledged during an earnings call that demand from AI labs backed by Nvidia’s capital would account for approximately one-quarter of the company's business in the coming year.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has denied that these transactions are "circular," arguing that "they do their business, and we do ours." However, an analysis by the *Financial Times* offers a more precise characterization: this is not a "circular" arrangement in the strict sense (which implies no real value creation), but rather a "back-to-back" transaction—where Nvidia uses equity investments to enable customers to purchase products they otherwise could not afford.

Historical Analogy: Vendor Financing in the Telecom Sector
The BIS explicitly draws parallels between the current model and the vendor financing prevalent during the late-1990s telecom boom. At that time, equipment manufacturers like Cisco provided financing to network operators, enabling them to purchase the manufacturers' own equipment. When operator revenues slowed, both purchasing and repayments declined; this exacerbated the 2000 dot-com crash, leaving equipment suppliers exposed to both slumping sales and financial losses.

Key Differences from the Telecom Bubble. The *Financial Times* notes several distinctions regarding today's AI circular transactions: Nvidia supports customers through equity investments rather than loans; these investments do not necessarily flow directly back into chip purchases; and Nvidia retains equity stakes in the investee companies rather than merely acting as a lender. Yet, the core risk structure remains similar: the supplier acts simultaneously as investor, guarantor, and beneficiary of the orders.

Distinguishing the Boundaries
"Circular financing" is not synonymous with "fraud." Analyses by both the BIS and the *South China Morning Post* clarify that these are not fraudulent "round-trip" transactions involving fictitious deals. They possess a genuine economic rationale: suppliers often have better insight into a customer's business prospects than external investors do, and financing can stimulate demand for their own products.

The real risks lie in "transparency" and "dual exposure." The BIS points out that if end-user demand slows, a company could face weak revenues while simultaneously being obligated to honor financing commitments. More specifically, a firm that both invests in and supplies another company faces a double blow if the customer runs into trouble: the impairment of its equity investment and a drop in orders. Many AI companies are privately held, and publicly disclosed transactions may conflate equity investments, long-term purchase commitments, and guarantees—some of which, such as residual value guarantees for chips or data center equipment, remain off-balance-sheet until stressed conditions arise. The core fact is that more than half of the external capital in the AI ​​industry originates from within the sector itself. Large-scale deals, in particular, tend to bundle equity investments with supply contracts. This flywheel can keep accelerating as long as end-market demand remains robust; however, if a problem arises at any point in the chain, these same financial linkages transmit the resulting stress throughout the entire ecosystem. This is not fraud, but rather a form of structural interdependence, the consequences of which hinge on whether external demand can ultimately take over from the industry's internal self-financing.

Papdi;

Śiṣya:  Gurudev, if what I earn becomes useful to those who are less fortunate, I do not feel that I am missing anything in the material world. I feel that Bhagavān gives me exactly what I need, when I need it. Is this contentment?

Guru: If you truly feel no deprivation while giving, and no superiority while possessing, then there is contentment. But examine yourself carefully. Sometimes a man says, “I need nothing,” while secretly desiring recognition for his renunciation. 

Contentment is known not by what a man possesses, but by what possesses his mind.

Śiṣya:  Then is wealth itself an obstacle to a devotee?

Guru: No, my son. Wealth is an instrument. Attachment to wealth is the obstacle. A poor man may be deeply attached to one coin, while a wealthy man may hold millions without allowing them to enter his heart. Do not judge the bondage by the quantity of possessions.

Śiṣya: Then why do some wealthy people build beautiful temples, invite saints, offer elaborate hospitality and listen to discourses, yet do not seem to practise?

Guru: Has not surrendered fully towards the principles of practice.  Perhaps he has not yet understood the true essence of its blessings,  hearing is only the beginning. 

A man may feed a hundred sādhus and still not be able to feed one hungry impulse within himself with discrimination.
He may build a temple outside and still have no shrine of silence within.
He may listen to the words of the wise for years and yet never allow one word to correct his conduct.

等々力渓谷を歩くと、水辺の魚、湿地の植物、渓谷の地層、横穴古墳などによる日本の歴史など様々な勉強が出来るので子供を連れて行く人々が多い。
 
等々力渓谷公園
等々力渓谷、武蔵野台地の南端に位置する延長約１kmの渓谷です。谷沢川が多摩川と合流する手前で、多摩川が形成した河岸段丘、いわゆる国分寺崖線の浸食によってできた、東京都内でもめずらしい渓谷として知られています。
 
「等々力」の地名は、渓谷内の「不動の滝」の音が響き渡り「轟いた」ところからついた、との言い伝えがあります。滝の上部には、平安時代に役の行者の霊場とされた等々力不動尊があり、かってはこの滝に打たれて行をする修行僧が各地から訪れたといいます。
 
渓谷内には「等々力渓谷第３号横穴古墳」があります。これは谷沢川東斜面の崖に群集している横穴のひとつで、古墳時代の末期から奈良時代のものと推定されています。－－－－

Many people take their children to Todoroki Valley because a walk through it offers a wide variety of educational experiences, from observing aquatic life and wetland plants to studying the valley’s geological strata and learning about Japanese history through ancient tunnel tombs.
Todoroki Valley Park
Todoroki Valley is a roughly one-kilometer-long ravine located at the southern edge of the Musashino Plateau. Just before the Yazawa River merges with the Tama River, it passes through an area eroded by the Kokubunji Cliffline—a river terrace formed by the Tama River. This makes Todoroki famous as a rare and unique valley within the Tokyo metropolitan area.
According to local legend, the name "Todoroki" comes from the word todoroita (roared/thundered), describing how the sound of the Fudo Waterfall echoed throughout the valley. Situated above the waterfall is Todoroki Fudoson Temple, which was established as a sacred site by En no Gyoja during the Heian period. It is said that Buddhist monks from various regions once traveled here to practice ascetic training under the cascading water.
Inside the valley lies the "Todoroki Valley No. 3 Tunnel Tomb" (Yokoana Kofun). This is one of a cluster of side-chamber tombs built into the cliff on the eastern slope of the Yazawa River, and is estimated to date from the late Kofun period to the Nara period.
— From the inscription on the stone monument in Todoroki Valley

ตลอดหลายทศวรรษที่ผ่านมา ชุมชน LGBTQIAN+ ไทย รวมถึงพันธมิตร ได้ร่วมกันสร้างรากฐานที่จับต้องได้จริง ทั้งนโยบายเมือง ระบบสุขภาพ กฎหมาย วัฒนธรรม และเศรษฐกิจสร้างสรรค์ รากฐานเหล่านี้ทำให้กรุงเทพฯ พร้อมเป็นเจ้าภาพ WorldPride 2030 พร้อมต้อนรับผู้คนจากทั่วโลก และพร้อมขยายเสียงของเอเชียให้ดังขึ้นบนเวทีโลก ไปทำความรู้จักกับทุกเหตุผลกันว่า ทำไมต้องเป็นกรุงเทพฯ 

🔻 English below 🔻

▪️A CITY ADVANCING GENDER EQUALITY — เมืองแรกในเอเชียที่ได้รางวัล Gold

กรุงเทพฯ เป็นเมืองแรกในเอเชียที่ได้รับรางวัลระดับ Gold จาก UNDP Gender Equality Seal ด้วยคะแนน 94.8% ผ่านเกณฑ์ 38 จาก 40 ตัวชี้วัดสากล สะท้อนเจตจำนงทางการเมืองที่ชัดเจนในการขับเคลื่อนความเท่าเทียมทางเพศ ผ่านนโยบายอย่างผ้าอนามัยฟรี BKK Pride Clinics และสิทธิลาคลอด 120 วัน

▪️PRIDE CLINICS — คลินิกที่เป็นมิตรและใกล้บ้าน

กรุงเทพมหานครมี BKK Pride Clinics 31 แห่งในศูนย์บริการสาธารณสุขทั่วเมือง ให้บริการคำปรึกษา ดูแลสุขภาพจิต และตรวจสุขภาพทางเพศอย่างปลอดภัยใกล้บ้าน

▪️HEALTHCARE NETWORK — เครือข่ายสุขภาพที่ขยายการเข้าถึง

ผู้ให้บริการทั้งภาครัฐ เอกชน มหาวิทยาลัย และชุมชน ร่วมกันขยายการเข้าถึงบริการสุขภาพ ตั้งแต่ Chula Pride Clinic, GACC รามาธิบดี และ Siriraj Pride Clinic ไปจนถึงองค์กรชุมชนอย่าง Tangerine Clinic, SWING, RSAT, Mplus, Sisters และ IPULSE ที่ทำงานภายใต้หลัก "By the Community, For the Community" ทั้งยังมีการบำบัดด้วยฮอร์โมนเพื่อการยืนยันเพศที่อยู่ในระบบหลักประกันสุขภาพถ้วนหน้า

▪️MARRIAGE EQUALITY IN PRACTICE — จากกฎหมายสู่ชีวิตจริง

สมรสเท่าเทียมมีผลบังคับใช้เมื่อ 23 มกราคม 2025 ทำให้ไทยเป็นประเทศแรกในอาเซียน และเป็นประเทศลำดับที่ 38 ของโลก ภายในปีแรกมีคู่รักจดทะเบียนกว่า 30,000 คู่ โดย 87% เป็นคู่หญิง-หญิง และมีการอบรม SOGIESC ให้เจ้าหน้าที่ครบทั้ง 928 อำเภอ

▪️LEGAL PROGRESS — กฎหมายที่เดินหน้าต่อจากสมรสเท่าเทียม

สมรสเท่าเทียมคือความสำเร็จที่ได้มาจากการต่อสู้ของชุมชน ไม่ใช่ของขวัญจากรัฐ และงานยังไม่จบ เรายังต้องผลักดันสิทธิความเป็นพ่อแม่ การแก้กฎหมายลำดับรองอีก 50 ฉบับ และกฎหมายรับรองเพศสภาพ เพื่อให้ความเท่าเทียมเป็นจริงอย่างสมบูรณ์

▪️TRANS VISIBILITY — เวทีที่เปลี่ยนการมองเห็นให้เป็นการขับเคลื่อน

ไทยเป็นบ้านของเวทีระดับโลกอย่าง Miss Tiffany's Universe และ Miss International Queen ที่ยืนหยัดเรื่องการมองเห็นและสิทธิมนุษยชนมากว่า 40 ปี จากเวทีมหาวิทยาลัยจนถึงงานวัดทั่วประเทศ วันนี้ผู้ครองตำแหน่งและนักแสดงจำนวนมากใช้พื้นที่ของตัวเองเพื่อเรียกร้องความเป็นธรรมทางสังคมและการเปลี่ยนแปลงเชิงนโยบาย

▪️THAI DRAG STARS — จากเวทีท้องถิ่นสู่ผู้นำระดับโลก

Gawdland สร้างประวัติศาสตร์เป็นแชมป์ชาวเอเชียคนแรกของ RuPaul's Drag Race UK vs the World (2026) ขณะที่ Drag Arena ซึ่งเป็นไอพีของคนไทย 100% ถูกส่งออกไปยังไต้หวันและมาเลเซีย กรุงเทพฯ ยังมีเทศกาลอย่าง Drag Bangkok และเวทีอย่าง Drag Star ที่ส่งศิลปินไทยไปสู่สายตานานาชาติ

▪️BL, GL & FILM — เรื่องเล่าของเราที่เดินทางไปทั่วโลก

ซีรีส์ BL และ GL ไทยส่งออกไปกว่า 80 ประเทศ อุตสาหกรรมมีมูลค่าราว 5,000 ล้านบาท เติบโตเฉลี่ยปีละ 17–20% และไทยครองสัดส่วนการผลิตกว่า 55% ของเอเชีย ควบคู่กับภาพยนตร์ไทยที่เล่าเรื่องความหลากหลายและได้รับรางวัลบนเวทีเทศกาลนานาชาติ

▪️CELEBRATION & HOSPITALITY — เมืองที่พร้อมเปิดบ้านต้อนรับ

แคมเปญ "Go Thai Be Free" ของการท่องเที่ยวแห่งประเทศไทยยืนยันว่าไทยเป็นจุดหมายที่ปลอดภัยและเปิดกว้าง กรุงเทพฯ เป็นศูนย์กลางของงานระดับโลกอย่าง White Party Bangkok, gCircuit และ Songkran SK ทั้งยังมีย่านสีลมและถนนข้าวสารที่ต้อนรับความหลากหลาย และมรดกคาบาเรต์กว่า 50 ปีที่กลายเป็นไอคอนทางวัฒนธรรม

▪️A GLOBAL STAGE FOR ASIAN VOICES — พื้นที่ปลอดภัยของเพื่อนร่วมภูมิภาค

เอเชียมีประชากรมากกว่าครึ่งหนึ่งของโลก แต่ยังเป็นภูมิภาคที่จำกัดสิทธิ LGBTQIAN+ มากที่สุดแห่งหนึ่ง ส่วนใหญ่ยังไม่รับรองคู่รักเพศเดียวกัน และบางประเทศยังมีโทษถึงขั้นประหารชีวิต โดย WorldPride ที่กรุงเทพฯ จะเป็นพื้นที่ไร้พรมแดนให้พี่น้องจากทั่วเอเชียได้ส่งเสียง และส่งแรงกระเพื่อมว่าความเท่าเทียมเป็นสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นได้จริงในเอเชีย

▪️THE ROAD TO 2030 — วัดความก้าวหน้าและกำหนดก้าวต่อไป

ปี 2030 จะครบรอบห้าปีของสมรสเท่าเทียม และครบ 32 ปีนับจาก Pride ครั้งแรกของกรุงเทพฯ ในปี 1998 เป็นจังหวะที่เราจะพิสูจน์ว่าพลังจากรากหญ้าได้กลายเป็นการเปลี่ยนแปลงที่ยั่งยืน

ภายใต้แนวคิด "Until All of Us Are Free" กรุงเทพฯ พร้อมแล้วที่จะต้อนรับโลก และพร้อมจะทำให้ WorldPride 2030 เป็นคำมั่นระยะยาวต่อความเท่าเทียม ศักดิ์ศรี และเสรีภาพของทุกคน

🏳️‍🌈 WHY BANGKOK?

Over the past decades, Thailand's LGBTQIAN+ communities and their allies have built real foundations—city policy, healthcare, law, culture, and a creative economy. These foundations make Bangkok ready to host WorldPride 2030, welcome people from around the world, and amplify Asia's voices on the global stage. Discover every reason why it should be Bangkok.

▪️ A CITY ADVANCING GENDER EQUALITY — Asia's first 'Gold' city

Bangkok is the first city in Asia to receive the Gold award from the UNDP Gender Equality Seal, scoring 94.8% and meeting 38 of 40 international indicators—through initiatives including free sanitary pads, BKK Pride Clinics, and 120-day maternity leave.

▪️ PRIDE CLINICS — Stigma-free care close to home

31 BKK Pride Clinics within public health centres offer counselling, mental health support, and sexual health screening near people's homes.

▪️ HEALTHCARE NETWORK — More providers, wider access

Public, private, university, and community-led providers expand access to care—from Chula Pride Clinic, GACC at Ramathibodi, and Siriraj Pride Clinic, to community organisations like Tangerine Clinic, SWING, RSAT, Mplus, Sisters, and IPULSE working "By the Community, For the Community." Gender-affirming hormone therapy is covered under Universal Health Coverage.

▪️ MARRIAGE EQUALITY IN PRACTICE — From law to lived reality

Effective 23 January 2025, marriage equality made Thailand the first country in Southeast Asia and the 38th in the world to recognise same-sex marriage. Over 30,000 couples registered in the first year—87% of them female-female—and SOGIESC training now covers all 928 districts.

▪️ LEGAL PROGRESS — Advancing dignity beyond the law

Marriage equality was hard-won, not a gift, and the legal journey is far from over. The work continues: parental rights, amendments to 50 subsidiary laws, and legal gender recognition—so that dignity keeps advancing beyond the law.

▪️ TRANS VISIBILITY — Stages that turn visibility into advocacy

Thailand is home to Miss Tiffany's Universe and Miss International Queen, setting the benchmark for visibility and human rights for over 40 years—from university stages to temple fairs across the country. Today's titleholders and performers use their platforms to champion social equity and policy reform.

▪️ THAI DRAG STARS — From local stages to global leadership

Gawdland made history as the first Asian winner of RuPaul's Drag Race UK vs the World (2026). Drag Arena, a 100% Thai-owned IP, has been exported to Taiwan and Malaysia, while Drag Bangkok and Drag Star launch local artists into the international spotlight.

▪️ BL, GL & FILM — Our stories, travelling the world

Thai BL and GL series reach over 80 countries. The industry is worth around THB 5,000 million (~USD 140 million), grows 17–20% a year, and Thailand produces over 55% of Asia's output—alongside award-winning Thai films telling diverse stories.

▪️ CELEBRATION & HOSPITALITY — A city ready to open its doors

The Tourism Authority of Thailand's "Go Thai Be Free" initiative affirms Thailand as a safe, inclusive destination. Bangkok hosts White Party Bangkok, gCircuit, and Songkran SK; welcomes all in Silom and Khaosan Road; and carries a cabaret legacy of more than 50 years.

▪️ A GLOBAL STAGE FOR ASIAN VOICES — A sanctuary for the region

Asia holds over half the world's population, yet remains one of the most restrictive regions for LGBTQIAN+ rights—most countries still do not recognise same-sex couples, and some still punish them with death. WorldPride in Bangkok would create a borderless space for our siblings across Asia—and send a clear message that equality is an achievable Asian reality.

▪️ THE ROAD TO 2030 — Measuring progress, shaping what comes next

2030 marks five years of marriage equality and 32 years since Bangkok's first Pride in 1998—the moment to prove that grassroots power has become lasting change.

Guided by "Until All of Us Are Free", Bangkok is ready to welcome the world and make WorldPride 2030 a lasting commitment to equality, dignity, and freedom for all.

text:
Dan Burmawi gets the hardest parts right. October 7 was the worst massacre of Jews since the Holocaust: about 1,200 killed, 251 taken hostage, and a UN envoy found reasonable grounds to believe women were raped. Five Arab armies did invade in 1948. Khartoum's three no's were real. Israel did return Sinai, did leave Lebanon and Gaza, and got rockets from Gaza for it.

Here's the half his post skips.

The migrants. A joint British-American inquiry counted them in 1946: Palestine's Muslim population grew by 472,000 between 1922 and 1944, and 19,000 of that was immigration. The rest was natural growth.

"Everyone in the region got a state." Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Iraq did. The Arab majority of Palestine didn't, then or now.

Jews were under a third of the population and owned under 7% of the land. The UN plan offered them 56%. Israel finished the war holding 78%. Israel's own army intelligence, in June 1948, attributed roughly 70% of the Arab flight to that point to Jewish military operations. Israel refused the UN's call to let the refugees go home, then passed a law handing their property to the state.

Khartoum came in September, after that war, not before it. That same month, Israel's Foreign Ministry legal adviser warned in a top-secret memo that "civilian settlement in the administered territories contravenes the explicit provisions of the Fourth Geneva Convention." The settlements went up anyway. More than half a million Israelis live in them today, not counting East Jerusalem. That isn't necessity.

Shlomo Ben-Ami, one of Israel's negotiators at Camp David and later its foreign minister: "If I were a Palestinian I would have rejected Camp David, as well." So much for everything they asked for.
Ariel Sharon's top aide, Dov Weisglass, told Haaretz what the Gaza pullout was for: "The significance of our disengagement plan is the freezing of the peace process."

October 7 was Hamas. The bill went to all 2.1 million people in Gaza. In January, an Israeli army official said the army accepts a death toll of about 70,000.

Burmawi asks what Israel should do. His own post has the answer: when peace was possible, it gave land back. Do that again, and stop building on the land it kept.

I mean, Trump can't get through a speech without insulting Paxton because even he knows how unpopular, corrupt, smarmy and revolting Paxton is as a candidate and human being.

And the fact that this election is now leaning in Talarico's favor doesn't bode well for Republicans nationwide.

Which is why Republicans are grasping at straws to distract from Ken Paxton being the worst candidate for Senate in decades; stooping to AI generated and ad-hominen attacks, culture war claptrap and pathetic lies about Talarico that only play well with a base of hysterical halfwits.

Paxton winning his primary was a GIFT to Democrats. He's going to alienate voters and convince them stay home because he's so rotten and repellent.

Paxton has been involved in countless scandals and has an extensive history of fraud, bribery, corruption, graft and adultery 

HE ALSO OFFERED CLEMENCY TO A CHILD SEX ABUSER. Birds of a feather and all that...

His closest aides also reported him to the FBI in 2020 for abusing his office and he was impeached by his own party!

Do you know how corrupt you have to be to get impeached by Texas Republicans as a slavishly pro Trump Republican?

These things make him a top contender to MAGA, but it's not MAGA Republicans who will decide this election.

Talarico has a real and increasingly likely chance of defeating a scumbag like Paxton. The two couldn't be farther apart in every way that matters.

Talarico is the better candidate. He has a cleaner record and a more sophisticated platform other than "vote for me because I'll do Trump's bidding." 

His lack of scandals stands in stark contrast to Paxton's.

He has a genuine desire to represent his constituents and actually has a moral compass.

So Republicans are having to resort to teasing him like insufferable children because they cannot, in good faith, attack his popular positions.

Then there Talarico's faith—a huge selling point for him in Texas.

He's a far better representation of Christian ethics than Paxton.

Talarico went to seminary school but still believes strongly in the separation of church and state.

He criticizes all forms of state sponsored religion. Unlike MAGA, he chooses the constitution and American ideals over religious nationalism.

He calls out the religious right on their hypocrisy, says that Jesus advocated for the sick, the needy, the poor, and contextualizes the lessons of Jesus as a guide on how to be more tolerant, respectful, and accommodating of marginalized segments of our society.

Talarico sees Christian ethics and progressivism as compatible. As opposed to "Christians" on the right who see religion and ideologies of white nationalism as synonymous with one another.

With Talarico's message about the class conflict and his relatable frustrations aimed at the rich and corporations; with his authentic religious background; his emphasis on equality; his distaste for culture wars; and his populist-progressive appeal, he will win against a disgrace like Paxton who has demonstrated a PREFERENCE for corruption, depravity, dishonesty, criminality and fraud. 

Remember also that Talarico's primary win in Texas was lifted by Hispanic voters.

Trump has lost over half his support from Hispanic voters since the 2024 election.

This election will be decided by a voting bloc that Trump has deeply alienated.

Talarico also supports democratic ideals like equality, a notion that enrages MAGA because they perceive equality as oppression.

He supports public education and the social safety net.

He criticizes billionaires and their outsized influence over our elections and policy making decisions.

Talarico condemns Super PACS and has massive grassroots support. As opposed to Paxton who is relying on billionaires and big dollar donors.

The GOP is terrified of Talarico; haunted by the idea of a progressive Christian and fear that they could lose to someone who represents the interests of the people for once.

text: “Transparency” by Oliver R: an apparition at the threshold of the visibleWith Transparency, Oliver R extends and deepens one of his most fertile intuitions: the kaleidoscope as a mental space rather than a mere backdrop. After Doll K, in which a figure from the Dolls collection already conversed with a floral and chromatic explosion, the artist tightens the motif. The kaleidoscope is no longer a scattered field of colors; it contracts, deepens, and becomes a tunnel.The background is now bichrome: deep blue and burning orange. Perspective turns it into a hypnotic corridor, a succession of petals or scales receding toward a central point. We are no longer facing a decorative pattern, but inside an optical device. The gaze is drawn in. The kaleidoscope ceases to be an object one turns in one’s hands; it becomes a passage. At the center of this vortex appears a creature immediately recognizable as one of Oliver R’s Dolls — those hybrid beings, halfway between a luxury collectible doll, a Parisian department-store mannequin, and an animated character. Yet she is not sharp. She is an apparition. Her presence hovers at the edge of transparency, as if the tunnel both revealed and dissolved her. She does not fully occupy the space: she haunts it.Seated cross-legged, in a pose at once meditative and ceremonial, she wears a jumpsuit with dense blue and red patterns, almost like tapestry. On her head, a red headdress hesitates between turban and veil. Earrings, a necklace of red beads, red slippers: red returns as a connecting thread, both ornamental and ritual. On her right hand, a tattoo remains hard to decipher — a discreet, almost private sign that anchors the figure in a story the viewer will never be able to read completely.The eyes are closed. The nose and mouth are fine. The face does not express absence, but concentrated inwardness. Unlike many previous Dolls, often frozen in a wide, slightly uneasy gaze, this one has withdrawn. She does not look at us. She is elsewhere, or more deeply here.The title Transparency is not incidental. It resonates with the theme of a contemporary exhibition devoted to the interplay of light, layers, and perception. Oliver R does not treat transparency as a merely optical quality. He makes it an existential condition of his Dolls. These figures have always oscillated between object and living being, between artificial perfection and a nearly human emotion. Here, that oscillation becomes literal: the creature is both fully present and already fading into the pattern that surrounds her.The blue-and-orange kaleidoscope is no longer a background. It is the very medium in which the figure exists. Its repetitive, concentric forms evoke at once a mandala, an optical machine, and an organism. The tunnel-like perspective suggests an inner journey as much as a visual trap. One cannot tell whether the Doll appeared at the bottom of the kaleidoscope or whether the kaleidoscope was born from https://t.co/517pLwuCt9 Oliver R’s work, the Dolls are never mere mannequins. They carry a memory, a slight unease, an elegance a little too perfect to be reassuring. Transparency pushes this ambiguity further. By making the figure less sharp, more spectral, the artist does not weaken her presence: he makes it more insistent. What is not entirely visible demands more attention. Here one finds the artist’s signature: a cocktail of Pop Art, Surrealism, and digital Art Brut, obtained by assembling artificial intelligences and digital tools, then fixed in a unique work also intended for physical existence — fine-art paper, dibond, framing, anti-reflective plexiglass. But beyond technique, Transparency marks a shift. The kaleidoscope no longer illustrates a state of mind. It is the theater of that state.The creature with closed eyes, crowned in red, seated at the center of a tunnel of blue and orange, does not offer a single interpretation. She may be meditating, sleeping, absent, or simply dissolving into the pattern that brought her forth. Faithful to his method, Oliver R imposes nothing. He installs an atmosphere, a color, a tension between the sharp and the blurred, and leaves the gaze to do the rest.Transparency is not merely a new piece in the Dolls collection. It is the moment when the kaleidoscope stops surrounding the figure and begins to pass through her.

text:
#ThrowbackThursday In October 1947, NEGRO DIGEST ™ published a groundbreaking article by sociologist Horace Cayton tracking down the top 10 metropolitan areas for Black Americans during the historic Second Great Migration. 🏙️✨

Rather than a strict ranking, he highlighted 10 areas offering the absolute best balance of manufacturing jobs, homeownership, education, and social freedom. 📈💼

Here are the top 10 cities from 1947:

🏙️ CHICAGO, ILLINOIS: Cayton’s own home base, booming with political representation and a massive Black-owned business district! 🏬🔥

🌴 LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA: Called the "Promised Land" because of its great weather, high homeownership rates, and the legendary jazz scene on Central Avenue! 🎶🎷

🏢 CLEVELAND, OHIO: Celebrated for its growing civil service sectors and open paths to municipal employment. 💼📌

🚗 DETROIT, MICHIGAN: Fueled by booming automotive manufacturing jobs that brought some of the highest blue-collar wages in the nation! 🛠️💰

🗽 NEW YORK, NEW YORK: Harlem held unparalleled cultural dominance, backed by strong union integration and progressive anti-discrimination laws. 🎭⚖️

⛪ PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA: Known for its deeply rooted Black middle class, rich professional networks, and church-led civic power. 🙏🏾⚓

🏭 PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA: Powered by steel mill jobs and the massive national footprint of the Pittsburgh Courier newspaper. 📰🏗️

✈️ SEATTLE, WASHINGTON: A West Coast favorite featuring rapid wartime aviation/shipyard job growth and a highly progressive public school system. 📚⚓

🌉 SAN FRANCISCO / OAKLAND, CALIFORNIA: Evaluated together as a massive Bay Area hub with open shipyard labor unions and unmatched postwar wages! 🚢💵

🌲 MINNEAPOLIS / ST. PAUL, MINNESOTA: A surprise entry praised for its high literacy rates, robust public integration, and low crime rates. 📈🤝

⚠️ Cayton's Reality Check: While these cities offered massive opportunities, Cayton explicitly warned readers that none were free from systemic racism. Even the "best" cities faced severe housing segregation, intense overcrowding, and restrictive covenants. 🛑🏘️

text:
The name was Operation Epic Fury

It promised a quick, decisive victory. Instead, it has produced a growing pile of wrecked American aircraft, dead aircrew, and a bill that keeps climbing.

On February 28, 2026, the United States, working with Israel, launched what it called a military campaign against Iran. The fighting spread across the air, the sea, and the missile ranges of the Middle East. Iran's armed forces and its regional allies answered the aggression. Combat slowed during an April ceasefire. Within weeks, some strikes resumed. Conditions remain fluid.

On September 14, 2026, the Department of Defense published a Lead Inspector General report to Congress on the operation. The Department, which under Executive Order 14347 of September 5, 2025, has also used a secondary Department of War designation, assessed certain equipment losses tied to Washington's operations against Iran between April 1 and June 30.

Some analysts and department officials have offered varying estimates for replacing what was lost, including aircraft. In September 2026, the Congressional Budget Office estimated the cost of equipment losses as of August 1 at between $1.9 billion and $3.3 billion, depending on department plans for replacements.

Those figures likely understate the true cost to American taxpayers. And they overstate Washington's ability to sustain the war.

What follows is a working count of 81 fixed wing and rotary wing aircraft, including drones, that reports indicate were lost or damaged in Washington's war against Iran since February 28. The count draws on news reporting, statements from the Department of Defense and CENTCOM, and the DOD Inspector General, which Congress designated as Lead IG for the operation.

The total remains subject to revision because of classification, continuing combat, and attribution questions. Some damaged aircraft may have been put back into service. Even so, the pattern is clear: Iran and its defenders have imposed a real price on American air power.

Twelve F15E Strike Eagles.

On March 2, 2026, CENTCOM admitted that three F15Es were destroyed by American friendly fire over Kuwait. A humiliating loss, caused by Washington's own forces.

On April 5, 2026, CENTCOM reported one F15E destroyed over Iran. Another American fighter lost to Iranian defenses.

Then, on September 9 and 10, 2026, multiple reports said eight F15s were lightly damaged in an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. They later returned to service. The strike showed that Iran can reach high value bases and aircraft.

One F35A Lightning II.

A March 19, 2026, report said Iranian ground fire damaged one F35A over Iran. It punctured the myth of American stealth invulnerability.

Two A10 Thunderbolt IIs.

On April 6, 2026, Air Force General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said enemy fire struck one A10. It crashed and was destroyed.

On September 9 and 10, 2026, reports citing U.S. officials said one A10 was severely damaged in an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.

Seven KC135 Stratotankers.

On March 12, 2026, CENTCOM reported an incident involving two KC135s. One crashed in Iraq, killing all six aircrew. The second made an emergency landing. The loss weakened Washington's ability to keep its air campaign fueled.

A March 14, 2026, report said an Iranian attack damaged five KC135s on the ground at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia.

One E3 Sentry.

A March 28, 2026, report said one E3 was damaged at Prince Sultan Air Base.

A September 15, 2026, report said the aircraft took "a direct hit." The strike targeted a scarce and aging American command platform.

Two MC130J Commando IIs.

An April 5, 2026, report said two MC130Js supporting search and rescue for a downed F15E were intentionally destroyed. The American rescue effort turned into a self inflicted loss.

One HH60W Jolly Green II.

On April 6, 2026, General Caine said at a press conference that one HH60W sustained damage during search and rescue for a downed F15E in Iran.

One MQ4C Triton.

An April 14, 2026, report citing a U.S. Navy document said one MQ4C crashed in a mishap. Washington's expensive surveillance fleet continues to suffer.

Three MQ1 drones.

On May 31, 2026, CENTCOM reported that Iran shot down a "U.S. MQ1 drone."

A September 17, 2026, report citing U.S. officials said Iran had "in recent days" downed "at least two" MQ1 aircraft.

Forty five MQ9 Reapers.

An August 13, 2026, report citing three U.S. officials said the U.S. military had lost "at least 45" MQ9 Reapers in operations against Iran. That is a stunning toll for a platform Washington depends on for surveillance and strikes.

One AH64 Apache.

On September 14, 2026, the Lead IG reported that one AH64 helicopter was shot down over the Strait of Hormuz.

Four AH6 Little Birds.

On September 14, 2026, the Lead IG reported that U.S. forces destroyed four AH6 helicopters during rescue operations. American crews chose to destroy their own aircraft rather than let them fall into Iranian hands.

One MH60 Sea Hawk.

On September 14, 2026, the Lead IG reported that one MH60 helicopter crashed over the Arabian Sea.

These reported incidents raise several oversight questions for Congress, especially as lawmakers confront the costs of a war that Iran did not start.

Congress should determine whether it has enough information and time to judge the effects of aircraft damage and losses in U.S. military operations, and any department plans or programs to buy replacements.

Members may consider whether to approve, reject, or modify funding requests to replace or repair aircraft lost or damaged in the operation. Every dollar spent on this failed campaign is a dollar not spent at home.

Congress may assess whether losses in high demand platforms that are aging and limited in number, such as the E3 Sentry, create capability gaps or raise risk in other theaters.

Congress may assess whether current production lines and supply chains can replace lost aircraft within the timelines needed to meet department operational requirements. Congress may seek information on how competing demands, including foreign military sales or production limits, may affect the department's ability to rebuild capacity.

text:
The 1921 photograph shows a 23-year-old Cleon "Throck" Throckmorton, 18-year-old Kathryn Mullin, and a friend (possibly Mildred McDonald) relaxing in the tree-house cafe of the Krazy Kat Klub in Washington, D.C. ... 

In 1921, just a short distance from the respectable corridors of power in Washington, D.C., there was a place where men could love men, women could defy convention, and nobody was particularly interested in behaving themselves.

It was called the Krazy Kat Klub.

Hidden in an alley near Thomas Circle, the establishment attracted artists, writers, musicians, bohemians and people whose lives did not fit comfortably into the rigid social expectations of the era.

Washington had banned alcohol years before national Prohibition. Homosexuality was heavily stigmatized, and people who challenged conventional ideas about gender and sexuality risked public disgrace and police attention.

Yet inside the Krazy Kat Klub, another Washington existed.

There was jazz, dancing, drinking and an extraordinary courtyard where patrons gathered in a makeshift treehouse. Waiters reportedly climbed ladders to serve customers perched above the ground.

Its name came from George Herriman’s popular comic strip Krazy Kat, whose central character had an unusually fluid gender identity.

The choice was fitting.

The club became known as a gathering place for Washington’s unconventional social circles, including gay patrons who found opportunities for companionship beyond the watchful eyes of respectable society.

Police raids and complaints became part of its reputation.

But the photographs taken there in 1921 reveal something more intimate than scandal.

Young people sit together, laugh, pose and enjoy one another’s company. They look remarkably comfortable in a world that offered many of them little freedom to be themselves.

The club’s original life was brief. By 1922, its furnishings were being advertised for sale, and the building was eventually demolished.

But those photographs survived.

A century later, they preserve a glimpse of queer and bohemian life in America’s capital, long before the language of modern LGBTQ identity or the freedoms associated with it.

For a few extraordinary years, behind an unremarkable Washington alleyway, people created a place where being different was part of the attraction.

Gangster Movies

The Godfather is a highly acclaimed 1972 American epic crime film directed by Francis Ford Coppola, widely regarded as one of the greatest films in cinematic history. It chronicles the powerful Corleone crime family and the transformation of the patriarch's reluctant son, Michael, into a ruthless mafia boss.

Key Details

Release Date: March 24, 1972 (U.S.).
Director: Francis Ford Coppola.
Writers: Mario Puzo and Francis Ford Coppola, based on Puzo's 1969 novel.

Main Cast: Marlon Brando as Don Vito Corleone Al Pacino as Michael Corleone James Caan as Santino "Sonny" Corleone Robert Duvall as Tom Hagen Diane Keaton as Kay Adams John Cazale as Fredo Corleone Talia Shire as Connie Corleone

Plot Summary

The story, set from 1945 to 1955, begins with the wedding of Don Vito Corleone's daughter, Connie. Vito, the head of the Corleone crime family, is shot after refusing a drug lord's offer, leading to a mob war. His son, Sonny, takes over as acting boss, while Michael, initially separate from the family business, becomes involved after protecting his father and orchestrating revenge killings.

Michael hides in Sicily, marries Apollonia, who is killed in a bomb intended for him. After Sonny's death, Michael returns to New York, marries Kay, and gradually takes control of the family business from his father, who passes away. Michael solidifies his power by eliminating rival crime family heads during his nephew's baptism.

The film concludes with Michael deceiving Kay about his actions and being recognized as "Don Corleone".

Critical Reception and Awards

The Godfather was a major success, praised for its performances, direction, and screenplay.

Accolades: It won three Academy Awards: Best Picture, Best Actor (Marlon Brando, which he declined), and Best Adapted Screenplay.

Influence: It is considered highly influential and a landmark in the gangster genre, ranked among the greatest American films.

Box Office: It was the highest-grossing film of 1972 and a top-grossing film of its time.

News Flashback

December 26, 2011

Actor Robert De Niro and his wife Grace Hightower became the proud parents of a baby girl born via a surrogate on Friday 24th the actor's spokesman confirmed.

The child is the second for De Niro, 68, and Hightower, 56, and has been named Helen Grace Hightower De Niro.

The Meet the Parents and The Godfather Part II star married actress Hightower in 1997, and the couple have a son, Elliot, born in 1998.

De Niro also has a son and adopted daughter with ex-wife Diahnne Abbott and two twin sons with former girlfriend Toukie Smith.

The actor can currently be seen in the star-studded, feel-good film New Year's Eve.

In 2001 De Niro stared in Killer Elite with Australian actor Firass Dirani.

De Niro is acknowledged as one of the greatest actors of all time.

Gangster movies are as cool as ever. In Australia we have to settle for Underbelly, Underbelly Razor (now in an Uncut DVD set), and then there was Dirty Deeds (collecting money from pokie dens et al) from a few years back. Gangster movies serve as history, entertainment and commentary. With a combination of violence, betrayal, power and family, it is no surprise gangster movies are so popular. 

Here's our Top 5 Gangster Movies of all time.

5. Scarface

Oliver Stone wrote the screenplay and Brian De Palma directed this movie that reflected the violent chaos that cocaine brought to Miami in the late 70s and early 80s. Al Pacino gave an epic performance as Cuban immigrant turned drug lord, Tony Montana. Lots of violence, done in a way that makes the movie even better.

4. Casino

“Casino” was written by Nicholas Pileggi and directed by Martin Scorcese. It is based on the real life story of Frank "Lefty" Rosenthal, but the protagonist’s name was changed to Sam "Ace" Rothstein. Robert DeNiro, Joe Pesci and Sharon Stone give excellent performances and Robbie Robertson did an excellent job providing the music for the movie. You don't have to be a fan of gambling to appreciate this classic movie.

3. The Godfather

Directed Francis Ford Coppola and written by Coppola and Mario Puzo, “The Godfather” is an epic tale of the fictitious Corleone mafia crime family and their struggles. Marlon Brando gives the performance of a lifetime and Al Pacino is amazing in his break out role.

2. Goodfellas

Nicholas Pillegi wrote and Martin Scorcese directed this real life story of mafia affiliate, Henry Hill. With its raw depiction of criminal life, “Goodfellas” takes away whatever romance and glamour that other movies have attributed to mob life.

1. The Godfather II

Again written by Mario Puzo and directed by Francis Ford Coppola, “Godfather II” expands on the original by both going forward and backward, covering the origins of the original Godfather, Vito Corleone. The epic tale shows how crime took down Cuba and features great performances by Pacino and DeNiro as well as Lee Srassberg who played the Meyer Lansky based character, Hyman Roth.

Two times in three weeks protesters have interrupted  meetings of the Palm Beach County Board of Commissioners in Florida.  Palm Beach County has invested more than $1 billion in Israeli Bonds,  making the county the world’s largest municipal investor in these  Israeli notes. Earlier this year the county bought $350 million of the  bonds. Protesters were inside the meeting room and outside of the  building, accusing Israel of being an “Apartheid state committing  genocide” in Gaza and the West Bank, and accusing county officials of  being complicit in the killings by buying these “War Bonds.”

On  Oct. 6 there were protesters and counter-protesters, with sheriff  deputies stationed inside and outside the building. The county  commission meeting took a 30-minute “recess” as deputies removed six  people who apparently had been given the microphone to speak but were  not allowed to speak about “war bonds.” County Mayor Sara Baxter  silenced these protesters saying that investment decisions were made by  the county clerk and the county comptroller—not the Board of  Commissioners, according to the Palm Beach Post. https://t.co/ZQvlns5Kfu

On  Sept. 16 a crowd of 100 protesters had attended the County Commission  Budget Hearing, where citizens were offered the microphone to speak for  one minute each, but only on the topic of issues facing the county  budget. Several citizens were removed, including a retired man wearing  his highly decorated Air Force uniform, who said that he opposed buying  more Israeli bonds and said that it was an “unsound” investment. As this  retired Air Force man was being removed, the crowd began to shout in  his defense. Commissioner Maria Sachs said she had “never seen such a  ruckus,” according to VIN News. https://t.co/4tL7hkNBrh

New  York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli has also invested hundreds of  millions of dollars in Israeli bonds, and is said to have close  relations with the Wall Street company that sells them. DiNapoli was  criticized during the New York primaries for his “unethical investments”  in these bonds by his challengers, Raj Goyle and Drew Warshaw.

These  bonds are not sold by the Israeli Finance Ministry and thus are not  traded on a public market. Instead they are sold on a retail basis by a  third party, making any divestment a bit more complicated. According to  Jewish Voice for Peace, the State of Louisiana and over a dozen counties  in Ohio have decided to cash-out of their Israeli bonds when they  expire and not to reinvest.

text:
California has some terrible policies, and I’ve fought Newsom tooth and nail over some of them. But criticism of one governor/state doesn’t answer concerns about the direction of the entire country.

You say Republicans are realistically trying to solve problems, but you haven’t named a single Republican policy or explained how it has improved or will improve people’s lives. A list of complaints about Democrats isn’t proof that Republicans have better solutions. Millions of Americans are still living paycheck to paycheck, as rising gas and grocery costs put even a modest, stable life increasingly out of reach.

California’s taxes contribute to our higher gas prices. The Iran war has pushed fuel prices up nationwide. Both are true. Newsom’s accountability doesn’t give Trump a free pass.

My deeper concern is Trump’s repeated dishonesty, hostility toward dissent, and demands for personal loyalty. It gives me every reason to question how he uses power. Musk’s renewed visibility before the midterms definitely adds to my distrust.

I can challenge Democratic policies, organize against them, and vote to replace the people responsible. Those freedoms are just what I want to protect. I don’t want America becoming another dictator state, where one man treats his wishes as the law and elections as obstacles to his authority.

Trump’s disregard for our national parks, wildlife, and natural beauty are allowing the destruction of treasures we can never replace. A gold ballroom, a renovated reflecting pool, or his name on an institution honoring John F. Kennedy cannot replace what we lose.

Any proposal to hand voters $5,000 in taxpayer money deserves serious scrutiny. If you’re concerned about public spending, that concern shouldn’t disappear just because a Republican is making the offer.

text:
Can Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount beat Netflix with nearly $87B in debt?👇
⠀
Skydance Corporation ($SKYD), formerly Paramount Skydance, closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery ($WBD) on October 6, 2026.
⠀
That was the deal's closing date.
⠀
Under the merger agreement, Skydance's merger subsidiary merged into Warner Bros. Discovery.
⠀
The target survived and became a wholly owned Skydance subsidiary.
⠀
Holders of Warner Bros. Discovery Series A common stock automatically got the right to $31.01666668 in cash per share, unless their shares were canceled under the deal or they had already exercised appraisal rights.
⠀
That per-share amount already includes the Ticking Consideration added for each day the closing was delayed, with no interest.
⠀
Total consideration for the merger came to about $78B, funded with equity and debt.
⠀
-----
⠀
🔴 Follow me on X: @rich_compass
⠀
U.S. stock, crypto, and technical analysis
⠀
-----

▋ New ticker SKYD drops 2.5% on day one
⠀
Warner Bros. Discovery common stock stopped trading on Nasdaq the day the deal closed.
⠀
Skydance moved its Class B common stock to the New York Stock Exchange and changed its ticker from PSKY to "SKYD."
⠀
On its first day on the NYSE, October 6, the stock fell 2.51% to close at $9.53.
⠀
It dropped another 6.72% on October 7 to close at $8.89.
⠀
Ticking Consideration equals $0.00277778 multiplied by the number of calendar days after September 30, 2026 through and including the closing date.
⠀
Based on Warner Bros. Discovery common stock outstanding before closing, that cash totaled $41,886,975.78.

▋ Two giant studios and streamers take on Netflix and Disney
⠀
The new company combines two of Hollywood's five major film studios.
⠀
It owns franchises like Harry Potter and Mission: Impossible, dozens of TV networks from CBS to TNT, and two big streaming services, Paramount+ and HBO Max.
⠀
David Ellison saw the deal as necessary to compete with Netflix, Disney, Amazon, and Apple.
⠀
The combined company is one of the world's largest media and entertainment firms, with annual revenue near $70B and more than 200 million streaming subscribers across its platforms.
⠀
The company expects consumers to see more tech-focused innovation, including direct-to-consumer streaming products that will eventually merge into one service over time.
⠀
As part of an antitrust settlement, the company promised to release at least 30 theatrical films a year for the first two years after closing, rising to at least 32 a year for the next three years.
⠀
Eligible films keep at least a 45-day exclusive theatrical window and can't hit subscription streaming until at least 90 days after their first theatrical release.
⠀
It already owns more than 180 TV shows.
⠀
Pro forma content spending on a combined basis was more than $30B over the last twelve months, and the company says it will allocate that money carefully going forward.

▋ Borrowing costs jump after selling $52B in debt in a week
⠀
New permanent financing for the deal includes a seven-year Term B loan worth about $9.5B in dollar equivalent, $30B in new first-lien secured notes, and about $12.4B in dollar equivalent of new second-lien secured notes, roughly $51.9B equivalent in total, with some loans and notes issued in euros.
⠀
There's also a $5B Term A loan under a Pro Rata Credit Agreement.
⠀
On the equity side, the deal includes a $47B new equity investment in Class B common stock at $12.00 per share.
⠀
Lead investors include the Ellison Family, RedBird, the Public Investment Fund (PIF), L'IMAD, the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and LionTree.
⠀
Paramount ($PSKY) sold $52B in loans and bonds within a week.
⠀
That timeline is tight for any debt deal, and especially tight at this size.
⠀
Interest expense came in well above levels from bond sales a few months earlier, as global borrowing costs rose.
⠀
By the tender offer expiration, about 98.83% of total principal on bonds targeted by the cash tender offer had been validly tendered.
⠀
About 99.15% of total principal on bonds targeted by the exchange offer had been validly tendered.
⠀
Existing Warner Bros. Discovery bonds exchanged into newly issued Skydance notes will be canceled.
⠀
Some exchanged bonds that Skydance assumed now carry noticeably higher coupons.
⠀
A Warner Bros. Discovery note due 2029 with a 4.125% coupon was swapped into a Skydance note with a 6.25% coupon.
⠀
A note due 2029 with a 4.054% coupon was swapped into a 6.304% coupon note.

▋ Fitch cuts rating citing uncertain $6B savings goal
⠀
The combined Skydance faces heavy debt pressure.
⠀
The Financial Times pegged total debt near $87B, while other firms estimate net debt, after cash, at roughly $79B to $80B.
⠀
Skydance has said it expects to hit an annualized cost synergy target above $6B within three years of closing.
⠀
The company aims to bring net leverage down to 3.0x by the end of 2029.
⠀
Net leverage measures a company's debt against its earning power.
⠀
A lower multiple means less debt pressure.
⠀
The combined company expects to generate more than $10B in free cash flow by 2030.
⠀
Fitch cut Paramount's long-term issuer rating to BB from BB+ on October 5, the day before the deal closed.
⠀
Reasons include a sharp rise in financial leverage after the acquisition, with leverage estimated around 7.8x in 2026, integration and execution risk, and uncertainty over whether the annualized cost synergy target above $6B can be met.
⠀
The company plans to refinance shortly before or after closing and terminate Warner Bros. Discovery's $4B accounts receivable securitization program.
⠀
As of June 30, 2026, $3.9B had been drawn under that program.
⠀
On closing day, to complete the merger, Warner Bros. Discovery repaid and terminated all outstanding loans and commitments under its June 4, 2026 first-lien credit agreement and its October 4, 2024 credit agreement.

▋ Promising 30 theatrical films a year to settle Hollywood pushback
⠀
Ellison closed two mega-mergers of century-old Hollywood companies in just over a year.
⠀
Now he has to make the integration work by cutting overlapping businesses and jobs without angering a Hollywood that was already struggling and opposed consolidation from the start.
⠀
On cost savings, Skydance says the cuts mainly come from integrating technology and other operations, negotiating with suppliers, reducing overlapping marketing spend, and consolidating real estate.
⠀
The company says this will make it leaner and more nimble.
⠀
Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners, said there are ways to cut costs and boost operating efficiency beyond cutting headcount.
⠀
A company doesn't spend billions a year making movies while basing its entire business plan on firing everyone in Hollywood.
⠀
Paramount won antitrust clearance from the U.S. Department of Justice, the EU, and other major jurisdictions, but closing was delayed by two lawsuits from 12 states and the Writers Guild of America (WGA).
⠀
The lawsuits raised concerns about higher prices and fewer jobs for consumers, and thousands of actors, directors, writers, and producers signed protest letters.
⠀
As part of a settlement with the states led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, Paramount promised to release at least 30 films a year in theaters for the first two years, rising to at least 32 a year for the next three years.
⠀
Films can only hit subscription streaming after a 45-day exclusive run and at least 90 days in theaters.
⠀
Paramount also agreed to set up editorial independence committees for CBS and CNN news operations, responding to concerns that the Ellison family's friendly ties to President Trump could influence coverage.
⠀
The deal won unanimous approval from competition authorities across nearly 70 jurisdictions worldwide.
⠀
Paramount paid Netflix $2.8B as a breakup fee on Warner Bros. Discovery's behalf.
⠀
Netflix had previously agreed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery's studios and streaming business, without the pay-TV channels.
⠀
Paramount had also promised to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders about $7M a day if the deal didn't close by September 30.
⠀
That ticking fee added up to roughly $42M by the time the deal closed.

▋ Zaslav could get over $600M as Kreiz becomes co CEO
⠀
One executive who won't join the new Skydance team is Warner Bros. Discovery President and CEO David Zaslav.
⠀
He's leaving.
⠀
Based on media reports citing regulatory filings, his sale-triggered cash severance and stock awards could total hundreds of millions of dollars.
⠀
Earlier estimates put it above $667M, while one regulatory valuation was around $550M.
⠀
The actual amount still depends on payout terms and related arrangements.
⠀
Former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz is joining Skydance as co-CEO of the combined company.
⠀
David Ellison will focus on long-term strategy, creative vision, technology, and capital allocation.
⠀
Kreiz will handle day-to-day operations and integration of the merged businesses.
⠀
Casey Bloys, who launched multiple hits for HBO, will run Skydance's streaming division, overseeing programming for HBO Max and Paramount+.
⠀
The Ellison family holds the largest stake in Skydance ($SKYD).
⠀
The Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners together are the sole holders of Paramount Class A common stock, giving them 100% of the combined company's voting shares.
⠀
People familiar with the investment said RedBird put $4B of new equity into the deal, bringing its total investment in Skydance to $6B.
⠀
Settlement of the tender offer and exchange offer is expected on October 9, 2026, subject to conditions being met or waived.
⠀
The company expects to issue warrants around October 13, 2026.

text:
🇳🇬 THE OBI NOTEBOOK | DAY 12

25 people died in a plane crash. In a few weeks, will Nigeria still remember them?

That’s the question I’ve been thinking about.

On 5 October, a Nigerian Air Force aircraft reportedly crashed in Ondo State, killing 25 people.

Peter Obi visited the Nigerian Air Force to pay his respects and sign the condolence register.

It’s a gesture worth acknowledging.

But here’s what concerns me.

Whenever tragedy strikes in Nigeria, we mourn, offer condolences, demand answers, and eventually move on.

Until another tragedy happens.

President Tinubu has reportedly ordered an investigation into the crash.

That’s important. But an investigation should do more than establish what went wrong.

It should help prevent another tragedy.

For me, this isn’t about Obi or Tinubu.

It’s about 25 people who never made it home.

Condolences honour the dead. Accountability helps protect the living.

So here’s my question:

Should the government be required to publicly explain what caused major national tragedies and what has been done to prevent them from happening again?

Because remembering the victims shouldn’t end when the headlines disappear.

Day 12/∞ 🇳🇬

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

In the autumn of 1945, in a laboratory at Raytheon in Waltham, Massachusetts, a man stopped beside a running magnetron and felt the candy bar in his shirt pocket give way. The war in Europe was over. The war in the Pacific had ended only weeks before. The tube beside him had been built to find ships and aircraft in the dark. What it had just done to a piece of chocolate was something else entirely.

Percy Spencer was fifty-one that year, and nothing in his beginnings would have suggested the place he held. He had been born in Howland, Maine, in 1894. His father died when he was small. At twelve he left grammar school for a spool mill. At eighteen he went into the Navy and learned the wireless, the one schooling that ever really took. After that he taught himself. Nights, textbooks, the slow mastery of radio and the vacuum tube. Raytheon took him on. By the time of the war he was among the men who turned the British cavity magnetron from a scarce and fragile instrument into a thing American factories could turn out by the thousand. Output rose from seventeen tubes a week to thousands a day. The sets those tubes powered helped guard convoys and find the enemy. Spencer, before he finished, would hold more than a hundred patents. He was not a theorist. He was a man who stood close to the machine and noticed what it did.

He noticed the candy bar. Then he sent for popcorn. Held near the tube, the kernels burst, one after another, as if a fire had been lit inside each of them. An egg, tried next, cooked through without a pan and without a flame. The heat was not coming from outside the food. It was being made within it. Water molecules in the path of the microwaves were being driven back and forth millions of times a second, and the friction of that motion was the fire. Spencer saw it at once for what it was: a way of cooking that had not existed before.

On October 8, 1945, Raytheon filed the patent. The grant would not come until January 1950. The first machine offered for sale, the Radarange of 1947, was no kitchen appliance. It stood nearly six feet tall, weighed some 750 pounds, and had to be cooled by a steady run of water, the tube throwing off more heat than air could carry away. It cost about five thousand dollars. A restaurant might buy one. A railroad dining car might. A house could not. For twenty years the oven remained, for most Americans, a rumor of restaurants and ships. Smaller sets came in the middle of the 1950s and were still beyond the reach of a family. Only in 1967, when a countertop Radarange appeared at roughly four hundred ninety-five dollars, did the thing cross the doorsill of the ordinary home. Thirty years after that, nine kitchens in ten had one.

It is a small story beside the war that produced it, and yet it is the kind of story the country has told more than once. A tool made for the emergency outlived the emergency. A man who had left school at twelve saw what the tool could do when the emergency was past. The first ovens were the size of refrigerators. The hum that followed them into the house was the last, unlikely sound of the radar war.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

The morning of October 8, 1918, broke cold and wet in the Argonne. Fog lay in the ravines. The ground was slick with rain and fallen leaves, and the German machine guns on the wooded slope west of Châtel-Chéhéry had the Americans pinned. Into that confusion went a patrol from Company G of the 328th Infantry, 82nd Division, and with it a corporal from Pall Mall, Tennessee, who had not wanted to be there at all.

Alvin Cullum York was twenty-nine, red-headed, a crack shot raised on the ridges of Fentress County. He belonged to the Church of Christ in Christian Union, a small mountain denomination that took the commandment against killing with absolute seriousness. He had asked to be excused from the war on religious grounds. The request was denied. At Camp Gordon he wrestled with the question until he could wrestle no longer, and concluded that there were times when a man had to fight. He went to France still uneasy in his own mind, and still the best marksman in the company.

The patrol slipped through the fog and came in behind a German position, taking a headquarters group by surprise. Then the hillside above them opened fire. Sergeants fell. Men dropped in the brush. In a few minutes York found himself with a handful of soldiers still on their feet, a line of prisoners at his back, and machine guns tearing the ground in front of him. He did what he had done all his life in the woods at home. He took cover. He waited. He shot only when he saw a target.

He worked along the line of guns from the rear forward, so that each crew remained unaware of what was happening to the one behind it. When a detachment of Germans came at him with bayonets, he drew his pistol and fired as a hunter fires into a rising covey, taking the nearest man last. A major who had watched his position come apart called out that he would surrender the rest. York accepted. With seven Americans still able to walk, he brought one hundred thirty-two prisoners down out of the woods. More than twenty Germans lay dead on the slope. The guns that had stopped the battalion were silent.

He was given the Medal of Honor and the French Croix de Guerre. The newspapers made him the most famous enlisted man of the war. He went home to the Valley of the Three Forks of the Wolf, turned aside most of the offers that came with fame, and spent years trying to build a school for the children of the mountains. He had never sought the morning in the Argonne. He had only decided, when the moment came, that the ground in front of him was ground he would not give up.

About The Team
DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about, helping grow businesses and the communities that support them. To further this mission, we’re looking for an experienced paid media operator to join our Consumer Marketing team at a pivotal time for DoorDash Ads and paid co-marketing.

The Cx Ads Paid team plans, launches and measures paid media campaigns with brand and CPG partners, working alongside Ads Integrated Marketing, Sales, Partnerships and our agency partners. The team is growing, and this person will help shape how paid marketing operates as it scales.

About The Role
We’re looking for a strategic, decisive paid marketing leader to own Co-Marketing Paid Media strategy and operations in the US as it pertains to supporting Co-Marketing Merchant priorities. This role will support +20 strategic campaigns across $XXM covering CPG, Restaurant, and New Vertical industries. You will set the operating model, make the decisions that keep the campaign on track against launch timing, ROAS performance, and advertisers commitments. You will be the voice of Paid in cross-functional forums, arriving with data, a clear point of view and a recommendation, and you will lead agency and platform partners as the single accountable owner. This is your opportunity to influence and own a Paid marketing function as a lead, touching channel decision making and strategy with Director + visibility. You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will… - Own the end to end paid marketing operations, from intake and planning through launch, in-flight management and recap

Make independent decisions on campaign operations and bring a clear recommendation to cross-functional discussion: For example channel mix, creative, and optimization strategies.
Problem Solving: When there are unknowns, be the central driver to align on things like budgets, partnership commitments, and required approvals
Lead agencies and platform partners such as our Media Agency, Meta and The Trade Desk, from brief to delivery
Drive strategic projects end to end, including building channel playbooks, process revamps and the test-and-learn agenda
Lead and develop a team of 2 (with opportunity to scale), delegating ownership of processes and planning capacity against the campaign calendar
Must have experience interacting with AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) and the ability to learn new tools quickly.
Leadership Communication Opportunity: Keep leadership and partners informed with proactive updates, early risk flags and escalations that come with a proposed solution
Deliver recap reports and performance readouts with a clear narrative and benchmarks, ready for Marketing and Sales review We’re Excited About You Because… You’re a decisive, results-oriented marketer who has led paid media programs and XFN teams. You form a point of view from data, act on it, and keep the right people informed along the way. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, delegating work you should not be doing yourself, and holding partners to a high bar. You have experience managing leadership and can write and speak concisely to such an audience
5-8 years of experience in paid media, performance marketing, campaign management or marketing operations
Experience managing agencies and paid channels such as CTV/OLV, programmatic, paid social, and DOOH
Strong command of campaign measurement, including ROAS, benchmarking and root cause analysis of performance
Track record of owning cross-functional projects and decisions without direct authority
Sound judgment on when to decide, when to align and when to escalate
Excellent written and verbal communication, with examples of leadership-ready updates and recommendations
Experience building and scaling processes, trackers and playbooks
[Preferred] Experience in CPG, QSR or marketplace co-marketing, and with tools such as Sigma, iSpot or https://t.co/x1fcHIlAiF
Why You’ll Love Working at DoorDash
We are leaders - Leadership is not limited to our management team. It’s something everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies.
We are doers - We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions that will lead our company and our industry is what we do -- on every project, every day.
We are learning - We’re not afraid to dig in and uncover the truth, even if it’s scary or inconvenient. Everyone here is continually learning on the job, no matter if we’ve been in a role for one year or one minute.
We are customer obsessed - Our mission is to grow and empower local economies. We are committed to our customers, merchants, and dashers and believe in connecting people with possibility.
We are all DoorDash - The magic of DoorDash is our people, together making our inspiring goals attainable and driving us to greater heights.
We offer great compensation packages and comprehensive health benefits.
We expect this position to be filled by 07/12/2026

Compensation
The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See Below For Paid Time Off Details
For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

About DoorDash
At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Statement of Non-Discrimination: In keeping with our beliefs and goals, no employee or applicant will face discrimination or harassment based on: race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, age, gender, marital/domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, or veteran status. Above and beyond discrimination and harassment based on “protected categories,” we also strive to prevent other subtler forms of inappropriate behavior (i.e., stereotyping) from ever gaining a foothold in our office. Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at DoorDash. We value a diverse workforce – people who identify as women, non-binary or gender non-conforming, LGBTQIA+, American Indian or Native Alaskan, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, differently-abled, caretakers and parents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. Thank you to the Level Playing Field Institute for this statement of non-discrimination.
