Beyond Los Angeles traffic, the high desert opens into a Benedictine invitation: stop moving, keep the hours, listen, and remain.

Saint Andrew's Abbey stands in Valyermo, United States. A Benedictine abbey in the high desert offering simple private retreats with meals and opportunities to join the monks in daily prayer. Saint Andrew’s Abbey carries a lineage from European Benedictine communities into a California monastery founded at Valyermo in 1955, where guests can still build a simple retreat around prayer with the monks.

This destination does not need an invented anniversary to become meaningful. Its place in the Catholic story comes from the worship, memory, art, witness, or pilgrimage already documented there. That matters editorially: a compelling sacred-place story should never require a made-up feast or a vague claim that “the Church celebrates” something on a date the Church has not actually assigned. Catholic Tourist treats the living site itself as the subject and lets the verified record determine when a calendar connection is appropriate.

The human story here is carried by a community rather than by a single canonized figure. That is worth noticing. Catholic history is not only a sequence of famous names; it is also the accumulated fidelity of worshipers, religious communities, craftspeople, families, catechists, clergy, and pilgrims whose prayer gave a sacred place its continuity. Reading the site this way keeps the story from turning into celebrity history and returns attention to the Church as a people gathered across generations.

This is an active monastery and retreat house rather than an apparition, tomb, or miracle site; its significance comes from living Benedictine prayer, hospitality, work, and sacred reading. This is the discipline behind the story. Church recognition, ecclesiastical custody, public devotion, local tradition, archaeology, and tourism promotion answer different questions. Naming the category honestly does not drain wonder from a place; it allows devotion and history to stand without asking either one to pretend to be something else.

Saint Andrew's offers straightforward Benedictine retreat hospitality in the high desert, with meals and the opportunity to join the monks' daily prayer. The destination guide identifies Pray with the monks: Build a simple private retreat around the abbey's current daily prayer schedule. and Ask about weekends: Weekday availability is broader; weekend rooms are more limited.. These are not boxes to check at speed. They form a sequence for reading the site: first identify the devotional or historical center, then notice the surrounding evidence, and finally make room for worship or quiet reflection. A photograph can preserve the appearance of a moment, but a pilgrimage needs enough time for the meaning of the place to become coherent.

There is also a healthy difference between curiosity and credulity. Saint Andrew's Abbey can be approached with real openness without exaggerating what the sources establish. Catholic faith does not depend on turning every tradition into a scientific finding or every testimony into a universal decree. Careful language protects the people who live with the devotion, the pilgrims who are trying to understand it, and the credibility of the Church’s witness. The truest version of a story is usually more interesting than the viral version because it contains real people, real limits, and a place that can still be visited.

Practical preparation protects that deeper visit. Weekdays are generally available and weekends more limited. Contact the retreat office before making travel plans. Desert terrain and the lodging buildings vary. Describe mobility and room needs in the reservation request. 31001 North Valyermo Road, Valyermo, California 93563. Confirm arrival directions because the abbey is outside the main Los Angeles transit network. Effective January 1, 2026, requested donations are $105 single or $90 per person double, including meals. Official information should always outrank a cached itinerary, especially during feast days, restoration work, seasonal closures, or major pilgrimages. Travelers should also remember that access to a church building does not guarantee access to every chapel, relic, museum room, or devotional area described in its history.

The most useful question after learning this history is not “Did I know this already?” but “What does this place ask me to remember?” Saint Andrew's Abbey may preserve courage, conversion, sorrow, gratitude, missionary patience, artistic labor, or confidence in intercession. Memory becomes Christian when it leads beyond admiration toward communion: prayer for the living, gratitude for those who came before, repentance for failures, and renewed attention to Christ. A map can locate the destination; only that response turns discovery into pilgrimage.

The source trail is deliberately visible. This editorial package was reviewed on 2026-09-14, with https://t.co/P2IlJl4COZ as its controlling source. That record is not there to lend borrowed authority to an embellished tale; it lets an editor return to the institution, church, diocese, shrine, public heritage body, or other responsible custodian behind the catalog entry. If the official source later changes a schedule or clarifies a claim, the destination and its future stories should change with it. Source verification is a continuing obligation, not a one-time badge.

Pilgrimage begins before the journey when attention changes. A traveler can arrive at Saint Andrew's Abbey merely asking what there is to photograph, or arrive asking what generations of Christians learned to pray here. The second question slows everything down. Architecture becomes more than backdrop; an image becomes more than an object; a tomb becomes more than a historical marker. The place starts to disclose the practices that sustained it—Mass, intercession, penance, thanksgiving, care for the poor, endurance under pressure, or confidence in God. That attentive posture is part of the pilgrimage, even for someone encountering the destination first through a screen.

Ask for the humility to receive silence not as emptiness but as room in which the Word of God can finally be heard. Whether the journey happens soon or remains a hope for later, let the story lead beyond novelty. Read further, pray for the people who keep this place, and approach its history with both confidence and humility. Catholic Tourist exists to help people find the sacred wherever they go; the final purpose is not another saved location, but a deeper encounter with Christ and His Church.

text:
Drarthrozun, The Scourge of Slaughter

Drarthrozun serves Erythnul, the god of Hate, Envy, Malice, Panic, Ugliness, and Slaughter.

.To Erythnul, the only thing better than constant slaughter, is defacing beauty. He revels in it. But unfortunately, none of his souls are good looking- they are either bashed enough by themselves, or he bashed them an eternity ago. 

And for once, in millennia, Erythnul sat down and felt incredibly depressed, a notion that one of his petitioners noticed as he approached with genuine concern, only to be bashed against the wall by Erythnul and turned into a bloody pulp… but the depression wasn’t gone.

It would be many years later that news came to him that a demon in the Abyss had attained a high kill count. That didn’t surprise him, but then, the demon who gave him the news smirked.

“He scarred Adonides. His beautiful face forever marred. Goes by the name of Drarthrozun”

Erythnul felt his heart pumping again. He knew that little weasel Adonides: a minor duke of Hell with too big of an ego and who surrounds himself with temptresses like Empussa, who had spurned his own advances before. This was good. This was very good.

With but a thought, Erythnul appeared in the midst of the Blood War and cut, bashed and bit off every demon and devil that got in the way until he found Drarthrozun, in the middle of breaking a devil in half over his knee.

“You’re coming with me. You’ll be my face above and…”

He bashed a demon’s face in and continued.

“…. You’ll get to slaughter a lot more things than devils down here. Accept my offer and you will not regret it.”

Drarthrozun smiled and both deity & demon fist pumped and disappeared in black fire.

text:
US backs $1.5B conditional loan for chips used in drones, radar, missile defense | Neetika Walter, Interesting Engineering

The US Department of War has offered semiconductor manufacturer Wolfspeed up to $1.5 billion in conditional financing to expand domestic production of advanced chips used in drones, radar, electronic warfare, and missile defense systems.

The proposed 30-year loan, announced through the department’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), would support the development and manufacturing of silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor technologies. These materials are used in high-performance power systems and radio-frequency electronics.

The North Carolina-based company plans to use the financing to upgrade its GaN manufacturing capabilities for next-generation communications and electronic warfare systems. The company also aims to develop radiation-resistant versions of its existing SiC products and future GaN devices for demanding defense and aerospace applications.

Radiation hardening helps protect electronic components from damage or malfunction caused by radiation, making it particularly important for satellites, spacecraft and military systems operating in harsh environments.

Advanced chips strengthen defense

Unlike conventional silicon semiconductors, SiC and GaN are wide-bandgap materials that can operate under demanding electrical conditions. They are particularly useful in systems requiring high power, efficient energy conversion and high-frequency performance.

Silicon carbide can handle high voltages and temperatures while reducing energy losses, making it useful in power electronics. Gallium nitride, on the other hand, is suited to high-frequency applications, including communications equipment, radar and electronic warfare systems.

According to the Department of War, the proposed financing would strengthen domestic access to semiconductor materials used in propulsion systems, directed-energy weapons, drones, radar and missile defense.

The company also plans to advance GaN-on-SiC wafer technology, which combines gallium nitride‘s high-frequency performance with silicon carbide’s ability to dissipate heat. This makes the technology useful for powerful radar, communications and electronic warfare systems.

“SiC and GaN have critical national security applications,” said Robert Feurle, Wolfspeed’s CEO. “With this financing, the company would be well positioned to not only continue to serve the DoW but also expand its capabilities for the benefit of U.S. national security as a whole.”

Financing remains conditional

The proposed financing would support a multiyear manufacturing and technology development program across Wolfspeed’s domestic operations. The company has facilities in North Carolina, New York, and Arkansas.

The agreement also includes a potential equity component. Wolfspeed would issue warrants allowing the Department of War to purchase up to 7.5 percent of the company’s fully diluted equity, with the warrants issued proportionally as loan installments are funded.

The financing is structured as a senior secured loan facility, allowing Wolfspeed to draw funds in stages rather than receive the entire amount upfront.

The proposed investment aligns with the Trump administration’s efforts to expand domestic semiconductor manufacturing and reduce reliance on overseas supply chains for strategically important technologies.

However, Wolfspeed said the transaction remains subject to substantial due diligence, government authorizations, final agreements, and other closing conditions. The company cautioned that there is no guarantee the loan will be finalized or that any funding will ultimately be provided.

text:
$WOLF: A leading North American player in silicon carbide (SiC) wafers and power devices. It filed for pre-packaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 2025, emerged on September 29 of that year, and saw the case involving its Texas subsidiary conclude in September 2026. On October 7, it received a conditional commitment from the U.S. Department of Defense’s Office of Strategic Capital for a secured, draw-down loan of up to $1.5 billion with a 30-year term, intended for domestic SiC/wide-bandgap device production and GaN upgrades. Funds have not yet been disbursed; the deal requires due diligence, a final agreement, and regulatory approval. In exchange, the DoD may receive warrants representing up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity, issued in tranches.

Macro Context
Electric vehicles, data center power supplies, and defense applications all demand higher-efficiency power semiconductors; SiC offers superior high-voltage tolerance and lower energy loss compared to silicon. The U.S. aims to keep the wide-bandgap supply chain domestic, and policy funding is willing to give a "second chance" to companies that have faced setbacks but retain production capacity. As AI server rack power consumption rises, power components have shifted from supporting roles to becoming a bottleneck—a rare demand tailwind for WOLF.

September 2025: Restructuring took effect; old debt was drastically reduced, and equity was reset. Impact: The company survived, but the narrative for legacy shareholders was fundamentally altered.
August 19, 2026: FY2026 Q4 revenue was approximately $150 million, aligning with the midpoint of guidance; GAAP gross margin was -25%, and adjusted EBITDA was roughly -$62 million; cash and short-term investments totaled $1.1 billion as of June 28. AI data center revenue doubled year-over-year and grew approximately 20% quarter-over-quarter. Impact: Demand showed bright spots, though profitability had not yet recovered.
October 7, 2026: Received the DoD's conditional commitment for a loan of up to $1.5 billion (30-year term); the stock surged in after-hours trading. The biggest potential impact: If finalized, it effectively provides a floor for production capacity and defense orders using ultra-long-term, low-cost capital; if it falls through, the initial price gap-up will likely be erased. Terms include a four-tranche drawdown structure (initial tranche ~$600 million) with a 36-month window, contingent on securing at least $750 million in other qualifying capital.

Asset Overview
Operations span from materials (SiC substrates and epitaxy) to devices (MOSFETs and diodes). The 5th-gen SiC MOSFET has launched; a 10kV product won a 2026 industry innovation award, and a memorandum of understanding (MOU) exists with GE Aerospace. Production is anchored in North Carolina, New York, and Arkansas, with plans to keep low/high-voltage GaN, GaN-on-SiC RF epitaxy, and radiation-hardened capabilities within the U.S. Key applications include EV inverters, industrial power supplies, AI data centers, telecommunications, aerospace, and electronic warfare.

Vertical integration—from substrates to devices—combined with domestic U.S. 200mm SiC capacity creates a competitive moat that few rivals can replicate in the short term. Defense and radiation-hardened capabilities serve as added differentiators, allowing the company to avoid relying solely on price wars in the automotive sector. Weaknesses are equally clear: yield issues, factory ramp-up struggles, and negative gross margins previously drove the company to bankruptcy; meanwhile, STMicroelectronics, Infineon, and ONsemi are all actively pursuing SiC.

Bull Case: The market currently prices the stock as a "restructured shell with negative margins." If the $1.5 billion commitment converts into a drawable facility, the cost of capital and downside risk profile will be fundamentally rewritten. As AI power supply and defense orders grow as a share of revenue, the valuation anchor can shift from "post-bankruptcy recovery play" to "strategic asset." The upside story isn't about an immediate earnings explosion, but rather the simultaneous improvement of financing conditions and demand structure.

Target Price: $36–$40

text:
True or false?: Market conditions almost always trump individual talent.

Was listening to Scott Galloway tell a story on his Prof G Podcast the other day. 

His first company was called Prophet... a global brand and marketing consultancy.

It was the late 1990's tech bubble, and he was inexperienced enough to think things could keep going up forever. He had a chance to sell the company for a 10x multiple. Didn't do it.

Then 2000 came around. The market tanked. He ended up selling a few years later than he should have for about a 2.5 multiple.

The most interesting part? Galloway said that by all accounts his company was a MUCH better business when he sold it than it was during the bubble.

Better talent. Better systems. Better customer relationships and recurring revenue.

No matter. The market always wins.

In our business if you bought in 2021, you were most likely cooked. Doesn't matter how well you ran your deal.

And on the flip side... if you sold into a 3 cap market in 2021? It probably doesn't matter if you're a horrible operator who mismanaged your deal.

Now, this is not all "luck." Knowing when to buy and when to sell is a skill. "The market just screwed me" is an excuse making loser attitude. You have agency.

Does that mean you're going to be perfect? Nope. But never use the market as an excuse.

The best time to sell is when everything is going amazing. And it will be the very moment where it feels like you should keep riding the wave.

Galloway offers the following advice, whether it's selling a building or a business:

1. Make sure to drum up multiple bidders.
2. Be prepared to walk away from the negotiation. He mentioned his bigger exit (his company L2) sold for a huge price because at one point, he told the buyer he was walking... which of course caused the buyer to scramble and get him his number.
3. Sell into a good market. Easier said than done.

Anything else you would add?

text:
The Collapse of the $73 Billion CDC Partnership

The most damaging setback occurred in October 2026, when CDC Data Centres abruptly terminated their joint venture with Firmus. The ambitious deal, known as Project Southgate, was designed to build a network of massive AI data centres across Australia, effectively doubling the nation's total capacity. The partnership collapsed with only 2.5% of the planned project capacity completed (a single 42-megawatt site in Melbourne), forcing Firmus to pivot its growth strategy toward Asian markets like Malaysia and Indonesia.

2. Sceptical Investors and the IPO Price Slash

Just weeks away from its targeted public listing, the company's valuation has faced a harsh reality check. Originally seeking a blockbuster $43.9 billion valuation at $11 a share, institutional brokers were forced to reprice and slash the offer price due to weak demand from both international and local investors. Major domestic pension funds, including UniSuper, publicly snubbed the roadshow, citing that "too little was known about its underlying business".

3. Severe Customer Concentration Risks

Leaked investor pitch decks revealed that 80% to 90% of Firmus's projected revenue pipeline relies entirely on just two anchor contracts: chipmaker Nvidia and an unnamed American tech giant (subsequently revealed to be Meta). Analysts have raised alarm over this extreme customer concentration, noting that any reduction in demand from these two entities exposes the company to extreme financial vulnerability.

4. Regulatory, Grid, and Environmental Backlash

Firmus's aggressive plans to build "AI factories" in Tasmania have triggered significant friction:
• Illegal Development Accusations: Local councils launched investigations after Firmus allegedly commenced unauthorized site clearing and construction work in Wesley Vale without valid planning permits.
• Grid and Water Strain: Energy experts and state politicians have challenged Firmus's claims, arguing that their massive energy requirements (>400MW) risk triggering power shortages and price spikes. The company also faced severe public backlash following a leaked plan to divert state-owned agricultural irrigation water to cool its servers.
• Generator Restrictions: The George Town Council placed tight restrictions on the operation of Firmus’s 276 backup diesel generators, restricting them to emergency use only—a decision Firmus is actively appealing in court.

5. Administrative and Legal Distractions

The company's operational credibility has also been tested by minor financial embarrassments and internal legal disputes. Media reports surfaced that Firmus missed its very first rental payment to landlord CDC Data Centres, requiring senior management intervention before the bill was sheepishly paid. Furthermore, co-founder Oliver Curtis—whose past insider-trading conviction already attracts heavy media scrutiny—has been drawn into messy court litigation involving a $140 million ownership dispute over 1.1 million Firmus shares between former private credit financiers.

text:
The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information leading to the identification or location of Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in the United States in connection with the 2021 Microsoft Exchange Server attacks known as HAFNIUM.

The reward is for information leading to his identification or location, the news outlet NTD reported this week, citing a notice from the department's Rewards for Justice program.

Zhang remains at large, U.S. authorities say, meaning he has not been arrested. The charges against him have not been tested in court.

Rewards for Justice is the State Department's national security rewards program. It says it has paid more than $250 million to over 125 people since 1984.

Zhang is wanted for his alleged role in "malicious cyber activities against U.S. critical infrastructure," NTD quoted the notice as saying.

The amount and that wording match an offer the program was already making in January 2025. That offer was for information on anyone who hacks U.S. critical infrastructure at the direction of a foreign government.

Zhang and a second man, Xu Zewei, are charged together in federal court in Houston. The indictment, the document that sets out the charges, has nine counts.

text:
🚨💰 500,000 FOLLOWERS. MILLIONS OF VIEWS. THOUSANDS OF LIKES. AND STILL STRUGGLING TO PAY THE RENT.

Now imagine someone with just 5,000 followers.

Nobody recognizes them in public.

Their videos rarely go viral.

Their posts might receive only 30 likes.

But every month...

💳 Customers are buying.

🤝 Clients are renewing.

🏦 Bills are getting paid.

👨👩👧👦 Their family is being supported.

📈 Their business is growing.

NOW TELL ME SOMETHING… WHO IS ACTUALLY MORE SUCCESSFUL?

Because I believe social media has convinced an entire generation to chase something that looks like success instead of building something that creates it.

And the difference could be costing people YEARS of their lives.

❤️ LIKE if you believe financial freedom matters more than internet fame.

💬 COMMENT A or B before reading further.

🔁 REPOST this because someone with 500 followers needs to hear it today.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 IMAGINE YOU WAKE UP TOMORROW AND SOMEONE OFFERS YOU TWO SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS.

You can own either one.

No payment required.

No hidden conditions.

But there's one rule.

YOU CAN ONLY CHOOSE ONE.

📱 ACCOUNT A — THE INTERNET SUPERSTAR

👥 500,000 followers

👀 Millions of monthly views

❤️ Thousands of likes

💬 Hundreds of comments

🔥 Videos constantly going viral

🌍 People recognize your face

Your notifications never stop.

Brands occasionally contact you.

Strangers call you an inspiration.

Your friends think you've made it.

But there's something nobody sees.

Your rent is overdue.

Your income is unpredictable.

You spend hours creating content without knowing whether it will generate a single sale.

Your followers love watching you.

But very few are willing to buy from you.

Every month feels like starting from zero.

Now meet the other account.

💰 ACCOUNT B — THE QUIET ENTREPRENEUR

👥 5,000 followers

👀 A few thousand views

❤️ 20–50 likes per post

💬 A handful of comments

📱 Almost nobody knows your name

But behind the scenes…

💳 Customers are purchasing.

🤝 Businesses are signing contracts.

🔁 Existing clients are returning.

📧 New inquiries are arriving.

⭐ Satisfied customers are recommending you.

🏦 Your business is profitable.

❤️ Your family has greater financial security.

You don't have the fame.

You don't have the applause.

But you have something powerful.

A BUSINESS THAT DOESN'T NEED TO GO VIRAL TO SURVIVE.

👇 WHICH ACCOUNT WOULD YOU CHOOSE?

A — Fame and followers?

B — Customers and financial stability?

And more importantly, WHY?

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💔 HERE'S THE PART THAT SHOULD MAKE EVERY CONTENT CREATOR THINK.

Imagine working for three years.

Three years of filming.

Three years of editing.

Three years of posting.

Three years of chasing algorithms.

Three years of checking notifications.

Three years of comparing yourself with other creators.

And slowly, your numbers grow.

1,000 followers.

10,000 followers.

50,000 followers.

100,000 followers.

500,000 followers.

People celebrate your achievements.

Your videos go viral.

Your account looks incredible.

Then one evening…

You open your banking app.

And realize something terrifying.

YOU'VE SPENT THREE YEARS BUILDING AN AUDIENCE, BUT YOU HAVEN'T BUILT A RELIABLE BUSINESS.

You know how to get attention.

You know how to entertain strangers.

You know how to make people press LIKE.

But you still don't know how to turn that attention into sustainable income.

That's the trap.

And it catches more people than we realize.

🚨 BEING POPULAR IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING PROFITABLE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

☕ LET ME SHOW YOU SOMETHING WITH TWO COFFEE SHOPS.

Two entrepreneurs open coffee shops on the same street.

The first becomes a TikTok sensation.

Millions of views.

Thousands of comments.

People taking photographs outside.

Influencers mentioning the business.

But inside?

Too few paying customers.

The owner is struggling to cover rent, salaries, and expenses.

Now imagine the second coffee shop.

Only 800 Instagram followers.

No viral videos.

No celebrity endorsements.

But customers love the coffee.

They return every morning.

They bring their friends.

They recommend the shop.

They spend money.

And the owner finishes each month with a healthy profit.

WHICH COFFEE SHOP WOULD YOU RATHER OWN?

The one everyone talks about?

Or the one customers consistently support?

Because the lesson is simple.

👀 Views create awareness.

❤️ Likes show engagement.

💬 Comments create conversations.

🤝 Trust builds relationships.

💳 Customers generate revenue.

🏦 Profit keeps a business financially sustainable.

And these are NOT the same thing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 NOW IMAGINE TWO CONTENT CREATORS.

Meet James.

James has 480,000 followers.

He posts about AI, entrepreneurship, and online income.

His videos regularly attract hundreds of thousands of views.

His audience constantly tells him:

"YOU SHOULD SELL A COURSE!"

"I WOULD DEFINITELY BUY!"

"TAKE MY MONEY!"

So James creates a course for $199.

He does the mathematics.

If just 1% of his 480,000 followers buy, that's 4,800 customers.

4,800 × $199 = $955,200.

Nearly a million dollars in potential revenue.

He's excited.

He launches.

His promotional video receives 200,000 views.

Thousands of likes.

Hundreds of comments.

But sales?

Far below his expectations.

Why?

Because someone commenting "AMAZING CONTENT" isn't necessarily someone ready to spend $199.

APPLAUSE DOESN'T AUTOMATICALLY BECOME INCOME.

Now meet Emma.

She has 3,800 followers.

She helps small businesses improve their marketing.

Her content rarely gets more than 1,000 views.

But her audience includes business owners who genuinely need her expertise.

One afternoon, she publishes a simple post explaining how local businesses can attract more customers.

Only 600 people see it.

One business owner sends her a message.

They arrange a call.

She explains how she can help.

The owner signs a $2,000 monthly agreement.

One post.

One qualified inquiry.

One customer.

$2,000 in recurring monthly revenue, provided the contract continues.

Now imagine Emma eventually builds relationships with eight clients paying the same amount.

That's $16,000 in monthly revenue before expenses and taxes.

These are hypothetical examples, not promises of earnings.

But they illustrate something important.

YOU DON'T ALWAYS NEED MORE PEOPLE WATCHING. SOMETIMES YOU NEED TO REACH THE RIGHT PEOPLE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 AND NOW I WANT TO ASK YOU A QUESTION THAT MIGHT MAKE YOU UNCOMFORTABLE.

Are you genuinely trying to build a business?

Or are you chasing followers because getting likes feels easier than asking someone to buy?

Think about it.

How many times have you said:

"I'll start when I reach 10,000 followers."

"I need a better website."

"My logo isn't professional enough."

"I need better equipment."

"I need to learn another skill."

"I'll launch next month."

And then next month arrives.

Nothing changes.

Another month passes.

Still nothing.

Meanwhile…

Someone with 200 followers sends their first business proposal.

Someone with an ordinary phone makes their first sale.

Someone with a basic landing page gets their first customer.

Someone with no audience contacts a local business and secures a contract.

Not because they're necessarily smarter.

Not because they're more talented.

But because they were willing to take action.

PERFECTION CAN BECOME THE MOST EXPENSIVE EXCUSE IN BUSINESS.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

❤️ IF YOU HAVE ONLY 100, 500, OR 1,000 FOLLOWERS, THIS PART IS FOR YOU.

Please stop thinking your audience is worthless.

Imagine standing on a stage.

In front of you are 500 people.

Five hundred real human beings.

People with families.

People with ambitions.

People with businesses.

People with problems they desperately want solved.

Now imagine just ten of those people genuinely need what you offer.

And three become paying customers.

Would you still call that audience insignificant?

Your next customer might already be following you.

Your next business opportunity might already be watching.

Your next referral might come from someone who has never liked a single post.

YOU MAY BE SO BUSY LOOKING FOR YOUR NEXT 10,000 FOLLOWERS THAT YOU'RE IGNORING THE PEOPLE ALREADY LISTENING.

Read that again.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💰 WHAT IF YOU CHANGED YOUR GOAL FOR THE NEXT 30 DAYS?

Forget chasing 100,000 followers for a moment.

What if your goal became:

🎯 Find your first paying customer.

🤝 Build five genuine business relationships.

📧 Generate ten qualified inquiries.

💳 Make your first profitable sale.

⭐ Deliver a service so valuable that a customer recommends you.

🔁 Turn a one-time buyer into a repeat customer.

Imagine how differently you would approach social media.

Instead of asking:

"HOW CAN I GO VIRAL?"

You'd ask:

"HOW CAN I SOLVE A REAL PROBLEM?"

Instead of:

"HOW CAN I GET MORE LIKES?"

You'd ask:

"HOW CAN I EARN MORE TRUST?"

Instead of:

"HOW CAN I ATTRACT EVERYONE?"

You'd ask:

"WHO ACTUALLY NEEDS MY SERVICE?"

That's when social media can become more than entertainment.

It can become a tool for building a business.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💔 SOMEONE READING THIS RIGHT NOW IS THINKING ABOUT GIVING UP.

Maybe they've been posting for six months.

Maybe two years.

Maybe they've watched people with less experience grow ten times faster.

Maybe they feel embarrassed by their follower count.

Maybe they're afraid to tell friends they're trying to build a business.

Because everyone seems to measure success by numbers.

But here's what I want that person to understand.

YOUR FOLLOWER COUNT IS NOT YOUR WORTH.

Your value isn't determined by an algorithm.

Your ability to help someone isn't determined by how many likes you receive.

Your business potential isn't automatically limited by your audience size.

You can have a valuable skill before you have an audience.

You can solve a real problem before you become famous.

You can earn your first customer before you reach your first thousand followers.

And you can build a sustainable business without ever becoming an internet celebrity.

It takes work.

It takes trust.

It takes persistence.

And sometimes it takes many attempts before something works.

But please don't confuse slow audience growth with personal failure.

YOU DON'T NEED TO IMPRESS THE ENTIRE INTERNET TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE IN SOMEONE'S LIFE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 LET'S TRY SOMETHING DIFFERENT IN THE COMMENTS TODAY.

Instead of only celebrating followers, let's celebrate progress.

Have you ever:

💳 Made your first online sale?

🤝 Signed your first client?

📧 Received your first serious business inquiry?

⭐ Gotten a referral from a happy customer?

💰 Earned money with fewer than 1,000 followers?

If you have, SHARE YOUR STORY BELOW.

Tell us how many followers you had and what you did.

Not to boast.

But because somewhere in this comment section, a beginner might discover that their dream is possible.

And if you haven't made your first sale yet, that's okay.

Comment:

🚀 "WORKING ON MY FIRST CUSTOMER."

Maybe someone reading your comment has advice.

Maybe someone can introduce you to an opportunity.

Maybe you'll connect with another entrepreneur.

Let's make this comment section more useful than another argument about algorithms.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨 HERE'S MY CHALLENGE TO YOU.

Within the next 24 hours, do ONE thing that could help your business grow.

Not something that makes your profile look impressive.

Something that creates a real opportunity.

📧 Email a potential client.

☎️ Make that business call.

🌐 Publish your landing page.

💬 Ask your audience what problems they face.

💰 Create a simple offer.

🤝 Follow up with an interested customer.

📝 Send the proposal you've been delaying.

📱 Contact five businesses that might need your service.

Then return here and comment:

ACTION TAKEN ✅

Tell us what you did.

Because sometimes the most important business milestone isn't your next thousand followers.

It's your next meaningful action.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

❤️ AND THIS IS WHY I WANT YOU TO SHARE THIS POST.

Somewhere, there's a talented freelancer who thinks 300 followers isn't enough.

A small-business owner who believes they need to go viral to succeed.

A creator who has spent another night comparing themselves to someone with a million followers.

An entrepreneur who keeps delaying their launch.

Someone who has a valuable service but lacks the confidence to offer it.

That person might be your friend.

Your colleague.

Your family member.

Or someone following you right now.

🔁 REPOST THIS FOR THEM.

📤 Tag someone building a business.

❤️ Like it if you've ever felt discouraged by your follower count.

Because the message isn't that followers don't matter.

They do.

A large, engaged audience can create enormous opportunities.

But FOLLOWERS ARE A RESOURCE, NOT THE FINAL MEASURE OF SUCCESS.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 NOW LET ME LEAVE YOU WITH ONE FINAL THOUGHT.

Imagine it's five years from today.

Two people sit down to reflect on their journey.

The first says:

"I reached 500,000 followers. Millions of people watched me. My videos went viral."

The second says:

"I helped hundreds of customers. I built lasting relationships. My business supports my family. I have more control over my time."

Both achievements can be meaningful.

But if you had to choose only one…

WHICH FUTURE WOULD YOU WANT?

Because here's something worth remembering:

A million people can know your name without ever becoming your customers.

And a small number of loyal customers can help you build something extraordinary.

One customer can become a repeat buyer.

One repeat buyer can become a referral.

One referral can become a long-term business relationship.

One successful project can open doors you never expected.

That's how many sustainable businesses grow.

Not through one magical viral moment.

But through trust, value, relationships, and consistent delivery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚨💰 NOW IT'S YOUR TURN. LET'S SETTLE THIS DEBATE.

A 📱 — 500,000 FOLLOWERS, MILLIONS OF VIEWS, BUT STRUGGLING FINANCIALLY.

B 💳 — 5,000 FOLLOWERS, LOYAL CUSTOMERS, AND A PROFITABLE BUSINESS.

👇 COMMENT A OR B — AND TELL ME WHY.

And I have three more questions:

💬 How many followers do you currently have?

💰 Have you ever earned money from an audience of fewer than 5,000 people?

🔥 What's harder for you right now: gaining followers or finding paying customers?

I especially want to hear from people who built successful businesses with small audiences.

Your experience could inspire someone to stop waiting and start building.

❤️ LIKE if this gave you a different perspective.

🔁 SHARE AND REPOST so more entrepreneurs see it.

📤 TAG someone who needs encouragement.

🔖 SAVE this for the next time you start comparing your numbers with someone else's.

🚀 FOLLOW for more conversations about entrepreneurship, digital marketing, AI, online business, and creating real value.

BECAUSE 500,000 FOLLOWERS MIGHT MAKE YOU LOOK SUCCESSFUL…

BUT 5,000 OF THE RIGHT FOLLOWERS COULD HELP YOU BUILD A BUSINESS THAT ACTUALLY CHANGES YOUR LIFE.

And sometimes…

THE MOST IMPORTANT PERSON IN YOUR AUDIENCE ISN'T YOUR 500,000TH FOLLOWER.

text:
Discipline is not the morning stack.
Breathing. Journal. Reading. Training. Sleep. Food. A hobby that isn’t the tape.
That’s just the shopping list.
Without discipline it’s a mood board you abandon on Wednesday.

None of that runs itself.
Not the drill when you wake up.
Not the gym when the body votes no.
Not the closed laptop when a candle is still talking.
Not walking past the cheap hit — sugar, timeline, “one more look.”
The habits are the costume.
The thing underneath is the ability to sit inside a rule when nobody is watching.

We live in a machine that sells unlimited choice and then bills you in attention.
A rectangle in your pocket shakes all day.
Cheap offers. Empty messages. Fake optionality. Video slop.
All of it has one job:
pull you off the few things that actually move the account and the life.

Freedom is not “do whatever.”
Freedom is the chance to build a cage that keeps you usable.
No limits and the modern world is just a more comfortable way to get hollow.
People call that living.
It’s usually just consumption with better lighting.

If you can’t govern appetite — even for an hour —
the stack of “opportunities” turns into dependency, noise, and a head that can’t hold a plan.
So you put rails on food and sleep.
You swap a dumb loop for a useful one.
You end up under cold water at a stupid hour
not because it is holy.
Because the alternative is bargaining with yourself all morning.

In the minute it feels worse.
Of course it does.
The old loop is designed to feel like relief.
The sugar hit is cheaper than the week of feeling better without it.
That math is boring.
It also compounds.
Limit now, collect later.
Or collect now and pay interest in focus.

Markets run on the same law.
Unlimited hours. Unlimited tickers. Unlimited ways to feel involved.
You don’t know what you’ll make.
You don’t know what you’ll give back.
The game does not clock out.

So you invent rules and wrap them in a system.
Not to become a monk.
To stop mistaking motion for work.
The tape, the feed, the new model, the live PnL —
all of it wants the same resource as the cheap video:
your attention.
Discipline is how you refuse the bid.

If the day has no rails, the session won’t either.
You don’t rise to your analysis.
You fall to whatever you refuse to restrict.

text:
I’ve been contemplating how much wealth has been lost, slipped through the hands of time. How many living souls discovered wisdom that could enrich our minds and soothe our souls, only for their words to become buried and forgotten?

So, a few times a week, I’ll be performing a little exhumation and resurrection, bringing forgotten words of wisdom and truth back into the light in a series I’m calling The Lost Library - for your pleasure and awakening…..

Today we remember Irish mystic George William Russell (1867–1935), known as Æ, was also a painter, as well as a poet, philosopher and social reformer.

One summer evening, listening to birdsong, he suddenly experienced the trees, grass, atmosphere and his own being as belonging to a single living companionship.

The boundaries between himself and nature seemed to soften.

He later wrote:

“A little breaking of the barriers and being would mingle with being.”

Russell believed that nature could reveal herself more deeply through love and contemplation.

Perhaps this is something we have forgotten.

We spend so much of our lives interpreting the world through thought that we rarely consider how our bodily felt experience and emotions offer another way of knowing ourselves and the world. Silent, yet full of life, rich with meaning in ways that words cannot always capture.

Russel’s work asks us to explore the relationship between consciousness, love and the living world.

He reminds us that understanding nature may involve more than discovering the principles by which it operates.

It may also involve learning how to experience it.

Source verification

The quotation is reproduced exactly from the original English text of The Candle of Vision, published by Macmillan in London in 1918. No translation is involved. The passage appears in the chapter “Earth,” beginning on page 170.

text:
How to get people to want your product without chasing them:

1- Stop talking about your product all the time.

People don't wake up thinking about you. 

They wake up thinking about themselves and their problems.

Talk about these things before you talk about your product.

2- Make people feel understood.

People buy from those who they feel understand them.

Use the exact words they use in their own minds back to them.

People don't think in terms like "MY LTV to CAC is so low" they think "WHY TF AREN'T MY ADS CONVERTING!!".

Talk to them like they talk to themselves. Use their own vocabulary and words back to them.

3- Paint a vision of a brighter future.

People take action when they perceive a clear gap in their lives, and are offered a bridge to cross that gap.

Show them what life could look like if they take action. 

And here's an important part, the brighter future looks different for every person. 

One founder I spoke to told me he has money, but wanted to build his brand so he gets invited to private rooms. Another told me he wants girls in his DMs (I'm not joking), while another wanted to raise a huge round in 12 months. 

Every reason is valid, you want to position your product specifically for every dream outcome people have.

4- Show great proof of success.

When people are presented with the bridge, their first instinct will be "Will it work for me". 

You overcome this by building belief through undeniable proof. 

Walls of testimonials, happy customers, screenshots of success. 

The closer the testimonials look to them (Literally look physically like them, but also have a similar situation) the more belief they'll build. 

5- Only then, extend your hand and invite them to take action via a call to action.

text:
Central Asia’s Middle Corridor at Risk: Don’t Let the West Hijack Central Asia’s Sovereignty

Beware Western Strings: Central Asia Must Guard Its Corridors from Political Agendas & Subversion.

Kazakhstan’s President Tokayev has floated the idea of integrating the Middle Corridor with the EU-backed Three Seas Initiative. On paper, this sounds like a grand vision: linking Central Asia’s transport arteries with Eastern Europe’s infrastructure grid. But before Central Asian leaders rush to embrace Brussels and Washington, caution is warranted. The track record of Western involvement in infrastructure across the Global South is not one of competence, but of politics, conditionality, and unfinished projects.

The Mirage of Western Infrastructure Competence
The EU and US are not known for delivering hard infrastructure in developing countries. Their strength lies in “soft projects”—consultancies, governance reforms, digital platforms—not in railways, ports, or highways. Compare this with China’s Belt and Road Initiative, which has already built functioning rail links from Chongqing to Duisburg, ports in Gwadar and Piraeus, and highways across Africa. Western projects, by contrast, often stall in feasibility studies, endless regulatory reviews, or political debates back home. Central Asia cannot afford to bet its future on promises that rarely materialize.

Political Strings Attached
Western financing never comes free of political strings. The EU and US routinely attach conditions on governance, transparency, or human rights. These may sound noble, but in practice they function as levers of influence. Infrastructure becomes a Trojan horse for reshaping domestic politics. Governments that resist find themselves undermined by media campaigns, NGO pressure, or outright funding freezes. For Central Asia, this means sovereignty is compromised. Instead of building railways, Western involvement risks importing political instability.

Undermining Elected Governments
Another pattern is bypassing local governments altogether. Western donors often funnel money through NGOs or international agencies, sidelining elected authorities. This weakens legitimacy at home and creates dependency on external actors. Worse, Western media narratives frequently portray local governments as corrupt or incompetent, eroding public trust. The result is not stronger institutions, but fractured sovereignty. Central Asia’s leaders should ask: do we want infrastructure that strengthens our states, or projects that hollow them out?

The Geopolitical Agenda
Let’s not pretend the Three Seas Initiative is a neutral connectivity project. It is a geopolitical instrument backed by Washington to counter both Russia and China. Integrating the Middle Corridor into this framework risks entangling Central Asia in Western strategic designs. Instead of multipolar connectivity, the region could become a pawn in a new Cold War alignment. For Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan, this is a dangerous gamble. Infrastructure should serve national development, not geopolitical containment.

Lessons from Africa and Eastern Europe
Africa offers a cautionary tale. Western-led projects there often collapse under the weight of conditionality and lack of financing. Meanwhile, Chinese-built railways and ports, though imperfect, actually exist and function. Eastern Europe too has seen Western promises of infrastructure fade into bureaucratic inertia. The Three Seas Initiative itself remains more of a political slogan than a network of completed projects. Central Asia should not be seduced by glossy brochures and summits that deliver little on the ground.

The Alternative: Multipolar Connectivity
Central Asia sits at the heart of Eurasia. Its future lies in leveraging geography to become a hub of multipolar connectivity. This means balancing corridors: the Middle Corridor through the Caspian, the Northern Sea Route via Russia, and the Belt and Road railways through Xinjiang. It means co-financing with China’s AIIB, Russia’s EAEU, and regional development banks. It means pragmatic partnerships with Turkey, Iran, and ASEAN. In short, it means building infrastructure that serves Central Asia’s interests, not Washington’s agenda.

A Call for Caution
Tokayev’s proposal deserves serious debate, but Central Asia must approach EU and US involvement with eyes wide open. The West’s poor track record in delivering hard infrastructure, its tendency to politicize projects, and its habit of undermining local governments all point to risk. Integration with the Three Seas Initiative could easily become another case of Western overpromising and underdelivering—while entangling the region in geopolitical games it did not choose.

Conclusion
Central Asia’s leaders should welcome diversified connectivity, but they must guard against becoming laboratories for Western political engineering. Infrastructure is not just about steel and concrete; it is about sovereignty, stability, and development. The EU and US have shown time and again that their involvement comes with baggage. If the Middle Corridor is to fulfill its promise, it must be built on pragmatic, multipolar partnerships—not on Western agendas that leave half-finished projects and fractured governments in their wake.

text:
I’ve been filling gyms with Facebook ads for over a decade.

And most owners still struggle to make them work.

They blame “lead quality.” They blame the “economy”. They blame everything EXCEPT their own lack of skill. 

If you fall into that trap, let me wake you up.

Here are 9 lessons that built multiple 6 - 7 figure gyms:

1️⃣ Whoever Can Afford the Most to Acquire the Client, Wins.

This is the Dan Kennedy principle I based my advertising on from day one.

Most gym owners are desperate for cheap leads. Whereas the gyms winning now are happy to pay $20. 

Why?

Because when you have the right unit economics, you can absorb higher acquisition costs and still make a profit.

Raise your value. Raise your pricing. Have systems for upselling, retaining and referrals within 30 days. 

Then you can spend more to get a customer and lead costs don’t bother you.

2️⃣ Hooks Are Your Weapons.

“Looking for 10 women in [YOUR AREA] ready to drop 10lbs in 6 weeks - without strict diets and NO boring cardio - or you don’t pay”

Cliché? Yes.
Effective? Always.

You don’t win with originality. You win with clarity.

Irresistible offer formula:

Specific person. 
Specific result. 
Specific timeline. 
Overcome skepticism. 
Limited availability.
Risk-reversal.

3️⃣ Stop Targeting “Everyone.”

Everyone = No One.

Split. Test. Ruthlessly.
Men only. Women only.
Then by age group.
Then by market awareness level.

We find most success in the 40 - 50 years, solution-aware market range.

They’ve got money, pain, and urgency.
And they buy fast.

4️⃣ Urgency Is Oxygen.

If your ad doesn’t have a countdown, it’s getting half the leads it should.

You must give people a reason to act NOW.

“This Monday” is my favorite. Timeless, evergreen, and brutal.

No dates. No editing.
People move when they feel the clock ticking.

5️⃣ Local Landmark Ads.

We have a Reticular Activating System in the brain. It’s subconsciously wired to spot things that are relevant to us.

This is why local landmark videos or photos work so well, 

When your prospect is scrolling and sees their local high street, they are far more likely to stop and see what it’s about. 

This gets attention (rule #1 of advertising) 

But it also builds trust. People trust what is local to them (irrational but true regardless).

6️⃣ Be Ready to Break Even

You think “break even” is losing.
That’s why you quit ads way too soon.

But I have a different mindset: 

If I spend $500 on ads this week and make only $500 back in sales, I’m fine with that.

Because not only did I get a new client who’ll be worth thousands to me in the long term… but I also just bought 50 more leads, many of which will convert in the weeks to come.

But the real point here…

Is that my ads will ALWAYS be on.

My gym ads will always be seen by my local market. 

I’ll outspend any other local gym.

And that’s why I’ll always win the market.

7️⃣ Know Your Numbers

You panic because you have no parameters.

No CAC.
No CPL threshold.
No clue what “good” even means.

That’s why you kill good ads too early and keep bad ones too long.

The amount of gym owners who stop their ads because of pansy emotions is insane.

But it allows me to dominate areas even easier so I’m all for it. 

8️⃣ Most Gyms Will Be Priced Out Soon.

You think it’s bad now? Wait 12 months.

Lead costs will double.
Competition will triple.
The weak will die off.

The survivors will be the ones who charge more, close better, and deliver world-class service.

If you can’t sell transformation, you’ll sell discounts until you close your doors.

9️⃣ Know the ROI Math.

Front-end offer: 3X ROAS in 7 days. 

5X ROAS in 30 days.

Lifetime value: 10 - 20X return within 9 months.

That’s the current KPI we aim for.

Bottom line:

You don’t have a “Facebook ads” problem.

It’s a strategy problem: you don’t know how much you should spend, nor what back end system must be in place to generate profit 

It’s a skill problem: you don’t know what ads to run, how to write the high filtering copy, market segmentation etc

And a mentality problem: you make decisions on emotions and guessing instead of following data.

That’s why our gym owners keep growing week after week after week after week… whilst the competitors complain about “lead quality”.

I install systems for burned out studio owners to get predictable client growth and build a business that works without them.

DM me to review your operations and see what I’d fix first.

Proxy wars as a disposal system

Lebanon is an escalation ladder. Palestine remains an open conflict. 
Iran is the direct confrontation. Viewed against an approaching civilizational handoff, the pattern stops looking random. 
These theaters are not stray flashpoints.

This is controlled demolition applied to geopolitics. 
Cold War and late-industrial arsenals are being spent down in real time. 
At the same time the fighting locks up and burns through what is left of the old energy base. Infrastructure is not merely damaged. 
It is cleared so a decentralized, technology-led system can be stood up on the rubble.
The sovereign-debt endgame
The real lever is the financing, not the battlefield. 
Western governments, led by the United States and the euro area, are pushing public debt to extremes through military aid on a trillion-dollar scale, procurement surges, and emergency subsidies.
The arithmetic is already closed. Global debt sits well above 330 percent of world GDP. 
No plausible tax take or growth path retires that stock. 
The ledger has passed the point where repayment is a serious option.
Deliberate escalation
Once the books are destined to be written off, fiscal restraint loses its purpose. 
Debts are inflated on purpose, to the outer limit, so the purchasing power of legacy fiat is worn away. War has always been the cleanest public excuse for open-ended money creation and exploding outlays. 
The bill is not meant to be settled. The apparatus that holds these claims is scheduled to implode, under control, before the handover.
From collapse to abundance
Wartime escalation and the financial break — a bond-market crisis plus the end of the petrodollar — are the required low point, psychological as well as economic. 
When populations are exhausted by crisis and war, the old foundation can fail without a fight.
That is the moment a three-part alignment is meant to move: government, the military, and technology principals, including the Trump–Musk line.
Technological redemption. Physics held in US Navy patent work associated with Salvatore Pais, and wireless energy transmission described by Steven Kwast, would be offered as the exit from scarcity. 
An energy crunch, and resource fights such as those around the Strait of Hormuz, would be framed as obsolete once abundance is treated as an engineering outcome rather than a geological limit.
The currency reset. 
A failed debt system would be replaced by an architecture no longer anchored to sovereign deficits, but to computing capacity in new, large data centers and to tangible assets. 
A universal high income, as argued by Elon Musk, would be the social shock absorber, distributing machine-generated surplus to the population.
The war scenarios are the last act of a transition sketched over decades. 
Their job is to burn off the material and monetary residue of the old order. 
On this reading none of it is an accident. 
It is the forced passage into a decentralized, technology-emancipated next era.

text:
The Antisemitism Canard: Weaponized False Accusations of Religious Hate

October 6, 1913: New Accusations Against Juror Henslee and the Disputed Affidavit of Virgil Harris

The Atlanta Journal, Monday, October 6, 1913, page 1, column 7

Three Monroe Men Reportedly Accuse Henslee

On Monday, October 6, 1913, The Atlanta Journal reported that three men from Monroe, Georgia, had submitted depositions accusing A. H. Henslee of expressing prejudice against Leo M. Frank prior to his trial for the murder of thirteen-year-old Mary Phagan.

The newspaper identified the men as J. J. Nunnally, Virgil Harris, and Dr. W. L. Rickert. Nunnally and Harris were described as buggy dealers, while Rickert was a dentist. All three were associated with Monroe, the county seat of Walton County, Georgia. The online transcription incorrectly identifies the county as Walker.

The newspaper reported that Deputy Clerk John H. Jones had received the depositions. The accusations concerned statements Henslee supposedly made while traveling through Georgia as a salesman.

According to the Journal, the witnesses alleged that Henslee had expressed a strong belief in Frank's guilt and had spoken harshly about him prior to serving on the jury.

One particularly serious accusation was attributed to Nunnally, who claimed that Henslee had spoken of Frank receiving the death penalty. Another witness reportedly described a conversation lasting approximately twenty minutes during which Henslee discussed his reasons for believing Frank was guilty.

The accusations were important because Henslee had served on the twelve-man jury that convicted Frank on Monday, August 25, 1913. Frank's attorneys were attempting to show that Henslee had entered the trial with his mind already made up (The Atlanta Journal, 1).

The Sparta Witnesses Renew Their Accusations

The October 6 Journal also published an open letter from three Sparta, Georgia, residents who had previously accused Henslee of expressing prejudice.

The men were John M. Holmes, S. M. Johnson, and Shi Gray.

They claimed that Henslee had discussed the Frank case in Holmes's office prior to the trial and had expressed a firm belief in Frank's guilt. Their letter accused Henslee of attempting to discredit them after they signed affidavits describing the conversation.

The three men also claimed that Henslee had mentioned being drawn for jury service.

Henslee denied their account of the conversation's date. He acknowledged visiting Holmes's office but maintained that the discussion of Frank's guilt occurred on Tuesday, September 2, 1913, after the verdict.

The timing was central to the disagreement. A juror expressing an opinion after hearing the evidence and returning a verdict was in a different position from a prospective juror who had already decided the defendant was guilty.

The Sparta men insisted that their account was accurate. Henslee maintained that they had confused the dates.

October 7: Henslee Answers the Accusations

On Tuesday, October 7, the Journal published Henslee's written response, dated October 6.

Henslee acknowledged visiting Holmes's office on June 27 but denied discussing Frank during that visit. He maintained that the conversation described by the Sparta witnesses occurred on September 2.

Henslee also denied accusations attributed to Julius A. Lehman, who claimed to have heard him discuss Frank's guilt during a railroad journey in June.

Henslee challenged Lehman's dates and described different railroad routes he claimed to have traveled. He stated that his employer, the Franklin Buggy Company of Barnesville, Georgia, kept records that could confirm his whereabouts.

The dispute had become serious enough that Henslee said he had visited Lehman on Saturday, October 4, and warned him that he intended to seek an indictment for making false accusations against him (The Atlanta Journal, 2).

October 8: Virgil Harris Denies Making an Affidavit

The most important correction to the October 6 report appeared two days later.

On Wednesday, October 8, the Journal published a letter from Virgil V. Harris of Monroe, dated Tuesday, October 7.

Harris stated that the October 6 article had incorrectly named him as one of the men who furnished Frank's attorneys with an affidavit against Henslee.

He denied making any such affidavit.

Harris also said he had been out of Monroe at the time Henslee supposedly made the statements attributed to him.

According to Harris, he had already explained his absence to attorney Stiles Hopkins when Hopkins visited Monroe seeking affidavits.

Harris's letter directly contradicted the October 6 newspaper report.

The correction is important because Harris was originally presented as one of three men supporting the accusations against Henslee. His own statement removed him from that group and challenged the accuracy of the newspaper's reporting.

Harris did not claim to know whether Henslee had expressed prejudice elsewhere. He stated that he had no personal knowledge of the alleged remarks and had never signed an affidavit concerning them (The Atlanta Journal, 3).

The Defense Continues Its Efforts

While the accusations against Henslee were being published, Frank's attorneys, Luther Z. Rosser and Reuben R. Arnold, were preparing their amended motion for a new trial.

The defense raised 115 grounds for overturning the conviction, including complaints about evidence, courtroom proceedings, and alleged juror prejudice.

Henslee and fellow juror Marcus Johenning were both accused of expressing opinions about Frank's guilt prior to the trial.

Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey was preparing the State's response. The October 6 Journal reported that Dorsey intended to study the legal objections while his assistants gathered evidence to defend the jurors.

The newspaper expected the hearing to begin on Saturday, October 11, although Dorsey later requested more time.

October 6: Newt Lee Is Denied Compensation

The same issue of the Journal carried another report connected with the Mary Phagan case.

On page 9, column 1, the newspaper reported that the Fulton County Board of Commissioners had refused a request to compensate Newt Lee for the months he spent in jail while held as a witness.

Lee was the night watchman who discovered Mary Phagan's body in the basement of the National Pencil Company factory during the early hours of Sunday, April 27, 1913.

His attorneys, Graham & Chappell, had petitioned the county for payment covering his confinement.

The commissioners rejected the request after receiving legal advice that the county had no authority to compensate a witness held by order of the courts.

County Attorney Luther Rosser declined to give an opinion because he was representing Frank. General Clifford L. Anderson examined the legal question instead.

Although several commissioners expressed sympathy for Lee, the board voted against compensating him.

The decision left Lee without county payment for the months he had spent in custody while the prosecution and defense prepared for Frank's trial (The Atlanta Journal, 1).

October 31: Judge Roan Rejects the New-Trial Motion

The accusations against Henslee and Johenning continued through October.

Both jurors denied having entered the trial with fixed opinions about Frank's guilt. Dorsey gathered statements defending them and challenged the accounts offered by the defense.

On Friday, October 31, 1913, Judge Leonard S. Roan denied Frank's motion for a new trial.

Frank's attorneys appealed to the Georgia Supreme Court.

On Tuesday, February 17, 1914, the Supreme Court affirmed Roan's ruling by a vote of four to two.

The court reviewed the dispute concerning the jurors and held that Judge Roan had the authority to decide between conflicting affidavits. It found no abuse of discretion in his treatment of the accusations against Henslee and Johenning (Frank v. State, 4).

Conclusion

The October 6, 1913, Journal article records a new effort by Frank's attorneys to challenge juror A. H. Henslee.

The newspaper reported accusations from Monroe residents and published an open letter from the Sparta witnesses. Both groups were presented as supporting the claim that Henslee had expressed prejudice prior to serving on the jury.

Henslee disputed the accusations and challenged the dates of the alleged conversations.

The October 8 correction involving Virgil V. Harris is particularly important. Harris denied signing an affidavit, denied witnessing the alleged conversation, and stated that he had already informed attorney Stiles Hopkins of his absence from Monroe.

The correction reduced the number of Monroe witnesses whose accusations could be supported by the newspaper's original report. It also showed that the public record was changing as the accusations were investigated.

Judge Roan ultimately refused to overturn Frank's conviction, and the Georgia Supreme Court upheld his decision.

The October 6 article, read alongside the October 7 and October 8 reports, shows how accusations against a juror were published, disputed, and corrected during the weeks following Frank's conviction.

References

The Atlanta Journal. (Monday, October 6, 1913). "Monroe Citizens Make Depositions Attacking Juror." Page 1, column 7. Also includes "Newt Lee Gets No Coin for Time Spent in Jail," page 9, column 1. Reports the original accusations naming Nunnally, Harris, and Rickert and the Fulton County commissioners' refusal to compensate Newt Lee.https://t.co/aNJ0ldqSW5

The Atlanta Journal. (Tuesday, October 7, 1913). "Henslee Answers Perjury Charges of Frank Defense." Contains Henslee's reply to the Sparta witnesses and his denial of the railroad statements attributed to him by Julius A. Lehman.https://t.co/qbkBq1tkv4

The Atlanta Journal. (Wednesday, October 8, 1913). "Frank Hearing to Be Postponed Another Week." Page 2, column 4. Includes Virgil V. Harris's October 7 letter denying that he furnished an affidavit against Henslee and stating that he had no personal knowledge of the alleged remarks.https://t.co/eLazLYKnM7

Supreme Court of Georgia. (February 17, 1914). Frank v. State, 141 Ga. 243, 80 S.E. 1016. Decision affirming Judge Roan's denial of a new trial, including the court's consideration of the allegations against Henslee and Johenning.https://t.co/SxWL6prrMo

Judge Ellis Protests Reckless Auto Drivers

The Atlanta Journal

Monday, October 6, 1913

Page 1, Column 6

Writes Chief Beavers a Letter Telling of Alleged Violations of Law

Judge W. D. Ellis, of the superior court, has written Chief of Police J. L. Beavers a letter requesting the arrest of an automobile driver, and incidentally registering a general protest against the way in which autoists are "fudging on the automobile laws."

Judge Ellis declares in his letter that in regard to the law regulating the passing of trolley cars by automobiles that the automobile drivers are acting like baseball players who are preparing to steal the next base; that they crowd the street car as much as possible, preparatory to a quick plunge ahead.

Judge Ellis in his letter to Chief Beavers states that Monday morning as he and James Holliday, of the Constitution, were preparing to board a car on Peachtree street, that automobile No. 18,806, driven by a negro chauffeur, dashed rapidly by in violation of the city road law, and he only saved himself from injury by a quick jump.

The violation of the law was so patent, he states, that several people noticed it, and he gives the name of Mr. Holliday and the street car conductor as witnesses, and at the same time expresses his own willingness to appear against the chauffeur when he is arrested.

Monroe Citizens Make Depositions Attacking Juror

The Atlanta Journal
Monday, October 6, 1913
Page 1, Column 7

Three Declare That A. H. Henslee Made Statements of Conviction in Frank's Guilt Long Before Trial

Judge Roan Sure to Hear Trial Motion

Solicitor Dorsey Busily at Work on Reply to Defense and Will Be Ready When Case Is Called Saturday
Additional depositions, charging that before the trial of Leo M. Frank, Juror A. H. Henslee showed prejudice and strong feeling against the defendant, have been received by Deputy Clerk John H. Jones.
The new depositions are signed by J. J. Nunnally and Virgil Harris, dealers in buggies, of Monroe, Ga., and Dr. W. L. Rickert, a dentist of the same place.

The three citizens of Walker county corroborate the five other men, who swear that Henslee before he took his juror's oath expressed his firm conviction of the guilt of the man upon whom he was to pass judgment.

All three of the Monroe citizens declared that not only did Henslee express his belief that Frank was guilty, but that he vehemently and bitterly denounced the man charged with Mary Phagan's murder.

Mr. Nunnally quotes Henslee as saying:

"They are going to break that Jew's neck."

One of the makers of the depositions declares that he heard Henslee discussing the Phagan murder with a number of other traveling men before the trial. Several of them denounced Frank, the maker of the deposition swears, and Henslee was the most bitter of them all against the defendant.

In one of the depositions it is charged that for twenty minutes Henslee discussed his reasons for believing in the guilt of the accused, and was still denouncing him when the affiant left the group of men who were discussing the case.

It is said that still more depositions attacking Juror Henslee are expected by the defense.

Roan to Hear Motion

Monday all doubt that Judge L. S. Roan will hear the argument of the motion for a new trial for Frank was dispelled when court attaches cancelled arrangements to hold a session of the criminal division of the superior court on Monday, October 13.

It had been expected that Judge Ben H. Hill would resign from the court of appeals and take his seat on the superior court bench in time to hold court next Monday, but now it is definitely known that he will remain on the appellate bench until Judge L. S. Roan can dispose of the Frank motion.

The motion is set for next Saturday, but there is little probability that it can be disposed of in a day or even several days, and therefore Judge Roan, as he will be hearing it as a superior court judge, cannot resign until the argument has been concluded.

The cancelled arrangements for court week mean more delay before the criminal division can hold a session to alleviate the congested condition of the county jail, where more than 100 felony prisoners are awaiting trial.

Dorsey Working

Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey is devoting his entire time to the preparation of his answer to the defense's motion for a new trial for Leo M. Frank, and very likely he will be ready when the case is called for argument before Judge L. S. Roan next Saturday.

The charges against A. H. Henslee and M. Johenning did not come as a surprise to the state, although the solicitor knew nothing of several of the affidavits.

Reports of some of the affidavits, however, had reached the solicitor before the motion was served on him, and his men have been busy in an effort to sustain the two jurors.

Mr. Dorsey is going to devote the greater part of his time to a study of the law on the questions involved in the 115 counts upon which the defense asks the new trial, while the work of sustaining the two jurors will be handled largely by his assistants.

Open Letter

The Sparta citizens, whose statements in depositions form probably the defense's strongest evidence against Henslee, have addressed a sensational open letter to the juror, following the publication of his statement that the charges that he had expressed an opinion as to Frank's guilt were lies.

Their letter follows:

"You must recall in Mr. Holmes' office, on the day stated, and in the presence of the undersigned, we all discussed the Frank case and practically tried him, as it were, and that, in the discussion, you not only said that Frank was as guilty as [illegible], but you had much to say about Frank's being a moral degenerate, your exact language we cannot use, and further stated that you were drawn as a juror.

"We have no disposition to injure you or to make public your statement, as two of the witnesses, Gray and Holmes, have known you and your family for many years, and we do not know how the attorneys were acquainted with the fact of this conversation, but your remark was common talk in the town where there are a number of people who could have given the information to the attorneys.

"We declined to make a voluntary affidavit in the matter and said nothing until forced to by the court, but let us assure you that the reluctance to testify in no way changes the fact and you shall not be permitted to make statements in the public press denouncing us as liars in order to protect yourself from the criticism you have justly deserved.

"We await your answer.

"J. M. HOLMES,

"S. M. JOHNSON,

"SHI GRAY."

Police Are Likened to the Walls of a City

The Atlanta Journal
Monday, October 6, 1913
Page 4, Column 1

Dr. White Preaches Special Sermon Because of Admiration of Chief Beavers

More than a hundred officers and men of the Atlanta police force attended services at the Second Baptist church Sunday evening and listened to the special sermon preached to them by the pastor, Dr. John E. White.

"The policeman of today has the same relative value to a city as the walls had in ancient times," declared Dr. White.

"You can always judge a man's citizenship by his attitude toward the police force, and when I see a man attacking the preservers of law and order, and trying to get them into disrepute before the people, I know what sort of a citizen he is."

In the course of his sermon Dr. White explained that he had been prompted to preach to the police because of his admiration for Chief Beavers and his respect for the individual members of the force, and because it was the duty of a preacher to uphold law and order and endeavor to aid the preservers of it.

Dr. White's text, "I have set a watch upon the walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never sleep day or night," was taken from the thirty-second chapter of Isaiah.
The church was taxed to its capacity to accommodate the large congregation which attended to hear the sermon.
Newt Lee Gets No Coin for Time Spent in Jail

The Atlanta Journal
Monday, October 6, 1913
Page 9, Column 1

County Commission Refuses to Compensate Negro for Long Hours in Tower

The board of county commissioners at a meeting Monday refused to grant the petition of Graham & Chappell, attorneys for Newt Lee, that the county compensate the negro for the several months he spent in jail, held as a witness pending the trial of Leo M. Frank.

The petition was not granted because there is no law to allow the county to compensate a witness held by the order of the courts.

The legal phase of the matter was decided by General Clifford L. Anderson, as County Attorney Luther Rosser had declined to render an opinion on the legality of the petition because he is counsel for Frank.

Lee was held by the order of the state's authorities, not the county officials, General Anderson held, and while several of the commissioners expressed sympathy for the negro, they all voted to refuse his petition for compensation.

The commission also refused to grant the request of L. O. Turner, a member of the jury in the Camp murder case, to pay the bill of a physician who attended him when he was ill while locked up in the Kimball hotel as a member of the jury.

The commission refused this request on the same ground; namely, that if anyone is responsible it is the state, not the county.

Reference
