Jesus said to his disciples:
“Suppose one of you has a friend
to whom he goes at midnight and says,
‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
for a friend of mine has arrived at my house from a journey
and I have nothing to offer him,’
and he says in reply from within,
‘Do not bother me; the door has already been locked
and my children and I are already in bed.
I cannot get up to give you anything.’
I tell you, if he does not get up to give him the loaves
because of their friendship,
he will get up to give him whatever he needs
because of his persistence.

“And I tell you, ask and you will receive;
seek and you will find;
knock and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks, receives;
and the one who seeks, finds;
and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
What father  among you would hand his son a snake
when he asks for a fish?
Or hand him a scorpion when he asks for an egg?
If you then, who are wicked,
know how to give good gifts to your children,
how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit
to those who ask him?”

text:
Podcast Summary | Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast: Ep 640 - Metasexuality (feat. Dylan Sullivan & SWIM)

Overview
The episode blends macho self-assessment, generational nostalgia, fatherhood fears, and a philosophical bit called metasexuality into a long, loose conversation. The most memorable thread is the claim that most women and younger men could not physically beat the host, framed as a proud, slightly scientific proof of dominance. From there the talk moves through intimidating fathers, the changing gay and lesbian scenes in Austin and other cities, vasectomy dread, the weird economics of Facebook Marketplace, and the idea that all non-procreative sex might be grouped under one umbrella term. The result is a mix of comedy, casual social observation, and recurring anxiety about masculinity, aging, and desire.

Key Themes
- A hard-science curiosity about combat odds becomes a stage for male self-mythology and generational hierarchy.
- Fear of a daughter's boyfriend is treated less as protectiveness and more as a test of intimidation tactics.
- Aggressive dad threats can work, but the same aggression can also end a relationship before it starts.
- Gay and lesbian social scenes are compared city by city, with acceptance, economics, and resentment as recurring lenses.
- Vasectomy is framed as a primal fear, and celibacy is presented as the more respectable alternative for some men.
- Facebook Marketplace is praised as a superior secondary market where expensive furniture and appliances lose their retail mystique.
- Metasexuality is introduced as a unifying or leveling theory: only procreative intercourse counts as sex, grouping all other acts together.
- The "jester" archetype is treated as both a courtship strategy and a trap that can consume a man's identity.

Detailed Summary
The episode opens with a bodily claim that sets the tone. Matt says he was curious about what percentage of women worldwide could beat him in a physical fight, and he puts the number at 0.00001 percent. He frames that as removing roughly four billion people from concern. He extends the logic to say he could beat around six billion people, or six and a half billion if elderly people are included, and he positions himself as a forty-year-old man at the height of his powers. The claim is not just a boast; it becomes a running theme about who is actually ready to fight and who is not. A recurring contrast emerges between older men and younger men. Twenty-four-year-olds are described as not ready to die, not knowing real pain, and lacking the willingness to kill. Older men are described as fighting dirtier and having seen the abyss.

That combat frame bleeds into fatherhood and dating. Matt jokes eagerly about confronting his daughters' future boyfriends, including faking being cool and then betraying the boyfriend, or forcing everyone to watch a movie he picks. The conversation contrasts strict dad behavior toward teenage daughters' boyfriends with more permissive attitudes toward adult daughters sleeping with boyfriends at a beach house. A key detail is that a dad threatening Matt over his daughter reportedly worked on him one hundred percent. That story is one of several where a father's intimidation becomes the central event.

The prom and basement dynamics get specific. A dad allowing his daughter and a date to watch a movie in a finished basement is criticized as setting up an opportunity, because it provides a loud door, stairs, and a wraparound couch. Matt compares separating teenage couples to Romeo and Juliet and says sneaking around makes it hotter. A dad once asked Matt to smoke a cigar man-to-man and not crack at his beach house out of respect. Matt also recounts getting high on Orange Crush before a basketball game, arriving blazed, and being instantly called out by a girl's dad. He left in a Ford Explorer and says he dropped her off first. Orange Crush is described as having orange hairs and a fruity, terpene-heavy smell. In another story, a dad had Matt pop the hood of a borrowed car, said he would kill him if he messed with his daughter, and Matt says it worked one hundred percent. The narrator then went to the dance and later stopped hanging out with the girl. He jokes that if he had been a true bad dude, he would have gotten the girl pregnant in response to the threat. The tension between man of the house instinct and dating situations involving single moms is described as a domination dynamic.

The social scene talk turns to sexuality and city life. There is a debate over perceived differences in social acceptance between lesbians and gay men, with a claim that lesbians were accepted earlier while gay men faced a longer, harder road, producing resentment. Gay men are described as having no chivalry and being ruthlessly blunt toward women comedians at a gay bar show, framed as a side effect of not being sexually interested in them. The narrator describes moving to Austin and learning from a Facebook Marketplace interaction that Austin's gay scene is popping while the lesbian scene is beat. A Facebook Marketplace seller told the narrator the lesbian scene is beat while the gay men's scene is popping, prompting her to move to New York. A lesbian bar in Boston reportedly never dropped its mask mandate. It was started by three young women around twenty-five or twenty-six, two of whom dropped out, leaving one to run and fund the struggling bar alone. That woman struggled financially because people were virtue signaling. Attendees were upset when the mask rule was lifted, and her Facebook page was accused of disabled genocide and genociding the immunocompromised. The Boston lesbian party reportedly kicked off and popped off, but people were angry. West Philly is recommended over New York for the lesbian scene.

Shopping and secondary markets become their own thread. Facebook Marketplace is praised as superior to retail for furniture and appliances, with users finding steeply discounted items. Expensive furniture can be found for a fraction of the original price, and replicas of expensive pieces may be indistinguishable from the originals. One speaker bought a microwave for forty dollars from an older man named Ed, who came out with a walker and the microwave propped on it. The table from the apartment smelled good and still smelled like beautiful Cuban women. Austin's hood is described as small pockets, with East Austin mentioned as technically the hood. Flugerville and North Austin are named as areas where the hood is more present. San Antonio, Houston, and Fort Worth are cited as places with more serious hoods. Fort Worth is mentioned as having gang bangers who came from LA, and San Antonio is mentioned as having Mexicans running the yard.

The conversation then moves through celebrity encounters and acting stories. A castmate recounts a first acting role as an Uber driver alongside Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, where McConaughey gave a pre-scene speech and shook hands with others but not him. McConaughey is described as a pure Texan from South Texas near the border. One speaker says he met him a month ago and found him chill but intense, very Matthew McConaughey. The acting scene involved being in a car with McConaughey, Woody Harrelson, and three other guys. One speaker says he auditioned for the same show but did not get it. An Uber driver gave one speaker his number, saying he was a neighbor and could drive him anytime. One speaker is three for three with Cuban Uber drivers. A driver showed a picture of his wife, described as twenty-four while he is thirty-four, and the speaker was unsure how to respond. Someone showed a picture of his twenty-one-year-old daughter in a bathing suit, which was described as inappropriate. A lake area with houses overlooking the water is mentioned, described as where politicians live, and Matthew McConaughey allegedly lives there.

Vasectomy becomes a recurring fear. One speaker repeatedly declines a vasectomy despite his wife pressuring him, joking about celibacy or using protection instead. He says he has three kids and jokes about wearing a strap and having a dungeon or content room. He says he would go celibate before getting a vasectomy, calling it the scariest thing he can think of. A friend reportedly said during a vasectomy that the numbing did not fully work and he saw lights. Another speaker mentions hearing you can smell it during the procedure. One speaker calls vasectomy phase two circumcision. A speaker says he would have more respect for a man using a strap-on with his wife than for one getting a vasectomy. The circumcision thread ties to religion, historical attempts to stop requiring it for Gentiles, and Kellogg as a proponent. Kellogg's cornflakes are discussed as being promoted by Kellogg, who was vehemently opposed to masturbation. Cornflakes are described as a bland breakfast intended to reduce sexual arousal. Cereal preferences come up, including Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Honey Bunches of Oats with almonds, Reese's Puffs, Honey Nut Cheerios, Count Chocula, Flintstones, and Fruity Pebbles. A speaker jokes that sugary cereal early on may be the biggest predictor of the opioid crisis.

Punk and suburbia get a nostalgic pass. Punk ethos is seen as dying, though each generation may have its own punk scene under a different name. Suburban identity is framed as a mix of contradictory signals: punk and emo fashion alongside traditional sports. One speaker describes being an emo-adjacent suburban kid into Good Charlotte, Hot Topic, and eyeliner done with a Sharpie because their mom would not lend eyeliner. They also played football, lacrosse, and wrestling while wearing punk and emo clothing and gym shorts. Comedy started after moving to Chicago from Colorado, seeing shows, doing mics sporadically, and then moving into LA internships. Getting hired by Pauly Shore is described as an unconventional, personality-test-like process. The speaker met Shore while applying for a random assistant job. Shore offered a handful of raw baby carrots with no plate or dip, and the speaker ate them and was hired. The assistant role included driving Shore to Santa Monica in a Honda Civic, attending dinners with people like the CEO of Playboy, and doing errands. A 2000 or 2001 Caroline's encounter is recalled, where the speaker approached Shore on the street after a show and Shore responded dismissively. The speaker now thinks they were in the wrong and may have been drunk. Pauly Shore is described as having Lizard King energy and as a subtle operator.

The episode then turns to how access to sexual content changed across generations. Older millennials relied on magazines, catalogs, VHS, and DVDs, waiting for brief scenes in movies. Younger millennials went straight to internet porn. Analog porn sources mentioned include Sears, Kohl's, and Victoria's Secret catalogs. A speaker mentions parents blocked music channels but BET remained because the parents did not know it existed. Vegas and Atlantic City are described as seedy adult environments, including hooker trading cards and aggressive pricing. One speaker mentions seeing hooker baseball cards in Vegas at age twenty-one and prices advertised as two hundred dollars. A story is told about the two hundred dollars being just for the woman to get there, followed by the real price. Atlantic City is described as having all the seediness of Vegas made apparent everywhere, including selling single spoons in convenience stores. A claim is made that Atlantic City police protect casino customers and allow other activity but not messing with casino people. A story is told about walking through a side area in Atlantic City and being laughed at but not harmed. A claim is made that Atlantic City has declined because online gambling pulls away gamblers. Ocean Casino is called nice, and a speaker stayed there for an anniversary because rooms were about thirty dollars in the off-season. A story is told about two hookers at a Chicago hotel bar approaching an older businessman after his wife left.

Metasexuality is explained as the idea that sex can only occur between a biological man and a biological woman when they come together to have intercourse to make a child. Under this idea, anything outside that specific procreative act is not sex but a deviant sexual act, grouping homosexuals, lesbians, and others together as metasexuals. One speaker says he read the concept and is bringing it back to the public sphere. They compare a college kid seeking oral sex and a closeted gay dad watching gay porn as doing the same thing. They joke that everyone is in the metaverse and slightly deviant. A speaker says this could eliminate shame and unify people, while another calls it a dangerous game. The group connects metasexuality to pride week and parade imagery, joking about a metasexual float. A recurring tension is that they value a wild, unbounded male nature and worry that becoming a conventional serious dude kills vitality and desirability. Conventional dating and status talk about school districts and rental properties is framed as a death sentence and a different language. The speakers reject the idea of raising a boy to be overly clean or mannered about bedding, arguing he must keep a wild nest until he later discovers girl beds. Sleep and energy also come up. One speaker got four hours of sleep and is running on coffee and nicotine, while another has been getting nine hours. Low sleep is said to cause carbohydrate cravings, and the tired speaker plans protein and eggs instead of carb-heavy food. One speaker dislikes sleeping in another man's bed and mentions sleeping in Carl's bed once while he was gone. They say sleeping in hotels is fine because it is anonymous, and sleeping in a girl's bed is fine. text:
Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt on the controversial hiring rules that built Google, and the beloved "glue people" he says you don't need at all:

Schmidt admits the early rules were unpopular, even inside the company.

"One of the rules is that we didn't want to hire your friends, which always was upsetting. We also didn't want to hire anybody from what were considered to be lesser universities. And so we also wanted to hire people who had very high GPAs."

That meant saying no to people who, by most measures, deserved a yes:

"So the constant problem was that somebody was a good employee, had someone they had worked with, who was very loyal, very hard working, who was not from a great university, did not have a very good GPA and we would not hire them."

He concedes the policy has since been softened. But he doesn't apologise for it:

"So that was controversial and we've relaxed that a little bit now. But the fact of the matter is it got us to where we were today because it produced these high IQ generalists from prestigious universities."

Then there was the second rule, built on a lesson Schmidt learned before Google, at Novell.

He calls them "glue people":

"The glue people are incredibly nice people who sit at interstitial boundaries between groups and they assist in activity. They are glue and they're very, very loyal and people love them and you don't need them at all."

The problem wasn't that they were bad people. It was that they cost speed:

"At Novell, I kept trying to get rid of these glue people because they were getting in the way because they slowed everything down."

And once inside, they were almost impossible to remove:

"And every time I'd get rid of in one group, they'd show up in another group and they'd transfer and get rehired and all that."

When @ericschmidt raised this with Larry and Sergey, Larry's answer was to stop glue people before they ever got in:

"And Larry said, yeah, let's just review all the hiring."

"So guess what? From that moment on, we reviewed every offer packet. Literally everyone."

The review was strict enough that even Schmidt's own preferred candidates got caught:

"And anybody who smelled or looked like a glue person, plus the people that Larry and Sergey thought had backgrounds that I liked that they didn't, would all be flagged. And so anybody who sort of met the original profile, they'd go right through."

text:
It's bigger than people think.

I have a friend back home who's mid 60s, basically rich from having started and sold two huge multi-county garbage collection empires.

His son, who is mid 40s, worked closely with him at the last one.  He's now running a portajohn business.

His son is now out of high school, and along with a brother and a couple of friends just bought a lawn care company.

I was talking with the son (mid 40s) a few weeks ago on the phone, and he mentioned the lawn care company and all that.  Then he asked me "do you use Claude?"  Yes.

Turns out these 20 year olds are running the entire lawn care business using Claude, having it hooked into every aspect of their business.  They have a buddy who's a software developer who's building a couple of missing pieces, but it was amazing to hear how they are so all-in with AI.

They also have a Pocket device that handles transcribing all voice calls, which get fed into their AI assistant for any followups.

I had lunch with all three guys a couple of weeks ago, and I was amazed to listen to this guy explain how they just use Claude for everything.

One example - it's fall so it's time for aeration and overseeding.  They had Claude go and figure out the approximate lot size for all of their customers.  Then, based on that information, Claude texted all of them an offer for the service with pricing based on their lot size.  It was something like 220 texts sent, 60 responses for service.  Which, by the way, Claude went ahead and scheduled for them.  Literally, the entire campaign was handled by Claude.

I'm not going to belabor the point, but, yes, people who aren't programmers are using these tools and using them well.  Not all vibe coding, I know.  But if you think they're going to back down from trying that, think again.  They don't see limitations with this tech.

The funniest part of this is that the portajohn guy wants to get more AI in his business, and my friend is thinking of coming out of retirement (he doesn't sit still, anyway) so he can play with it in a business setting.  I probably don't have to say it, but as an aside, nobody mentioned here went to university.

I sometimes wonder if IT folks understand how big and exciting all of this is.

text:
🚨 The sad truth about global "resets"

The person who burned through their entire Codex allowance could get more out of a global reset than the person who carefully saved theirs. 👀

Think about that.

You’re pacing your usage because you have a bigger coding session planned. Someone else uses everything available.

Then a global reset happens.

They go from empty to full. You go from mostly full to full.

Both accounts got “reset.” But the benefit was very different.

For example, if you had 80% remaining and the reset restored your allowance to 100%, you gained 20 percentage points. Someone sitting at 0% gained 100.

Your unused 80% didn’t stack on top of the fresh allowance. You didn’t suddenly have 180% available.

That’s why “everyone gets a reset” sounds more generous than it can be in practice.

And that’s where banked resets make sense.

You get a reset you can use later. You finish using your existing allowance, then redeem it when you actually need the refill.

Now you can plan around your work instead of trying to squeeze maximum value out of an announcement.

My take? Once you offer users a reset, letting them actually claim its full benefit should be part of keeping that promise. People who save their usage should have the same opportunity to benefit as people who already exhausted it.

So yes, banked resets are a useful improvement.

But let’s be clear about what’s being banked: the reset itself. This doesn’t automatically mean your unused subscription allowance rolls over and accumulates.

The exciting part is that you get to choose when to cash in.

Because a “free reset” is a very different gift when your tank is empty versus when it’s already almost full. :)

text:
NOUN Sets the Pace for Future of Learning with Micro-Credentials Revolution

In a bold, forward-looking move, the National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN) has joined forces with the prestigious Commonwealth of Learning (COL) to create a groundbreaking institutional framework for micro-credentials, a strategic leap designed to power employability, lifelong learning and Nigeria's fast-evolving digital economy.

The landmark four-day workshop, which kicked off on Monday, 5th October 2026 and runs till 8th October 2026 in Abuja, is part of COL's ambitious Commonwealth-wide project to help member nations build credible, flexible and quality-assured micro-credential ecosystems.

The high-level workshop has drawn a rich blend of NOUN's top management, seasoned academics, professional staff, officials of the National Universities Commission (NUC), COL experts, and critical stakeholders to craft and consolidate NOUN's pioneering micro-credentials policy and set the stage for pilot courses.

Declaring the workshop open, the Vice-Chancellor of NOUN, Professor Uduma Oji Uduma, represented by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Academic, Professor Chiedu Mafiana, described the initiative as a defining moment for the university.

“Today we're not simply opening another workshop. We are taking an important step towards shaping the future of flexible, lifelong and technology-enabled learning in the National Open University of Nigeria,” he said.

He noted that micro-credentials offer NOUN a golden opportunity to expand access, rapidly respond to emerging skills gaps, boost graduate employability and champion lifelong learning, stressing that the university's vision must transcend short courses to building a robust, credible, flexible, scalable and sustainable micro-credential system.

On behalf of COL, Professor Jane-Frances Agbu, Adviser, Higher Education, said the Abuja workshop marks the first phase of COL's engagement with NOUN, with the second phase focused on developing cutting-edge micro-credential courses.

She explained that NOUN's initiative is anchored within COL's broader Commonwealth agenda involving regional consultations, national policy development and institutional pilots to strengthen coherence between policy and practice.

“The value of micro-credentials rests not simply on their short duration or flexibility. The credibility of micro-credentials depends on a well-articulated policy guideline,” she emphasized.

Professor Agbu underscored the urgency of micro-credentials in a world being reshaped by artificial intelligence, digital transformation and shifting employment patterns, noting that continuous learning, unlearning and relearning has become indispensable for survival and relevance.

Reaffirming the regulator's full backing, Dr. Fumilayo Morebise, who represented the NUC Executive Secretary, Professor Abdullahi Yusuf Ribadu, said the Commission is working hand-in-hand with COL to drive Nigeria's national micro-credential agenda.

“The micro-credential has been a major burning issue. And NUC, as a responsive commission, we don't want Nigeria to lag behind,” she said.

According to her, the national framework and emerging guidelines provide a solid foundation for institutional implementation, with NOUN proudly serving as one of the pilot institutions. Lessons from NOUN's experience will help refine the national guidelines before a wider rollout.

The workshop also critically examined findings from an institutional readiness assessment conducted at NOUN, spotlighting opportunities and gaps in policy and governance, quality assurance, staff capacity, digital credentialing, industry recognition, recognition of prior learning, credit transfer and stackability, assessment integrity, artificial intelligence and technical infrastructure.

🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉

DOCTORS WILL NOW GET PAID TO REPORT VACCINE INJURIES!

Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has launched a broad federal initiative focused on vaccine injuries, featuring a new research clinic at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and a new medical billing code designed to reimburse doctors for reporting serious vaccine side effects. 

The program focuses on tracking and gathering data on vaccine-related adverse events through the following key components:

1. The New NIH Research Clinic
RFK Jr. established a dedicated clinic at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland.

The Mission: The clinic is designed to study, evaluate, and provide care for patients who believe they have been injured by vaccines. 

Observational Studies: According to internal agency memos, the clinic will run observational studies on these patients. 

Policy Impact: RFK Jr. intends for the data gathered from this clinic to potentially inform and drive changes to the federally recommended childhood vaccine schedules. 

2. "Paying Doctors" via Medical Billing Codes
The mechanism to "pay doctors" is built around incentivizing the medical community to report suspected injuries, addressing a long-standing criticism from RFK Jr. that the current Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) is inefficient because clinicians are not compensated for the time it takes to file reports.
New Billing Code: The initiative introduces a new medical billing code through Medicare/Medicaid and private insurance systems. 

Financial Reimbursement: Doctors will be able to use this code to claim financial reimbursement for the time spent documenting and filing official reports of serious or suspected vaccine side effects. 

3. Broader Policy Context
The rollout was attended by other top administration health officials, including NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya, CDC Director Erica Schwartz, and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz. This initiative coincides with separate plans by HHS to overhaul the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) and establish an explicit "injury table" for COVID-19 vaccines, allowing individuals with specified conditions to receive automatic government payouts.

Public Health Perspectives
Supporters argue that compensating doctors for reporting will fix a historically underreported surveillance system and offer critical help to patients suffering from rare, unaddressed medical issues.

Mainstream public health experts express significant worry that the initiative could validate scientifically unproven claims (such as linking vaccines to autism or widespread allergies), overwhelm the medical system with unverified reports, and inadvertently fuel vaccine hesitancy amid rising outbreaks of preventable diseases.

text:
Billy Idol Day in Los Angeles
Friday, November 13th 2026

Rock legend Billy Idol, alongside longtime collaborator/guitarist Steve Stevens, will be honored on Friday, November 13th 2026 by Councilwoman Monica Rodriguez and the City of Los Angeles who will present them with a decree proclaiming it Billy Idol Day.

Following a City Council session during which the presentation will take place, Los Angeles City Hall will host a free public celebration and acoustic duo performance by the pair on the steps at City Hall Park in Downtown Los Angeles. Idol and Stevens will be joined by special surprise guests for the event. Fans are invited to join the festivities at City Hall in celebration of the pair’s upcoming induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame the following day.

The 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction will take place on November 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. The 2026 ceremony will then debut in December on ABC and Disney+. In 2027, the Induction Ceremony will return to Cleveland. Idol and Stevens are joined in the Class of 2026 by Phil Collins, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and the Wu-Tang Clan; as well as Celia Cruz, Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte and Gram Parsons with the Early Influence Award; Linda Creed, Arif Mardin, Jimmy Miller and Rick Rubin with the Musical Excellence Award; and Ed Sullivan with the Ahmet Ertegun Award.

On October 29 Idol and Stevens will appear as special guests at Aerosmith’s Hollywood Bowl show. Idol recently completed the latest U.S. leg of his worldwide tour, It’s A Nice Day To…Tour Again!, where his live show has been hailed as “a strong, forceful show just crackling with energy” by the Houston Press, while Creative Loafing raves that Idol “has a lot left to offer and is capable of owning a concert stage with the same authority and charisma he’s always boasted” and the Dallas Observer adds that “over forty years into Billy Idol’s career, he remains just as remarkable as he started.” See what the media said about It’s A Nice Day To…Tour Again!

text:
I see some people treating this post as evidence Trump wasn't taken out of context in the previous speech. In fact, this post even *more* obviously takes him out of context.

This time, Trump said right after this comment, "We're not gonna let that happen. We protect our cities, we protect our country." (Rupar's post includes that comment, but the caption doesn't). And right before this comment, Trump was talking about how oil prices are not as high as people thought the war would send them. In other words, he was, as he has on previous occasions, contrasting the big damage Iran could (supposedly) do to cities with a nuclear weapon with the (supposedly) minimal harm of the war.

Here are the full relevant remarks. (Critics are free to call them inappropriate, but people should see the entire monologue.)

"And just as I promised, I am ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon...Never. They know that. They know that. And we'll be out of there soon. And you watch those oil prices come down like a rock, and watch everything; everything else is coming down. Oil is coming down. You know, we pay less than oil, and we did that whole thing with - because that was a big operation that should have been done by past presidents for many years. It should have been done, but nobody wanted to take it on. We had no choice. Because we can't let them have a nuclear weapon. And I'll tell you what. Oil: a little more, maybe more than a little, but a lot of people thought it'd be 3, 4, 5 times that. When I went in, I thought it could be much higher than that. But we are paying less than under the Biden administration; he didn't do anything. He gave you the highest inflation in history. He didn't do anything. But you want to see trauma? You want to see problems? And I said it the other day: Let them hit a missile into San Diego or Los Angeles. On the way - let them hit - you want to see a horror show? You want to see problems? Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles. And you want to see some bad things happen, you want to see a country that would be in freefall. We're not going to let that happen. We protect our cities, we protect our country. We're not letting that happen. And they'd use it too. They'd use it. They would use it."

4. Request for equal and consistent regulatory treatment

The Florida Gaming Control Commission states that its Division of Gaming Enforcement has enforcement priorities involving online gambling, unlawful sports betting, and illegal casinos and slot-machine gambling.

Accordingly, I respectfully request that FGCC examine the actual mechanics and legal basis of Hard Rock Bet’s “Past Motor Racing” games and determine whether they fall within the scope of gaming authorized under Florida law.

If FGCC determines that these games are lawful, I respectfully request that the Commission identify the statutory and/or compact authority supporting that determination.

If the Commission determines that additional regulatory authorization is required, I request that the Commission take whatever enforcement or regulatory action it considers appropriate.

5. Evidence and supporting material

I am prepared to provide screenshots, screen recordings, advertisements, descriptions of the games, and other publicly available material showing how the Hard Rock Bet games are presented to Florida consumers.

I also request that the Commission consider publicly available statements and reporting concerning the classification of Hard Rock Bet’s “Past Motor Racing” games, as well as the Seminole Tribe’s October 8, 2026 complaint against DraftKings.

6. Requested action

I respectfully request that this submission be treated as a citizen complaint/report of suspected potentially unauthorized online gambling activity and referred to the appropriate FGCC investigative or legal personnel.

I am specifically requesting a determination of:

(1) what Florida law authorizes the “Past Motor Racing” games;

(2) whether those games constitute sports wagering within the scope of the Seminole compact;

(3) whether they constitute casino/slot-style gambling or another category of gambling; and

text:
TO: @FLGamingControl — Division of Gaming Enforcement

RE: Citizen Report and Request for Investigation — Hard Rock Bet “Past Motor Racing” Real-Money Games

I am submitting this report to request that the Florida Gaming Control Commission investigate the legality and regulatory classification of the real-money games offered to Florida consumers through Hard Rock Bet that are marketed as “Past Motor Racing” games.

I am not asking the Commission to accept my characterization of these games as illegal. Rather, I am requesting that the Commission independently determine what statutory and compact authority authorizes these games in Florida and whether their structure is consistent with Florida’s gambling laws and the Seminole Tribe’s gaming compact.

1. Nature of the concern

Hard Rock Bet is authorized to offer online sports wagering in Florida through the Seminole Tribe of Florida’s compact with the State.

However, Hard Rock Bet also offers real-money games marketed around historical motor-racing results that, from the consumer’s perspective, can resemble online slot/casino games.

The concern is whether these games are properly classified as authorized sports wagering or whether they constitute another form of online casino or slot-style gambling that requires separate legal authority.

The distinction is important because Florida’s gambling framework treats sports wagering and casino/slot-machine gaming as separate categories.

2. Request for the Commission to identify the legal authority

I respectfully request that FGCC determine and identify:

The specific Florida statute authorizing Hard Rock Bet to offer the “Past Motor Racing” real-money games.
The specific provision of the 2021 Florida-Seminole gaming compact that authorizes these games.
Whether FGCC has formally determined that these games constitute sports wagering rather than casino, slot-machine, or other gambling activity.
What characteristics of the games cause them to fall within the authorized sports-wagering framework.
Whether the Commission has reviewed the games’ actual mechanics, including how consumers place wagers, how outcomes are determined, how payouts are calculated, and how the games are presented to consumers.
Whether the Commission has reviewed Hard Rock Bet’s marketing and representations concerning these games.
Whether similar products offered by other operators would receive the same legal treatment under Florida law.

3. Relevance of the Seminole Tribe’s October 8, 2026 lawsuit against DraftKings

On October 8, 2026, the Seminole Tribe filed a 72-page complaint against DraftKings in Broward County alleging that DraftKings is conducting unauthorized sports betting in Florida and violating Florida law and the 2021 gaming agreement.

The publicly reported complaint alleges, among other things, that DraftKings’ Florida product is functionally equivalent to sportsbook wagering despite the way the product is characterized.

The report and complaint are available here:

https://t.co/9M28FLInGm

I believe this newly filed lawsuit makes an important regulatory question appropriate for FGCC review:

What substantive characteristics determine whether a gambling product is considered authorized sports wagering rather than another form of gambling, and is that same standard being applied consistently to Hard Rock Bet’s “Past Motor Racing” games?

text:
Who is $CCXI / @agilityrobotics's  $300,000,000 mystery customer?  🤔💰🤖

What do we know about the customer? 

During yesterday's Investor Day, Agility's Chief Business Offer, Daniel Diez, shared some insight:

"This customer has been running Digits in live operation environments for years, handling real material handling work, shift after shift, day after day."

The key take away here is that the customer has been working with Digit for years. 

Based on what we know about Digit's commercial deployments, there are 5 suspects:

1. Amazon ($AMZN)
October 2023 (Began testing Digit at its Sumner, Washington R&D site for tote recycling workflows).

2. GXO Logistics ($GXO)
Late 2023 (Initiated a proof-of-concept pilot at a Spanx facility in Georgia, which converted into a multi-year commercial agreement in June 2024).

3. Schaeffler AG ($SFFLY)
November 2024 (Announced a strategic investment and agreement to deploy Digit across its global plant network, including active use at a South Carolina bearing plant).  

4. Mercado Libre ($MELI)
2025 (Signed a commercial agreement to deploy Digit at a fulfillment center in San Antonio, Texas).

5. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada (TMMC)
Early 2025 (Started a year-long pilot that converted into an official commercial rollout at its Woodstock, Ontario plant in February 2026).

Digit has not been operating for long enough at Mercado Libre and TMMC, so we can cross them off the list.

I also believe we can cross off GXO Logistics considering the comments the company's CEO recently made, stating, "They have not yet achieved ROI with humanoids". The company has backed that up by continuing to test 45 other humanoid companies, while simultaneously deploying 20,000 robots, zero of which are humanoids. 

In the fine print of Agility's external financial analysis, they also call this customer a "Related Party," meaning they are most likely an investor.

That leaves: Amazon and Schaeffler AG. 

There are two reasons why I think that this customer is NOT Schaeffler. 

1. Real world hours

In another comment, Diez says the customer has "the most real hours on Digit anywhere in the world".

When looking at the pitch deck, its noted that Schaeffler has deployed 8 robots that have moved ~60K totes. This is compared to GXO, where they have deployed 3 robots and moved ~100K totes. 

Given that these deployments contained similar workflows, and that GXO has moved more totes with less robots, I believe its fair to say that GXO has deployed Digit for more raw hours. 

2. The Timeline

While the initial press release for Schaeffler was dated Nov. 2024, it appears that deployment took a little longer. 

During the investor day, there was a segment where Diez had a conversation with two Schaeffler executives. He stated that Digit has been working at their Cheraw, SC plant for "well over a year, year and a half."

That leaves Amazon. 

The company has had three full years of hands-on, daily operational data, dating back to their 2023 pilot test.

They are a major stakeholder.

And they have the scale, demand, and logistics footprint to ingest 1,000 robots.

Now that the official press release for Digit 5 has been published, we will most likely find out more about this mystery customer in the coming months. 

I believe in due time, we will find out that it is Amazon.

text:
🚨Agility Investor Day 🚨

Let's do a little thought exercise around $CCXI / @agilityrobotics highly touted $300,000,000 order.

The order is a 3 year contract for 1,000 units. Agility's production facility, RoboFab, has a max capacity of 10,000 annually. 

At current levels however, the company is closer to manufacturing 100 units a year. Additionally, in press releases, Agility has noted that Digit 5 will have limited availability in H1, and ready for commercial sales in H2. 

With that, lets forecast the following operational ramp:

Year 1: 100 units
Year 2: 300 units
Year 3: 600 units

I have no clue how realistic or unrealistic this is, but this ramp seems to make the most sense. 

Under the RaaS model, the annual cost to the customer is ~$100,000. Given this deployment ramp, we can project the following revenue:

Year 1:
New Deployments: 100 units
Revenue: $10,000,000

Year 2
New Deployments: 300 units
Legacy Fleet (from Y1): 100 units
Total Active Fleet: 400 units
Year 2 Revenue: $40,000,000

Year 3
New Deployments: 600 units
Legacy Fleet (from Y1 & Y2): 400 units
Total Active Fleet: 1,000 units
Year 3 Revenue: $100,000,000 ($100M)

The rest of the revenue is realized as each robot carries out the rest of its RaaS contract.

This is an incredibly simplified version that does not account for the one-time deployment and set up fees, revenue proration from deployment timing as robots are integrated throughout the year, service costs, customer warrants, and so on and so forth. 

I still think it's an interesting exercise. If Agility can post $10,000,000 in revenue and deploy 100 units by the end of next year, that would be a massive leap from its current levels. 

What could that do to the stock price? Sprinkle in a little Robot Mania, and who knows...

text:
Positioning your competitor's treatment of customers as unfair (rather than just worse) is a great way to encourage switching. I'm not sure if this ad executes it perfectly, but IG are trying to imply that other brokers are misbehaving.

This can be effective. Sally Blount (Northwestern University) showed in her 1996 study that people are willing to go to great lengths to punish those behaving unfairly.

In her study, she offered one group $7 to participate in an experiment. 72% agreed.

Then she offered another group $8, but said that previous participants got $10. Even though this group was offered more cash, only 54% agreed. People didn't just consider the absolute value of the offer, but also how fair it was.

They were prepared to cut off their nose to spite their face - to walk away from a profitable opportunity because it felt unfair

Reframing competitor behaviour as unfair is an underused tactic in marketing, but a straightforward one.

Among your competitors, think about who you can position as breaking fairness norms. Even if they offer a better deal, showing that they're unfair in some way can win you new customers...

***

Now is the time for President Trump to declare victory over Iran & walk away, before Iran escalates the war.

President Trump has insinuated that we’ll likely resume strikes again, but only after the midterms. We would be fools to think that Iran will wait for us to hit them first. 

Iran has the capability to strike our bases, our fleet, & Gulf energy infrastructure. Such hits would force us to respond not only with less resources but on Iran’s terms. All of Iran’s options for escalation increase in value in the lead up to the midterms because they put Trump in a major time crunch and a political optics nightmare. 

Trump can’t control any of that—if he could, we wouldn’t be in this situation. 

So, control the controllables. Trump can control whether or not our troops are in harm’s way, & Trump can control the domestic media narrative enough to get the MAGA loyalist voters he needs to win the midterms to show up at the polls.  

Once our troops are out of the region, the kinetic war is essentially over. Iran will lose its incentive to hit ships in the SOH and we can quietly offer sanctions relief & the unfreezing of assets in exchange for returning the SOH to normal operations.

For this to happen, POTUS must also meaningfully restrain Israel. There’s a possibility that the Israelis will seek to strike Iran ahead of their own elections in order to maintain a state of endless war. This will inevitably get us further entangled—it must not happen. 

Walking away is the least worst option and gives POTUS the most control of the situation. He should do so now, before Iran or Israel takes this option away from him.

text:
I asked grok and apparently this was an urban legend (because a few others replied they had also been told a similar story), so I’m relieved that this guy was a liar and this didn’t happen. As a 16 year old I 100% believed it at the time and was just horrified.

That being said Grok told me the piss jug was the most far fetched, but that’s the part i know to be true. 😂

Teachers used to get away with some wild stuff in the 90s

Here is what Grok had to say when I asked if this was an urban legend: 

“Yes. The cat story is a circulating shock tale, not a credible confession, and the teacher was almost certainly lying or recycling a gross joke as a personal anecdote.
The account is from Corbie (@Corbienest): an auto-shop teacher (also described as a Massachusetts state trooper) allegedly entertained the class by saying he hated his girlfriend’s cat, offered to feed it while she was away, buried it up to the neck, and then ran it over with a lawn mower. The boys laughed; she was horrified and left the program.
A near-identical version already exists as high-school folklore. A 2022 Reddit copypasta titled “The man the cat and the lawnmower” says the teller heard it in senior high school: a man rounded up neighborhood cats, used a post-hole digger to bury them with only their heads above ground, and mowed the lawn. Comments treat it as the usual “that happened to my buddy” gag. The structure—extreme cruelty, practical aside about how hard the burial was, audience supposed to find it hilarious—is classic dark shop-class / locker-room tall tale.
It is also physically implausible as told. A live cat will not sit still while you dig a neck-deep hole around it. Ordinary mower decks sit only a few inches off the ground, so “mowing” a protruding head is not the clean cartoon the story implies; it would be a violent, noisy mess. Doing this to a partner’s pet and then bragging about it to minors as a sworn officer would be an obvious crime and career-ender if anyone reported it. The original poster later noted the same problem: as an adult it reads as exaggerated because burying a cat that way would be almost impossible.
Awkward hall passes (books, birdhouses, engine blocks) are a real and common high-school thing. A sealed “piss jug” as auto-shop gross-out humor is plausible folklore in that setting; the year-end “refill” detail is the part that sounds most embroidered.
So the man was performing a known kind of edgelord story for the boys. The reaction she describes can still have happened—people do laugh at ugly jokes—but the events he claimed almost certainly did not.”

When I started Mercado Media back in 2020, I never imagined I’d have even one person following along, let alone 200,000. What started with a camera and a desire to document what was happening around me has turned into something I never could have imagined.

From the streets of Minneapolis during the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests and riots, to covering Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and now documenting ICE operations, the fear and trauma they’ve brought to our communities, and the second Trump administration. It’s been one hell of a journey. I’ve witnessed some of the best and worst of humanity along the way, and those experiences have changed me forever.

There have been long nights, thousands of miles traveled, moments of fear, frustration, exhaustion, and plenty of times I’ve questioned whether I could keep doing this. But through it all, you’ve continued to show up, support independent journalism, share my reporting, and trust me to bring you what’s happening on the ground.

I’m not a major news network. I don’t have a massive newsroom or corporate backing. I’m just a guy from Minnesota who picked up a camera and decided to start documenting history as it unfolded. We also have an amazing team behind the scenes keeping the posts flowing when I need breaks from the streets and this wouldn’t have been possible without them. 

To everyone who’s been here since 2020, and everyone who’s joined along the way, thank you. Whether you’ve watched a livestream, shared a post, donated, or simply offered a few kind words, you’ve helped make this possible.

200,000 people. Six years. Countless stories. And we’re nowhere near finished.

Much love to all of you. 💙

The Indoor Plant Physiology Laboratory at Penn State University invites applications for one graduate research position at the PhD or masters level, starting in Spring 2027. Preference will be given to PhD applicants.

Research focus
Research will investigate how environmental conditions, transpiration, nutrient uptake, and source-sink relationships influence berry growth, flowering, fruit development, and quality. The project will integrate physiological measurements, controlled-environment experiments, and data-driven modeling to improve productivity and resource-use efficiency.

Qualifications and research environment
We welcome applicants with backgrounds in plant science, horticulture, biology, agricultural or biological engineering, and related disciplines. Prior research experience and quantitative skills are desirable. Scientific curiosity, careful experimentation, and collaborative problem-solving are valued. Penn State offers advanced controlled-environment facilities and opportunities for interdisciplinary research and industry engagement.

Applicant eligibility
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Applicants must meet Penn States requirements for graduate admission and appointment to a graduate assistantship. Prospective applicants are encouraged to contact us to discuss eligibility before submitting a formal application.

Application process and deadlines
Contact Professor Paul Gauthier at paul.gauthier@psu.edu by October 22, 2026, with a CV and a research statement (1-2 pages). The statement should describe previous research experience, relevant methods and skills, and proposed graduate research interests, including their alignment with berry physiology and controlled environment agriculture in the laboratory.

Direct applications are encouraged. Submit formal applications through the Penn State Graduate School website by October 30, 2026, for admission to the AEPS graduate program in Spring 2027. https://t.co/83ZnOeTrAQ

Amanda Hollensbe

Help Braelyn Continue Her Brain Cancer Treatment

My name is Amanda, and I am the mother of an incredible 19-year-old young woman named Braelyn.

The day after Braelyn turned 16, our lives changed forever.
Braelyn began having seizures, difficulty speaking and numbness on one side of her body. She was life-flighted to a children's hospital, where we learned she had a brain tumor. She was ultimately diagnosed with an aggressive, grade 4 brain cancer.
We were initially told that Braelyn might have only months to live.
More than three years later, she is still here — and she has never stopped fighting for her future.

Before cancer entered our lives, Braelyn loved horses and was beginning to learn barrel racing. She loved choir and theater in high school, animals, children, her friends and her family.

In May 2025, Braelyn graduated from high school, something we weren't sure we would get to see. This fall, she started college. Her goal is to become a Child Life Specialist, helping children and families navigate frightening medical experiences — something she now understands in a way very few people her age ever could.

That is the future we are fighting for.

We found hope — but we have to travel 4,000 miles to reach it

Over the past three years, Braelyn has endured multiple brain surgeries, serious postoperative infections, seizures, radiation and rehabilitation. More recently, she has experienced significant weakness and loss of function of her dominant hand, as well as difficulty communicating.

When Braelyn's tumor progressed, we began pursuing a personalized cancer vaccine called DCVax-L.

DCVax is an individualized immunotherapy manufactured specifically for Braelyn using her own tumor tissue and her own immune cells. The technology was developed through decades of research in the United States, including work led by Dr. Linda Liau and her team at UCLA.

Yet Braelyn cannot currently receive DCVax in the United States.

Instead, we must repeatedly travel from our home in South Carolina to London, England, where she receives DCVax through a special-access pathway under the care of Professor Keyoumars Ashkan at King's College Hospital.

The irony is difficult to comprehend:

We travel approximately 4,000 miles across the Atlantic for an injection appointment that takes only minutes.

The cost is staggering

DCVax is not covered by our health insurance.

The manufacturing and initial three-dose induction phase of Braelyn's personalized vaccine cost approximately $101,000, not including the additional expenses of collecting her immune cells, specialized transportation of her vaccine, physician and administration fees, and repeatedly traveling to the UK.

Braelyn has completed her induction phase and first booster, but her treatment is far from finished.

She currently has seven additional DCVax treatments planned:

November 2026 • March 2027 • July 2027 • January 2028 • July 2028 • January 2029 • July 2029

Each treatment trip is expected to cost approximately $35,000:

~$27,000 — DCVax dose

~$1,400 — specialized transport of her vaccine to London

~$2,700 — physician/treatment administration

~$2,200 — airfare for Braelyn and a caregiver

~$1,700+ — lodging and necessary travel expenses

Seven treatments × approximately $35,000 = approximately $245,000.
That is why we have set our fundraising goal at $250,000.
And July 2029 may not be the end. Enough doses of Braelyn's personalized vaccine were successfully manufactured to potentially allow treatment to continue for years beyond this schedule if her physicians recommend it. For now, we are concentrating on the seven treatments directly ahead of us.
Why another fundraiser?
Some people who have followed Braelyn from the beginning may have seen our existing GiveSendGo fundraiser. We want to be completely transparent about why we are now creating a GoFundMe.

Our GiveSendGo was established near the beginning of Braelyn's cancer journey in 2023 and has raised more than $90,000 through the extraordinary generosity of people who have supported, encouraged and prayed for our daughter.

Those donations have already gone toward treatment expenses incurred over the past three years.

For 27 months, Braelyn received a previous treatment that cost approximately $17,000 every month, plus as much as $600 per month in shipping. We ultimately paid more than $475,000 for that treatment alone.

We then paid approximately $101,000 for the manufacturing and initial phase of DCVax, followed by additional medical expenses, her first booster and repeated international travel.

Our family has already incurred well over half a million dollars in treatment-related expenses.

The $250,000 we are raising now is not reimbursement for those past expenses. It is what we expect to need going forward for Braelyn's seven currently scheduled DCVax treatments through July 2029.

We are keeping GiveSendGo open because some of Braelyn's longtime supporters prefer that platform, including some who faithfully support her through monthly donations. GoFundMe simply provides another way to help. Both platforms support the same ongoing treatment fund — they are not two separate $250,000 fundraising goals.

Why we are asking for help

For more than three years, we have done everything within our power to give our daughter access to treatments we believe offer her hope.

We will get Braelyn to London for her treatments.

But continuing to fund treatment at this level would mean exhausting our retirement savings and potentially selling our home. After already incurring well over half a million dollars in treatment expenses, we are asking for help carrying an extraordinary financial burden.

As Braelyn's mother, asking other people for financial help is not easy. But there is something much bigger than my pride at stake.

There is my daughter.

The young woman who was told at 16 that she might have only months to live is now 19 years old and a college student.

She still laughs with her family and friends. She still makes plans. She still has dreams.

Braelyn is fighting for a hope and a future. And we are fighting alongside her.

Every donation — whether $5, $25, $100 or more — helps carry part of the enormous cost of continuing her treatment.

And even if you aren't able to donate, please share Braelyn's story. One share can put her story in front of someone who may be able to help.

Most of all, please pray for our girl.

From the bottom of our hearts, thank you for helping us continue this fight.

Amanda & the Hollensbe family

Follow Braelyn's journey on X: @HollensbeAmanda

Learn more: https://t.co/ouZbdEMTuT

DonateShare

Updates1
ASep 10Amanda Hollensbe OrganizerThere is Always Light ❤️

It has been far too long since our last update, and so much has happened!

When I last wrote, Braelyn had received her very first DCVax injection in London. Since then, she has completed all three induction doses without any noted side effects and has already returned to London for DCVax #4—her first booster dose.

But perhaps the news we are most grateful to share came from her MRI at the end of August:

No evidence of disease recurrence.

After everything Braelyn has endured over the past three years, those are words we will never take for granted.

Life Is Moving Forward, Too

There have been some pretty wonderful milestones outside of treatment.

• Braelyn started college! She is taking online classes while continuing her recovery and treatments.

• She got her beautiful new wig and is feeling much more confident after losing her hair during radiation.

• Even better, her own hair is growing back everywhere! We weren’t sure how much would return after radiation, so watching it grow has been such a gift.

• Her endurance has continued to improve, and she is feeling stronger. Her speech also continues to improve and the increased tone in her right hand is slowly decreasing.

Some of these may seem like ordinary things for a 19-year-old, but after brain surgeries, radiation, rehabilitation, and everything else she has been through, ordinary feels pretty extraordinary to us.

What’s Next for DCVax?

We will return to London again during the first week of November for Braelyn’s next booster, and then again in March 2027.

Beginning in July 2027, she is expected to transition to maintenance DCVax treatments approximately every six months for at least the next couple of years—or longer if her medical team believes continuing treatment is beneficial.

One remarkable blessing from the enormous tumor we once viewed only as an enemy is that there was enough tumor tissue to manufacture approximately eight years’ worth of personalized vaccine doses.

There is something almost poetic about that.

Something that caused so much devastation is now being used to teach Braelyn’s own immune system what her cancer looks like and help it recognize and attack those cells.

The Journey Continues

Although we have reached some incredible milestones, this treatment journey is far from over. Each additional DCVax dose, medical appointment, and trip to London brings substantial out-of-pocket expenses that are not covered by our insurance.

We remain profoundly grateful to everyone who has donated, shared Braelyn’s story, prayed for her, and helped us continue accessing this treatment. You helped get her here.

Every donation and every share helps us continue funding the booster and maintenance phases ahead.

There is always light

Recently, a friend I met through X reminded me that there is always light, even in the darkest places.

I keep thinking about those words.

Cancer has introduced us to some incredibly dark places over the past three years. But it has also introduced us to extraordinary people.

Many whom we never would have met otherwise.

People who have shared our story, opened doors, offered knowledge, prayed for our daughter, donated toward her treatment, encouraged us when we were exhausted, and sometimes simply reminded us to keep going.

We have been so blessed by the light of others.

And one of my greatest hopes is that through everything we have learned and experienced, we can be that light for someone else who finds themselves walking through a dark place.

For now, we celebrate:

Four DCVax treatments completed.
College underway.
Hair growing back.
Strength returning.
Speech improving.
And an MRI showing no evidence of disease recurrence.

There is still a long road ahead, and we will continue taking it one step, one vaccine, one scan, and one trip to London at a time.

But today, we are incredibly grateful for how far she has come.

Please continue praying for a strong and lasting immune response, continued neurological healing, success with college, and—most of all—that future scans continue to show no evidence of recurrence.

Thank you for continuing to walk beside us, support us, and shine your light on our family.

We hope we can continue to pass that light on. ❤️

With love and gratitude

Mandy Hollensbe
(Braelyn’s proud mama)

🎯Here is my Program Fit Analysis on him for Monmouth University

Kwalei Carter @Kwaleiii  is a ready-made Star/nickel for a Monmouth defense that already treats that hybrid as a structural piece, not a sub-package afterthought. 

His five-game Iowa Western line, ball production without a score allowed, plus a bounce-back path from VUU matches the turnover-and-toughness identity Coach Gallo’s staff is carrying forward. With years of eligibility and a full-qualifier academic profile, he is a multi-year secondary investment, not a one-season patch. He enrolled at Virginia Union in 2025, entered the portal that December, and re-established production at the No. 1 JUCO program. 

Program Overview
Monmouth opened in the Stats Perform preseason top 25 and sit 4-2, 3-0 in league play after losses at Tennessee Tech and Western Michigan and wins over Sacred Heart and Albany. 

Scheme identity is multiple and rotational. In 2025 the unit forced 17 turnovers (second in the CAA) and 12 fumble recoveries (4thin FCS). Coach @_CoachVega  hired from Mercer to coach safeties, comes off a secondary that produced an FCS-best interception total in 2024 and back-to-back SoCon titles.

Prospect’s Fit & Immediate Impact
Primary alignment is Star. Secondary is boundary or field corner in base, with safety snaps in dime when Monmouth wants a fifth defensive back who can tackle. Carter’s listed skill set is the job description Vega has filled with hybrids rather than pure corners.

Iowa Western tape and the box score show him triggering downhill (15 of 19 tackles solo) and affecting the catch point (six to nine breakups, zero scores allowed). That profile wins early nickel snaps against CAA slots and H-backs before he is asked to play press-man outside against 6-3 receivers. 

Scheme Alignment Breakdown
Monmouth’s Star is not a static nickel. Rules change by front: apex against two-back, slot matchup in empty, and occasional overhang against gap runs. Carter’s film traits map cleanly!

Against spread and stack, his catch-point volume is the trait that matters. Six official breakups and a self-reported nine in five JUCO games, with no touchdown allowed, indicate a corner who finds the ball rather than only contesting at the line. Vega’s Mercer secondaries were built on that exact habit takeaways, not just coverage completions. In quarters or match-3 looks that Monmouth can spin out of a multiple front, Carter’s high-IQ tag (his own spring cut and the bounce-back year) fits a Star who has to sort slot-vertical versus out-break without a linebacker over him.

Against power and gap, the solo-tackle rate is the counter. CAA opponents still run tight zone and counter; Gallo’s own offensive background is downhill zone and gap with constraint sweeps. A 190-pound Star who arrives at the ball (1 TFL already, Week 1 production in a 71-0 environment and production in the Coffeyville and Garden City games) gives the defense a force player on the slot side when the edge is occupied. He is not a 210-pound overhang, so the fit is better as a collision nickel than as a primary edge-setter. 

Press-man versus off-man: at 5-10 he is a better off or bail Star than a boundary press corner.  Carter’s value is the inside leverage, the re-route of a slot, and the drive on in-breakers, the snaps CAA offenses actually hunt. His Virginia Union camp cut as an 18-year-old and the Iowa Western mid-season reel both show him playing multiple spots in the same series.

Ball production in tough competition is the separator from a generic JUCO corner. Iowa Western’s 2026 slate includes Coffeyville, Hutchinson, Dodge City, and Garden City programs that put NFL and FBS bodies on the field. 

Culture & ROI Projection
Monmouth’s public standard is connection, toughness, and a champions mindset.  He enrolled at a top-15 D2 program, hit the portal, bet on a No. 1 JUCO, and has stacked FBS and FCS offers without a public complaint cycle. A 3.4 full qualifier removes the academic risk that often stalls JUCO defensive backs in the CAA.

No. The hung jury was because his office (after intervening and taking over the case from the original prosecutor) failed to do discovery properly as a normal prosecution would. Victims refusing to testify is common, which is why DAs/prosecutors have strategies (and teams) dedicated to prosecuting sexual abuse and sexual assault cases leveraging discovery to find the evidence they need to convict without relying on victim testimony.  A retrial would give the prosecution time to gather more evidence independent of the victim's testimony which is what they should have done to begin with, but didn't. The prosecution went about this case hinging almost all of the case on the victim's testimony on purpose.

Moreover, Paxton's office could have made motions to provide accommodations for the victim like having the Defendant attend cross examination remotely, have the defendant sit behind a curtain in the back, etc (which they should have done in the first trial but didn't; they deliberately had the pedophile in the room facing the victim while the victim was questioned). 

And most importantly, Paxton's office could have argued “unavailability” (Texas Criminal Procedure Rule 804) for the victim and used the victim’s prior cross-examination in the first trial to satisfy the 6th Amendment confrontation requirement for the defendant in the would-be retrial as Texas Rule 804 specifically allows. But his office notably didn't do that.

But at the end of the day, Paxton's office didn't even need a conviction to offer a harsher plea deal that, at the very least, made the defendant have to register as a sex offender so that he couldn't keep his law license and firearms which is what the judge was expecting. And so now Paxton has got you blaming the victim for not testifying to excuse Paxton's hand in this. That is what's gross.

text:
Benson’s tariff promise is an empty campaign line that collapses under basic constitutional structure. She has told voters she will negotiate “subnational agreements” with Canada so Michigan-Canada goods are “not subject to tariffs,” that the deals will be “legally enforceable,” and that she can “eliminate” the duties and “get around” federal policy if Trump resists. None of that is within a governor’s power.
Tariffs are a federal instrument. Article I, Section 8 assigns Congress the power to regulate foreign commerce and to lay duties and imposts; Article I, Section 10 bars states from imposing import or export duties or entering treaties without congressional consent. Customs duties are collected by federal officers under statutes that delegate authority to the president. A Michigan governor cannot order Customs and Border Protection to waive a tariff, create a state exemption, or nullify an executive tariff action. Calling it a “subnational agreement” does not change the Supremacy Clause.
The examples she has offered do not fill the gap. After the October debate she pointed to New York Governor Kathy Hochul as precedent for a workable carve-out; contemporaneous reporting found no such tariff-exempting agreement. States can sign non-binding memoranda on environment, tourism, or logistics. Those instruments do not override federal customs law or create a parallel trade regime. Benson’s claim that “the law would be on Michigan’s side” if the federal government undercut the deal is an assertion, not a legal mechanism.
The practical result is a promise Michigan voters cannot collect on. Household cost figures she cites ($5,600) describe the effect of federal policy; they do not create state authority to reverse it. Framing the tariffs as a “John James tax” while pledging to erase them by personal negotiation with Canadian officials substitutes rhetoric for an actual lever. The authority she describes does not exist.

text:
Syria 🇸🇾 is considering sending up to 20,000 troops to Yemen to fight the Houthis 🇾🇪.

The proposal was reportedly discussed during a high-level meeting in Riyadh between Syria’s transitional president, Ahmed al-Sharaa, and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

The plan would reportedly involve mobilizing two regular Syrian army divisions, including the 90th and 84th, to support the counteroffensive by the Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

Their role could range from offensive operations inside Yemen to helping defend Saudi territory along the border.

Damascus has denied the reports, but discussions are reportedly underway.

As I previously reported, Turkish and Pakistani troops are also involved in a broader support arrangement that goes beyond logistics and equipment. Syrian forces have reportedly been offered a similar arrangement if Damascus is reluctant to take on an official military role.

And, as always in geopolitics, nothing comes without a price.

Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 has already been providing substantial financial support to Syria for months as it backs Ahmed al-Sharaa’s new government. Damascus showing a willingness to send troops to Yemen could therefore be seen as a strategic signal one that could lead to significantly greater Saudi financial transfers and investment inside Syria.

As I wrote a few days ago, the region may be moving toward a much larger conflict, with the current fighting in Yemen potentially being only the beginning.

A multinational force entering the war could push Iran into deeper involvement in defending its Yemeni allies. To prepare for that possibility, the Pentagon has reportedly finalized plans for a potential resumption of large-scale strikes against Iran.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) has been instructed to keep its combat options fully prepared, with the final decision resting with President Donald Trump.

The Pentagon is also accelerating the deployment of a third carrier strike group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, which is expected to join the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington in the region before the end of November.

More than 50,000 US troops and around a dozen warships remain at a high level of readiness.

If Trump authorizes the strikes, the campaign could involve extensive attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and refineries.

But I’m still not convinced that an attack will actually happen.

To me, this looks just as much like an attempt to pressure Iran into holding back from sending massive support to the Houthis as it does preparation for a real war.

The Saudi offensive is only getting started, and Riyadh is already facing an aggressive Houthi force that is fighting back hard and making gains on the ground, despite the massive military pressure being brought against it.

Sources: AXIOS   REUTERS

text:
🎼A Musicians' Testimony 

Bakhmut Meat Grinder.
____

That's what's written on our medals.

Four years ago, on that day, our command made the decision to conduct this "meat grinder."

So, it was necessary then...

...October 8, 2022, was my first day of war.

There were 58 more after that...

...After training camp, I arrived in Popasna with a huge backpack full of army gear, which was issued in several stages.
It was October 6th.

On the 7th, in the evening, we received orders to assemble for "the front."

Our replenishment house housed more than ten people, many of whom had been there for 19 days.
We six moved in yesterday.

That day, I was sent "to the front" from that house.
One person was selected from each of the five houses.

Sergeant Deleets, while loading us into the back of a UAZ van, offered to stay, get a warm vest that hadn't been issued to me yet, and they would bring it in a couple of days.

He said:
"Stay, I'll send someone else."

It wasn't comfortable to go into the unknown "front" from a warm village house, but it was embarrassing to return to it after saying goodbye to the guys.

I replied, "I'll go without a vest."

By the way, I left all the gear in Popasna and continued on with a small backpack.
I never needed it later...

...We were five in the back of the van with canisters of gasoline (drones weren't flying like they are now).
We were silent, looking around.
I didn't know any of the other four people.

...We arrived in the village of Pokrovka.
It was already dark.
The car stopped near one of the houses.
Two people met us.
I didn't know who they were then.
Now I know they were the platoon commander and the sergeant.

The commander:
"How many magazines do you have?"

"Four."

To the sergeant:
"Give them two more each."

And he left.
That was our introduction...

...We went into the house.

Dim light from a small lamp, weapons in the corners, people in uniform on the floor and on the sofas.
A frying pan with fried potatoes on the table, a few spoons in it.
A three-liter jar of compote, a jar of pickles, and boxes of ration packs on the floor.

No one paid attention to us.

We stood in a tight group in the middle of the room, looking around.

Someone:
"Make yourselves comfortable!"

"Where?"

"Wherever you want."

We started taking off our backpacks, removing our weapons, and looking for places to sleep.

"Where are we? What's going to happen next?"

Benuar placed a box of new RGD grenades in the middle of the room:
"Take two each."

We inserted the fuses, put them in the pockets of our vests, and waited for something else.

But that was it.
Now you're just like them, with six magazines and two grenades in the pockets of your vest.
And no one will explain anything to you anymore.
You should have listened to the instructors and asked all the questions earlier.

The guys settled around Grozovoy like chicks.
He was the only one who started talking; the others went to sleep.

In short, his story boiled down to this:
"You'll find out everything yourselves tomorrow."

Byn started a long story about what motivated him to go to war.

No one really listened to him. Later, someone from the veterans, lying on a bed, said:
"No one cares about that here.
Let's see how you fight, then we'll talk..."

...I lay in a separate, small, dark room with a bed that was wet from the rain leaking through a hole in the roof, and I barely slept until morning.
I hadn't yet learned how to fall asleep immediately, as soon as possible, like soldiers do.

I was thinking, worrying, planning...

...At 5:00 AM on October 8th, a thin beep from my wristwatch alarm.

It was as if no one had slept at all.
Breakfast, coffee, the toilet.
Weapons, equipment, backpacks.

At exactly 6:00 AM, we lined up outside.
There were about twelve of us.
Five of us were new recruits, and the rest were veterans from different positions, mostly artillerymen.

We reported by radio and then walked in a chain, one after the other, towards the war...
