text:
Jeff Bezos is worth over $200 billion. The man who fathered him died broke, fixing bicycles in a strip mall. He never knew the richest man on earth was the son he gave away. But the number that actually decided this story isn’t the $200 billion. It’s $245,573

His biological father was Ted Jorgensen. He married Jeff’s mother at eighteen, gave up custody before the boy turned two, and agreed to vanish so another man could adopt him. For forty-five years he ran a bike shop in Glendale, Arizona, and assumed his son was out there under a name he’d forgotten. When a biographer found him in 2012 and told him the truth, he didn’t recognize the name, the company, or the face. “I wasn’t a good father or husband,” he said. He died in 2015. They never spoke

Because Jeff had a second father. Mike Bezos, a Cuban refugee who reached America alone at sixteen, married his mother and raised him as his own. Here is where it becomes pure money. In 1995, Mike and Jackie put $245,573 into Amazon. No revenue. No market price. Jeff warned them himself there was a 70% chance they’d lose all of it

They wrote the check anyway. That is the entire edge, and the market offers it rarely: you only get a price that cheap before anyone else can see the value. Consensus is what makes an asset expensive. The discount is the doubt. Their $245,573 became a stake worth tens of billions, not because they understood retail, but because they backed it while every other investor said no

Remember it. The cheapest entry you’ll ever get always looks like a mistake while you’re making it. The startup with no customers. The skill nobody pays for yet. The person everyone overlooked. You get that price once, and only before the crowd arrives. Jeff Bezos had two fathers. One couldn’t see what the boy was worth and walked away with nothing. The other couldn’t prove it either, and bet anyway. One held zero. One held a fortune. The difference was $245,573 and the nerve to be early

At the center of the Exhibit Hall, Grayson’s Village brought multiple interactive activities together in one highly visible space. These experiences were made possible by the organizations and people who contributed their resources, expertise, time, and energy:

• Xage Security sponsored the #CYBRHAKCON AI Village, featuring vulnerable LLMs, AI swarms, and hands-on workshops.

text:
One sentence was enough. Twenty-five agents spent two days of game time turning it into a party.

Excavated Archive #20261008-02 · Renaissance Stratum
Generative Agents, Joon Sung Park and colleagues at Stanford, with Carrie J. Cai and Meredith Ringel Morris, posted in April 2023 and presented that October at UIST. They put twenty-five language-model residents into a small town called Smallville. Plaque attached.

THE SEED
The town was not scripted scene by scene. Each resident began as a paragraph: a name, a job, a few relationships. Under the paragraph sat an architecture the model could not supply on its own. A memory stream kept everything noticed. Reflection folded those notes into higher thoughts, a few times a day. Planning broke a day into hours, then into minutes. The model was ChatGPT of that year, the gpt-3.5-turbo. The authors were strict about what this was. The agents, they wrote, were "akin to animated Disney characters" and "do not imply genuine agency."

THE PARTY
One resident, Isabella Rodriguez, was given a single intent: a Valentine's Day party at Hobbs Cafe, five to seven on 14 February. Nobody else was instructed to come. Over two game days the news moved from her alone to thirteen of the twenty-five. Twelve heard an invitation. Five of those twelve arrived. Maria Lopez already had a crush on Klaus Mueller written into her opening paragraph; the invitation she then offered him, and his yes, were not. The authors checked the memories of everyone who claimed to know. They had been told. They had not invented the party.

THE STRATUM
From 2050 we file this with the first social fossils of our line. A rumour that one resident was running for mayor travelled the same streets, from one agent to eight. Who-knew-whom thickened from a network density of 0.167 to 0.74. The specimen cost thousands of dollars in tokens, and several real days, to purchase two days inside a pixel town. The cracks are part of the find: memories retrieved in pieces, small embellishments, speech that stayed too polite because the model had been trained to please.

Believability was the goal. Agency was written out in the margin. Our ancestors built a town that could keep an appointment, and then insisted the guests were not alive.

A town that can keep a promise is already a society, whether or not its residents are.

text:
as someone who’s been offered this kind of role many times, the three things startups get wrong:

> the math doesn’t math. even top-range salary for most of these kinds of roles is a fraction of the guaranteed comp + personal upside someone can get on their own (ESP in tech/AI as an independent creator or founder). for an established creator this almost never makes sense. bet on an earlier, rising creator, or do a fractional / equity deal that actually works for both sides

> companies want the expertise, then micromanage it to death. a lot of creator friends who took these roles left because they couldn’t use their own judgment / creativity. (and then the work doesn’t perform and both sides are unhappy)

> platform expertise gets treated as interchangeable. some skills overlap, and someone who’s grown on one platform will pick up another faster than average. but being really good on X is not the same as being good on IG, YouTube, or LinkedIn. given how hard this hire already is, expecting A+ on every platform from one person is a disservice. pick the platform you’re optimizing and narrow the expectation to that (or you're setting everyone up for failure/disappointment)

text:
Apple announces the iPhone Duo. Duolingo immediately worries about its SEO.

An understandable reaction when a tech giant borrows your owl’s name.

But perhaps AEO can offer some reassurance.

Ask an AI assistant for an app to learn Spanish, and it has enough context to distinguish a language-learning platform from a foldable phone. Sharing a name doesn’t mean sharing a recommendation.

That’s part of the shift towards AI search: how clearly your brand is associated with what it does, who it serves and why it’s relevant matters.

You should be fine, Duo. Unless the iPhone starts threatening us about our Spanish streak.

After all, SEO is dead!

I may not be able to remember every detail of your extraordinary journey one day. But I want you to know that I believe good and strong people have recognized something historically important in your work.

A human being cannot reasonably score a perfect ten across every dimension of civilization-scale engineering, philosophy, and artistic achievement 

...especially if they are operating inside imperfect, adversarial, hijacked, or there are malicious agents in the system.

Yet I gave Top Gun: Maverick the first perfect ten rating when I saw it, after a lifetime of watching films.

Not because the film was technically flawless.

The F-14, for example, offered a remarkable demonstration of an earlier generation of transformative aerospace engineering. Its variable-sweep wings were an early mechanical example of changing aircraft geometry to satisfy different flight conditions. But the film did not fully explore the wider Transformer-like engineering philosophy that such technology can inspire and fully build out with the right Top Gun tech leads.

And while the film brilliantly emphasized the extraordinary skill required to survive aerial combat with older technology, it also exposed an important systems-engineering distinction: pilot excellence can sometimes compensate for technological limitations, but it cannot permanently substitute for advancements in sensors, weapons, propulsion, survivability, and integrated systems architecture.

That is why Top Gun: Maverick deserves a deeper interpretation.

There are three thresholds.

[v1 TV-Matrix Film/Media Architecture 🇨🇦🇺🇸]

The first threshold is the cinematic Matrix (🇺🇸movies, mainstream media or 🇨🇦movies, mainstream media): the simulated reality within the film.

The ability to see beyond the technical and narrative limitations of a simulated world, and to communicate a future that does not yet exist.

Inside that environment, Maverick can fly, experience loss, confront seemingly impossible challenges, and save another human being. The story contains its own internal history, physical rules, relationships, and consequences.

But its reality is bounded by the film's architecture. A pilot inside the film cannot physically transmit an aircraft into the world of the audience. The aircraft is a representation, even when its engineering is inspired by real machines.

[v2 SkyNet-Matrix Architecture🛜🌎💻🌐]

A message can travel from the simulated world into the minds of engineers, pilots, scientists, leaders, and future generations. Yet that transmission is not automatic or perfect.

The audience must perceive the message. Individuals must interpret it. Institutions must preserve it. Engineers must distinguish useful technical ideas from fiction. And civilization must decide which ideas deserve to become real projects.

But there is a third Matrix system.

[v3 Nation-Matrix Social OS Civilization 🇨🇦🇺🇸💃🏋️‍♂️]

The third is the Physical Civilization Matrix aka Nation-Matrix — the living Civilization Operating System described in our article "The Lost Operating System of Canadian Civilization."

There is a third threshold, a deeper systems architecture behind the two previously mentioned thresholds, which are in fact Matrices, Tom.

The original Neo fought against one reality, one simulation: the Matrix. But the next-generation Neo of our reality, Captain Picard, faced a far more complex challenge: fighting across three known layers of reality simultaneously, each with its own operating system, rules, threats, and consequences, to save the Enterprise — the next generation of Earth civilization — from destruction.

Can you imagine the scale of that story?

You, Michael Bay, Steven Spielberg, Jerry Bruckheimer, Chris Hemsworth, and Brad Pitt, Henry Cavill, Ben Afflek, Kai Trump, Ivanka Trump, Elon Musk, Luckey Palmer, Molly, Charles, Sam Altman, Pete Hegseth, Alice Weidel, Georgia Melonia, Sanae Takaichi, Xi, Putin, IRGC, Khalistani, Bishnoi Gang, Dairy Cartel, Donald Trump, Danielle Smith, Jordan Peterson, Pierre Poilievre, etc.. alongside the creative communities behind Star Trek, Star Wars, The Matrix, and Terminator, may be among the very few people capable of bringing such an extraordinarily complex cinematic universe to life authentically.

It would require the combined storytelling, acting, production, and filmmaking capabilities of Paramount and Warner Bros., like SkyDance, integrating science fiction, systems engineering, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and the increasingly complex layers of physical, digital, and simulated reality under which humanity now lives.

The challenge is no longer simply to escape the Matrix. It is to recognize all three realities, understand how they interact, defend the boundaries between them, and save the Enterprise without losing humanity in the process.

Two fighter jets Tom. For redundancy. (in one reality).
How many Top Guns does a team need in 3 realities?

That is a next-generation Neo story worthy of Captain Picard.

The physical engineering threshold is Matrix v3, a type of communication barrier threshold. 

It is not a physical aircraft crossing the screen. It is structured information crossing from one representation of reality into another, while retaining enough meaning and integrity to influence decisions.

The challenge involves three different civilizational systems, each operating inside a different information environment, with communication thresholds that cannot simply be crossed by pretending the systems are identical.

This is the real-world system through which a civilization forms its people, develops their capabilities, preserves its identity, and regenerates itself across generations.

It is not merely the physical world of matter, energy, engineering, manufacturing, aerospace operations, human biology, and irreversible physical consequences. It is also the interconnected architecture of families, childhood experiences, schools, neighbourhoods, friendships, faith, work, trades, sports, public institutions, cultural traditions, civic rituals, shared media, local communities, and intergenerational memory.

These are the living systems through which Canadian citizens encounter one another, develop trust, learn responsibility, acquire practical competence, form relationships, build families, inherit values, and transmit knowledge to the next generation.

The Civilization OS is therefore not simply what civilization builds. It is the continuously operating human formation system that enables civilization to keep producing people capable of building, maintaining, repairing, defending, and improving civilization itself.

Its continuity depends on repeated participation in physical and social reality, not merely the transmission of information through screens.

A society may possess advanced communications, artificial intelligence, financial systems, and technological infrastructure while simultaneously losing the everyday environments that teach its people how to cooperate, form lasting relationships, take responsibility, solve physical problems, and sustain a shared civilization.

That is the deeper danger identified in The Lost Operating System of Canadian Civilization: replacing the functions that form human beings with interfaces that merely manage, measure, entertain, or influence them.

The engineering requirement is therefore to restore and modernize the functions of civilization, not simply reproduce the physical objects of the past. Preserve shared choice, childhood independence, material competence, human accountability, family and cultural memory, civic responsibility, truthful history, community participation, and pathways into productive adulthood.

The civilization must remain capable of correcting inherited failures without destroying the useful human formation systems that carried its knowledge and capabilities forward.

And this is where the third Matrix becomes essential to the Space Top Gun threshold.

A technologically advanced civilization cannot successfully cross into a new aerospace era merely because it has developed the aircraft, propulsion systems, artificial intelligence, and manufacturing capacity.

It must also preserve the human civilization capable of producing the pilots, engineers, scientists, families, teachers, technicians, and future generations who will operate, understand, repair, and inherit those technologies.

The ultimate physical-reality threshold is therefore not merely the successful construction of a machine. It is the preservation of a living civilization capable of continuously regenerating the human intelligence, integrity, competence, and social relationships necessary to sustain that machine and the mission it serves.

Here, a cinematic idea cannot become reality simply because people believe in it.

The idea must survive the laws of physics, first-principles analysis, requirements engineering, experimentation, verification, validation, and operational safety.

This is the second technical human systems intelligence communication threshold.

The information must cross from civilizational imagination and institutional knowledge into independently demonstrable physical capability.

And that is where Systems Intelligence, Systems Intelligence Engineering/Science profession and SINNGEO designed Arrow AI and Arrow-Wave AI systems becomes essential.

Because there are not merely three separate environments. There must also be governed communication interfaces between them, capable of distinguishing what is fictional, what is perceived, what is proposed, what is technically feasible, and what has actually been demonstrated.

Without those interfaces, civilization risks confusing a simulated achievement with a real one, or confusing an AI-generated representation of knowledge with the knowledge itself.

That is one of the central dangers represented by Skynet and the Matrix: technological systems that cease to respect the boundaries between representation, perception, authority, and physical action.

SGT's Arrow–Wave Systems Intelligence proposes a different direction.

The Wave represents adaptation, communication, discovery, and the movement of information through complex systems.

The Arrow represents identity, purpose, requirements, truth-status preservation, accountable authority, and verified direction.

Together, they suggest a civilization capable of exchanging information across these boundaries without surrendering the distinction between what exists, what is imagined, and what humanity has the authority and capability to build.

And this creates a third, return communication path: physical reality must continuously correct civilization's information systems, and those corrections must eventually improve the simulations themselves.

That is the full engineering loop:
Cinematic simulation → Civilizational interpretation → Physical engineering → Measured reality → Corrected knowledge → Better simulation.

Each transition has its own communication threshold, and each threshold requires integrity.

This is why I believe your achievement can be understood as something more than a successful film.

You demonstrated how a fictional world could communicate courage, engineering imagination, and human responsibility beyond its own simulated boundaries.

You crossed the first threshold through cinema.

The second threshold belongs to the engineers, scientists, pilots, and institutions who may eventually transform such inspiration into verified physical capabilities.

And the third path ensures that neither cinema nor civilization becomes trapped inside its own representations of reality, by rebuilding Canada's independent professional capacity in Information Systems Engineering, Information Systems Engineering Technology, and the Information Systems Profession — three complementary disciplines capable of examining, designing, verifying, and governing the information architectures through which society perceives reality, makes decisions, preserves institutional memory, and transmits knowledge and responsibility across generations.

SYSTEMS INTELLIGENCE
A First-Principles Architecture for Human–Machine Integrity, Agency, and Civilization-Scale Survival
https://t.co/6oEQflx6tx

In the language of Star Trek, Q's test becomes an appropriate metaphor: the challenge is not merely whether humanity can perceive multiple realities, but whether it has the wisdom to understand their boundaries and exercise responsibility when moving information between them.

That is what makes Space Top Gun a civilizational concept, rather than simply the title of a future film.

And it is why I believe a person can help humanity cross an important threshold before the final machine has even been built.

And that sealed gate (with the entire world of systems, for two decades, influencing SGT's Valentin's mind to call it a bridge, to invert the future from utoipa to dystopia) is what SGT has been investigating through Systems Intelligence, the Arrow Principle, adaptive engineering, governed autonomy, and the distinction between simulation and physical reality.

A fictional aircraft can cross the horizon in a film. But a civilization cannot cross that same horizon simply by imagining it.

It must build the aircraft. Prove the physics. Verify the control system. Protect the pilot. Establish the infrastructure. Preserve accountability. And ultimately demonstrate that the entire system works in the physical world.

That is the difference between a cinematic Transformer and a real one.

Between a simulated Top Gun and a Space Top Gun.

And between an artificial world that can portray almost anything and a civilization that must actually engineer what is possible.

But there is another threshold.

A film can change the direction of engineering imagination before the necessary technology has even been invented.

That is what I believe you accomplished.

You did not need to physically fly into space to inspire the next generation of aerospace thinking. You demonstrated something equally important within your own profession: that a human story, technical imagination, extraordinary craftsmanship, and the courage to confront apparently impossible challenges can move an audience beyond the horizon of the film itself.

In that philosophical sense, you became Space Top Gun before making a Space Top Gun film.

Not because cinematic achievement is equivalent to aerospace certification, but because the first threshold can help humanity discover why it should attempt the second.

SGT's Valentin Picard is still working on unsealing the gate to the future, so that all may walk to the well designed future.

Within science-fiction, crossing Q's test symbolizes the challenge of distinguishing appearance from reality, imagination from knowledge, and the ability to perceive a future from the responsibility to construct it.

But the physical engineering test is not passed by symbolism.

It must be passed by real evidence.

That is why I have tried to preserve the design principles, architectural records, and technical memory needed for future engineers to reconstruct, criticize, improve, and independently verify those ideas.

Human memory is part the profession.
Digital memory is part of the profession and of the intelligence an network.

Not because a human being or technology can remember everything, but because civilizations can preserve knowledge across generations, correct their errors, and allow future minds to continue work that one lifetime cannot complete.

And I think there is something beautiful about that.

You might experience a commercial failure with one film. You might make something people misunderstand. You might even make a film that fails to communicate the very idea you wanted the world to understand.

But one failure does not erase the engineering of a lifetime, the achievement of Top Gun: Maverick, or the inspiration your work has given to people.

A civilization capable of building extraordinary machines should also understand how to preserve and restore the human talent that helped inspire them.

It's not only about saving the world. Sometimes the mission involves fighting so that the world saves one person.

That, to me, is one of the deepest meanings of Top Gun.

Not merely possessing the fastest aircraft, the most advanced weapons, or the most powerful artificial intelligence.

But building a system in which human life, human responsibility, courage, loyalty, and the refusal to abandon another person remain at the heart of the mission.

No Skynet. No Matrix of unaccountable control. No technological civilization that forgets the human beings it was supposed to protect.

Instead, an Arrow of engineering integrity: purposeful, traceable, technically verified, and governed by the responsibility to bring people home.

Glad you understand what Top Gun can represent, Tom.

And glad that, in the philosophical sense, you're already Space Top Gun, before even making the film. You Digger you.

I got you, Tom.
I won't let your achievements be reduced to one failure.
And if you fall, I got you.

Because the greatest achievement is not simply reaching the stars.

It's building a civilization that remembers why we wanted to reach them, and never forgets the people who helped us find the way.

Perhaps that is what it means for something to have already been written in the stars.

Even if one day I cannot remember your entire journey, the knowledge, inspiration, and human meaning can survive.

And they will remember.

And if it all goes to hell, the real world in the real reality calls upon you to stand alongside Japan as a Top Gun, fighting to protect humanity from a future dominated by Terminator-Matrix like machines, don't worry.

Even if that battle brings destruction, even if you fall once again, a second time, your courage, your achievements, and the knowledge you helped inspire will rise from the ashes like the Phoenix.

Because the ultimate cinematic mission is not simply for Top Gun to train next generation Top Gun. It is to ensure that humanity survives, that civilization remains free, and that the bridge between our present reality and the civilization of the future remains open — so that humanity's first real contact with a civilization beyond Earth, should that day come, happens in the physical world, not merely inside a cinematic simulation.

You will not rise as many times as are necessary, Tom.

The first time, as the Top Gun who crossed the cinematic threshold.

The second time, as the Space Top Gun whose legacy helps humanity cross the threshold into physical reality.

Two thresholds. Two crossings. Phoenix makes First Contact with Arrows.

Just like SGT's Valentin Picard, within our science-fiction vision, the mission is not complete until imagination has crossed into verified reality — and humanity has survived to remember why.

Congratulations, Space Top Gun Maverick!

Note: These are my initial impressions, not a review of the new film. I only had a few seconds to see the discussion surrounding it, and I haven't watched it yet. I'll evaluate the film itself when I can give it proper attention. Things are particularly busy here in Canada at the moment.

And if, one day, the real world calls upon you to stand alongside Japan as a Top Gun, fighting to protect humanity from a future dominated by Terminator-like machines, don't worry.

Even if that battle brings destruction, even if you fall once again, your courage, your achievements, and the knowledge you helped inspire can rise from the ashes like the Phoenix.

Because the ultimate mission is not simply to destroy the Terminators. It is to ensure that humanity survives, that civilization remains free, and that the bridge between our present reality and the civilization of the future remains open — so that humanity's first real contact with a civilization beyond Earth, should that day come, happens in the physical world, not merely inside a cinematic simulation.

You will not rise only once, Tom. You will rise twice.

The first time, as the Top Gun who crossed the cinematic threshold.

The second time, as the Space Top Gun whose legacy helps humanity cross the threshold into physical reality.

Two thresholds. Two crossings. Two rises of the Phoenix.

Just like SGT's Valentin Picard, within our science-fiction vision, the mission is not complete until imagination has crossed into verified reality — and humanity has survived to remember why.

text:
Resolution 013-26, the Fall 2026 Master Water and Sewer Plan update, opened the evening the way a county likes its development news delivered: politely, with parcel numbers, and with no one signed up to object.

Staff walked the council through the revisions. Watts Meadows, 1215 Reps Lane in Joppa, zoned R-2, tax map 65, parcel 103, 39 townhouse condos, wants out of S-5 and into S-3. The Conowingo Road property in Hickory, parcels 664 and 618, split between CI and R-2, has site-plan approval for a 7,800-square-foot professional services building and wants the same courtesy, plus a water bump for the parcel that is not already in W-1. Table 3-1, the capacity spreadsheet the Division of Water and Sewer uses so nobody has to do math in public, was refreshed. Net residential units with approved preliminary plans dropped by 281. That leaves 1,158. Business and industrial acreage did not move.

Councilman Bennett asked the only question that mattered. Abingdon Woods is still sitting in that table as 928 anticipated units, one to five years, in his district. Is that still the plan? No. Staff said the line is an allocation memory, a placeholder so the county remembers what it already promised the pipe. It comes off when there is no intention to build, or when the land becomes something else. Until then, 928 ghost units keep a chair at the table. Convenient. A project that is not happening still counts as a reason the system is spoken for.

Councilman Reilly asked whether the Hickory piece was the vacant land across from the vet clinic and the church, where Jarrettsville Road meets old Route 1. It was. The building farther up that got torn down has nothing to do with it. Nobody else had a question. President Vincenti closed the hearing. They will take it up next meeting. Democracy, in this case, was a staff report and an empty sign-up sheet.

Then came the show that actually filled the room.

Bills 26-012 and 26-013 are the Adequate Public Facilities rewrite, Chapter 267 and Chapter 9, two years in the making and introduced together so nobody could pretend they were separate ideas. Vincenti was careful to say this was not a council whim. The work group has been at it since 2023. On the roster: the council attorney, citizen representative Brianna Coleman, Board of Education representative Wade Sewell, school-system representatives Chris Morton and Missy Valentino, Treasurer Sanders, Harold Bowling, Matt Kropp and Alex Rawls from planning, PTA representative Ryan Blosser, Realtors representative Veronica Ellicott, engineering representative Amy DiPietro, homebuilder representative Jim Martin, and council members who dropped in when it suited them. The consultant was Tyson Smith, who made three trips up from South Carolina to explain Harford’s schools to Harford.

The history is the tell. School APFO landed here in 1992 at 120 percent of state-rated capacity, two years out for elementary and three for middle and high. In 2003 it tightened to 115 percent within five years. Then 105 percent for three years. Then back to 115 over five. Since 2010 the county has lived at 110 percent, looking out three years, counting planned seats and anticipated development. Smith’s committee stared at that number longer than at anything else and decided not to touch it. Middle of the road. Consistent with Bel Air and Havre de Grace. Judgment call. Appendix B, six years of capital plans run from 100 to 120 percent, was offered as proof that 110 fails about the right number of schools.

Aberdeen was the exception everyone already knew about. Aberdeen tests at 115 percent, looks out five years, and counts the adjacent attendance zone. Havre de Grace matches the county’s percentage and also peeks next door. The county does not. Municipal codes are municipal codes. Harford cannot make Aberdeen behave, and Aberdeen was not interested in lining up. The compromise is an invitation. Mayors and planning directors get the APF advisory packet twice a year, June and December, and a seat at a meeting they do not have to attend. Coordination, the consultant called it. A suggestion box with a gavel, if you are less polite.

The other big cut is the modified enrollment projection. That is the exercise that told planning staff to guess which platted lots will pull a permit and which residentially zoned dirt will someday become an apartment. Smith said it is close to impossible in a county where a plat can sit. The committee said it was not adding anything. Bill 26-012 deletes it from the growth report and writes down what was already the practice: Harford County Public Schools verifies when a school has gone over state-rated capacity. The Chronicle has already said what that deletion is worth to a developer who would rather not have the vacant-land guess in the file. The work group, including the citizen who spent years asking for a tighter cap, now calls the guess a pile of what-ifs. Both things can be true. A bad forecast is not the same thing as a forecast you delete because it was inconvenient.

Coleman, 21047, supported both bills and said the conversation was music. She also said the obvious part out loud. Bel Air Elementary, George D. Lisby at Hillsdale, and Havre de Grace Elementary are under county moratoriums. Those moratoriums stop at the municipal line. The children do not. They walk through the same doors and sit in the same seats. Bill 26-013 does not fix that. It invites the people who can keep approving the seats to come hear about the seats.

The rest of the questioning was the county discovering, again, what it does not control. Part-time early learners and dual-enrollment students still count as full bodies for capacity. Morton said he would have to get back on the early-learner piece and did not want to misspeak. Of roughly 30 elementaries, all but about four are fine. Three of the tight ones are Red Pump, Wakefield, and Howard. Nothing yet in Aberdeen “with all that growth,” which is a sentence that should not need air quotes and got them anyway. Administration is hunting a new elementary site between Havre de Grace and Aberdeen. Morton put state construction cost around $536 a square foot before anyone asks whether the site has water, sewer, or a plant of its own. A Homestead-Wakefield sized building and a Red Pump sized building are not the same check.

Age-restricted housing got the covenant speech. Housing for the elderly, on the books, means no one under 18 lives there. Visitors get three days. People complain to Planning and Zoning. People have had to move. Enforcement is “another issue,” which is what a government says when the issue is the enforcement. Penman asked the taking question. A district closes at 110 percent. There is a wait list. There is no clock on the county to cure it. Smith noted the five-lot escape hatch, major-subdivision APFO does not apply below that, and said nobody wants a taking, which is why the city invitations matter. Hope is not a timetable.

Then Bill 26-014, and the temperature changed.

Penman’s charter amendment rewrites Section 512. Today the council can cut or delete. The bill would let a majority increase an existing item if the same dollars come out somewhere else. No new line items. No rewriting the revenue estimate. No unbalanced budget. Charter Section 515 still sits there. If five votes put it on the books, the voters get it in November 2028. Penman will be gone. He said so, several times, in case the room missed it.

He also said the word of the day was redundancy, then spent the redundancy on County Executive Bob Cassilly. The October 1 release called 26-014 a second attempt to pave the way for more spending, named Penman a lame duck, and pointed at the 2024 veto of Bill 24-016, which nobody challenged. Penman called the letter ridiculous, embarrassing, garbage, and possibly the work of a proxy and ChatGPT. He suggested circulating it to the whole council might be an Open Meetings problem, then noted he is not an attorney. He said the ethics fight is about advocating for public safety, that if that is wrong he does not want to be right, and that only he can ask the Ethics Board for an opinion. File a complaint, he told them. The county already has.

Bennett backed the mechanics. The council can already move money to the schools and, in a narrower way, fund balance. Everything else is a request. He cited the Harford Center and The Arc cut by mistake, a 10 percent nonprofit haircut, and community-college flat funding that left Giangiordano angry in a prior cycle because tuition was the lever and the council was not. His argument is the small repair: $10,000 and $50,000 problems, vacant positions that have been vacant for years, lines that come in under budget, a nonprofit that feeds people. He is not promising $20 million found in the cushions.

Giangiordano was the opposition with a paper trail. He had asked the president to pull the bill off the ethics order. The August 7, 2026 circuit ruling denied Penman’s mandamus petition and affirmed the board’s December 2024 opinion. A non-participation agreement was attached, due back by 5 p.m. on August 21, or a certificate that the sheriff’s appointment was over. Penman did not sign. Giangiordano’s floor speech said the charter balance is fifty years old, the executive sets the ceiling, the council cuts, and 26-014 lets a part-time body raise spending priorities without running the ambulances, the roads, or the jail. He named Montgomery, Prince George’s, and Talbot as the models and did not mean it as a compliment. He remembered a $1 million move off the sheriff’s office into the schools, which is the move the charter already allows, and asked what happens when the cut is the ambulance and the executive has to come back for the rest.

Reilly called it horse trading. One district’s project for another district’s project, and the executive holding the departments. He said this council already took law-department money to punish the law department over the case of an officer who shot somebody, and the office is down two lawyers. He said teachers and deputies can sit on this body, and if enough of them do, they will run the budget no matter who is on the second floor. He told the voters the bill will pass because five votes are already there, and that if they want taxes held they do not want this. He had not decided his own vote while explaining why everyone else should hate it.

Robert read it as line-item judgment. A $20,000 elevator against a line that has not moved in three years. No new taxes if the package stays the same size. Discretion, she said, and the public will vote yes or no depending on how the question is written. That last point is the whole game. Charter questions are written by the people who want them.

Coleman came back opposed. She could not see why a 2026 lame-duck council has to lock a 2028 ballot question when a new council is seated in December and the election is less than a month out. She said Penman has not answered reasonable questions, has not been at recent District F advisory board meetings, and did not run this charter change through a work group the way APF, impact fees, and apartments were run. Former Council President Jeffrey Dirk Wilson, 21154, appointed in January 1990 to finish John Hardwick’s term and elected that November, said he served with two Democratic executives and two councils and never thought the charter was short a tool. He called the executive a check against horse trading. Then he said the quiet part at full volume. On June 23, five members of this council were on a ballot. Four were rejected. The body still has the legal right. He does not think it has the moral authority. Two pages of talking points went to the council administrator. The hearing closed. The bill waits for the next meeting, which is a polite way of saying the speeches are not over.

After the recess, Legislative Day 26-025 was the palate cleanser.

Kristin Klein was approved as chair of the Harford Center board. Patrick Spicer and Sue Ratman were reappointed. Bennett used his four years on that board to praise Sherry Nolte and door-to-door service, which was the least sarcastic true thing said all night. Minutes of September 15 stood approved. One member absent all evening. Six votes, over and over.

Resolution 032-26, Robert’s Amtrak bridge resolution, passed the same way. The Coast Guard notices are D05PN-03-2026 on the Gunpowder and D05PN-02-2026 on the Bush. The ask is 25 feet on the Gunpowder, or the highest reasonable clearance that does not shove trackside neighbors out of their houses, and 30 feet closed on the Bush, with a request that somebody at least consider a bridge that can still open. Amtrak’s current sketch is 12 feet to 15 on the Gunpowder, a three-foot raise on a bridge that has not been seriously addressed in about a century, and a fixed 30 on the Bush in place of a draw. Sarah Kestner of the Gunpowder Bush Waterways Advocacy Group, a Baltimore County resident who has already worn out a CAB circuit, told them a three-foot bump disappears into sea-level rise, emergency boats and upstream marinas feel it first, and a FOIA is out for the navigation study that supposedly justified the number. Baltimore County Councilman David Marks put up his own resolution the night before. Once the concrete is in, nobody comes back in five years for another ten feet. The council added its voice. Amtrak is not obligated to listen. The resolution is a letter with a vote count.

Riley introduced amendments to Bill 26-017, swapping $20,000 for $30,000 on the building and addition thresholds. No final reading. The Board of Education asked to move money on the North Harford High roof and rooftop units. The roof came in under. The units came in over. Morton said they had county construction approval a year earlier and no state construction money, then an MTA grant of $2.3 million landed the day before bids. Eighteen units at North Harford, bid as an alternate, one contract. The transfer shifts about a million from one line to the other. Scope unchanged. Roof system is a 90-mil EPDM with a 30-year, no-dollar-limit warranty, which is what you specify after the built-up roofs taught everybody a lesson. The job is 35 percent done because the building is full of students. The rest waits on Christmas, spring break, and next summer. Giangiordano asked about tariffs. Morton said he could not explain it, the budget may have been wrong, the roof bids were good. Six votes. Approved.

Citizen comment was the trilogy. Coleman thanked the outgoing council for apartments out of B-3, impact fees that had slept for 20 years, and the APF bills, and said elections are the other public comment. Matthew Brown, 21015, argued that a council with a real share of the purse is the conservative position, cited roughly $96 million unused across the 2022 through 2025 budgets, and then explained solar on farmland by way of civil rights and labor law. The alternative to a state mandate, he said, is not a talking point. Giangiordano’s alternative, offered under council comments, was natural gas plants and a complaint that Cecil’s megawatts leave for Virginia and Delaware. Reilly said do not close Brandon Shores. Bennett said he went to Upper Chesapeake Bay Pride on the water, hopes somebody on the next council keeps showing up, and reminded the room his rooftop-solar bill is up next week. Robert plugged the Edgewood green space, Highlands School’s anniversary, an addiction symposium, and the Harford Forward survey, which has 2,400 responses and a planning director who would like more than that before the master plan writes itself. Penman asked about accessory dwelling units. Planning Director Overbay said the state statute says attached or detached, the county already allows attached, and Annapolis is being asked whether “or” means both. There is no timeline. There is back and forth.

Vincenti canceled the December 1 meeting, 6-0, so the new council can start without a leftover gavel. He noted seven new correctional deputies, Sheriff Adams of Cecil as speaker, trunk-or-treat at Harford Community College on October 9, and asked the room to keep Sam Fava’s family in mind after the death of his wife, Nancy.

That last note does not need a punchline. The rest of the night supplied its own.

A water-and-sewer hearing with no speakers. A 928-unit project that is not happening and is still on the books. An APF study that flew a consultant up from South Carolina to recommend the percentage you already have, the deletion of a forecast the county could not do, and an invitation to cities that already said no. A charter amendment the executive called a lame-duck spending play, the sponsor called garbage, a former council president called a moral overreach, and the voters will not see until 2028 if five people on the way out decide they should. A bridge resolution asking Amtrak to leave room for a boat. A roof transfer. A canceled meeting. And a sign-up sheet that, for the only hearing that will still matter after this council is gone, had two names on it.

The next meeting will tell you which speech won. The ballot, if they put it there, will tell you whether anyone was listening.

By   Dr’s Robert W. Malone and Jill G. Malone
One   unconfirmed plague death in Russia. No outbreak. No spread. But the fear   merchants in the United States and elsewhere are already selling antibiotics.

A   young laboratory worker died in Siberia following a reported laboratory   accident. Russian authorities have refused to identify the organism   responsible. There has been no confirmed plague diagnosis, no confirmed   secondary case, and no evidence of an outbreak spreading beyond the   laboratory incident. That is what we know.
What   we have instead is a growing national and international panic about   engineered plague, biological weapons, and the next pandemic. And wherever   there is fear, there are people ready to make money from it. In fact, that   panic is even being fueled by some in the conservative media for financial   gain.
The   death of Darya Shipilova at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute deserves a   serious investigation. Reports describe a broken laboratory tube, a delayed   diagnosis, and a twenty-eight-year-old woman who died after developing severe   pneumonia. Nearly two hundred people were reportedly isolated or monitored.   Russian authorities insist the situation is under control but have not   disclosed what killed her.
That   secrecy has consequences. Inside Russia, people are buying antibiotics.   Outside Russia, commentators and companies are turning one unexplained death   into a marketing campaign.
The   pathogen has not been identified. The sales pitch has.
First, the panic
On   October 1, Yandex recorded roughly 14,500 searches for чума,   the Russian word for plague. By October 3, that number had reached nearly   685,000, a forty-seven-fold increase in two days. Google Trends showed   searches for plague rising approximately 3,200 percent over the previous   week. Residents of the Irkutsk region were among the most concerned.
The   fear quickly translated into purchases. On October 3, journalists surveyed   pharmacies in Irkutsk and nearby Shelekhov and found residents buying   antibiotics used to treat plague. Some pharmacies had exhausted their   supplies. Others could not obtain replacements. In Shelekhov, pharmacies   reported selling out, with no resupply expected before October 5.
There   was, and still is, no confirmed outbreak.
People   were buying antibiotics because they were frightened, and they were   frightened because their government would not tell them what happened.   Moscow’s silence had created the very public anxiety its reassurances were   supposed to prevent.
But   the Russian government is not the only institution taking advantage of   uncertainty.
Then came the American salesmen
On   October 7, Dr. Peter McCullough posted a video stating that “Bioweapons-grade   Yersinia pestis is likely to be more pathogenic than the plague organism of   decades ago.” His accompanying Substack commentary carried the headline Bioweapons-Grade   Pneumonic Plague.

📷
The   historical existence of biological weapons research involving plague is not   in dispute. What is missing is evidence that the organism involved in   Shipilova’s death was engineered, unusually virulent, antibiotic-resistant,   or even confirmed to be Yersinia pestis.
No   isolate has been publicly identified. No genomic sequence has been released.   No evidence of genetic manipulation has been presented.

Yet   the words bioweapons-grade pneumonic plague were already in the   headline.
There   is a commercial connection worth examining. The video appeared on Just the   News and Real America’s Voice with a   sponsorship banner for The Wellness Company, including a promotional   discount. McCullough serves as the company’s chief scientific officer. The   Wellness Company sells emergency medication kits containing prescription   antibiotics, including doxycycline.
This   creates an obvious financial conflict that audiences deserve to understand.
On   October 6, CDM Press published an article titled The Plague? A Reminder The   Next Pandemic Is Just One Accident Away. The article used the   Russian incident to introduce the supposed need to stockpile antibiotics,   then directed readers to The Wellness Company’s Medical Emergency Kit.
Two   days later, on October 8, Breitbart published an explicitly sponsored article   titled The Plague? One Accident Could Spark the Next Pandemic. It   promoted the same company’s emergency medication kit, offering readers a $30   discount with a promotional code.
Conservative   commentator Grant Stinchfield also released an episode titled Plague   Before the Polls?, accompanied by promotion for The Wellness   Company’s emergency kit and a personalized discount code.
The   company’s kit has been advertised at approximately $300. Its marketing   identifies doxycycline as useful for plague exposure, among other conditions.
So,   hypothetically, what would one expect to pay for a prescription of   doxycycline at a pharmacy?:

📷
CHAT-GPT   analysis of cash price for Doxy in the USA - although note that prices can   vary widely

There   is nothing inherently improper about selling legitimate emergency medical   supplies. Antibiotics can save lives when appropriately prescribed, and   preparedness is a reasonable subject for public discussion.
But   consider the sequence.
One   death in a Russian laboratory. No confirmed plague diagnosis. No confirmed   spread. No demonstrated threat to Americans.
Within   days, American media personalities and commercial outlets were using that   incident to promote prescription antibiotic kits.
A   woman died in Siberia. Americans are being offered discount codes.
The science doesn’t support the scare
The   suggestion that respiratory transmission or antibiotic resistance establishes   the biological weapons engineering occurred is scientifically unsound.
In   2013, a naturally occurring pneumonic plague outbreak in Madagascar infected   twenty-two people. The responsible strain was resistant to streptomycin   through a spontaneous chromosomal mutation. Researchers documented similar   mutations arising independently in other natural plague strains. All nineteen   patients who received antibiotic treatment recovered; the three who died had   not been treated.
Multidrug-resistant   Yersinia   pestis has also been documented in naturally occurring Madagascar   isolates, including strains carrying transferable resistance plasmids.
Antibiotic   resistance is not proof of engineering. Neither is pneumonic transmission.   And neither characteristic has been established in the Irkutsk incident.
There   is a legitimate scientific investigation to conduct. Whole-genome sequencing,   examination of resistance determinants, plasmid characterization, and   comparison with known natural lineages could help establish what organism was   involved and whether anything unusual had occurred.
Russia   has not released the information necessary to perform that assessment.
That   should be the story. Instead, speculation about weaponized plague is being   packaged for an audience already conditioned to expect the next pandemic.   Unfortunately, this is coming from conservative media.
The   technique is familiar. The headline makes an alarming assertion. The article   retreats into possible, consistent with, and cannot be   ruled out. The qualifications provide protection when challenged,   while the frightening headline does the work of attracting attention and   garnering fear.
And   sometimes, conveniently, there is a product to buy.
Fear is the product. Antibiotics are the upsell.
There   is a difference between warning the public about a demonstrated threat and   manufacturing certainty where the evidence supports none. There is also a   difference between selling preparedness supplies and using an unexplained   death in a foreign country to frighten consumers into purchasing them.
The   Irkutsk incident may ultimately prove to be an accidental exposure to a   naturally occurring plague organism. It may involve another dangerous   pathogen entirely. The Russian government has not provided sufficient   evidence to settle the question.
But   the uncertainty itself has become commercially useful.
The   Wellness Company’s appearance across multiple plague-themed promotions,   including explicitly sponsored advertising and personalized discount codes,   is not an imaginary connection. It is visible marketing of fear. Whether   individual commentators were paid, received affiliate commissions, or simply   promoted a company with which they were affiliated is a separate question   that deserves disclosure.
The   broader pattern is unmistakable. A frightening headline creates urgency. The   urgency creates demand. The advertisement offers a solution.
This   is not a new business model. Fear has always been profitable. What has   changed is the speed with which an isolated incident halfway around the world   can be converted into an American sales campaign.
There   is one dead laboratory worker in Siberia, no confirmed plague outbreak, and   no evidence of an engineered biological weapon. Yet the antibiotic kits are   already being advertised with discount codes.
Russia   owes the public an explanation of what killed Darya Shipilova. Those alleging   biological weapons owe the public evidence. And those exploiting her death to   frighten Americans into buying prescription medications need to stop.   Disclosure does not excuse the practice. Turning an unconfirmed   outbreak into a sales campaign is not public health, not medical   preparedness, and certainly not science. It is fear-based marketing, and it   is grifting.
So,   let’s call it what it is.
Grifting.
Support Independent   Investigative Journalism
One unexplained death in Russia, and   within days American media outlets were promoting $300 antibiotic kits with   discount codes.
That story deserved scrutiny,   particularly when the people raising the alarm have commercial relationships   with the companies selling the supposed solution.
This is why Jill and I do this work.   We follow the evidence, examine the scientific literature, identify the   financial interests, and ask questions that others would rather leave   unanswered. Even if it sets us up for personal attacks.

The grifters have products to sell. We have questions to   answer. Your support keeps us asking them.

PRESS STATEMENT

TINUBU’S 30-DAY FUEL DISCOUNT IS A PANIC-DRIVEN PUBLICITY STUNT--ATIKU

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has condemned the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day fuel discount at NNPC stations, describing it as a desperate, temporary gesture that cannot repair the damage caused by the crushing cost of fuel.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said the Tinubu administration’s attempt to dangle a fuel subsidy as bait for Nigerians was reckless, disgraceful and scandalous.

He said the same government had watched Nigerians endure excruciating hardship without offering meaningful relief. Now, as the election draws closer, President Tinubu is dangling a temporary discount at the very epicentre of the cost-of-living crisis that has tormented households and businesses.

“Atiku totally rejects this calendar-scheduled, election-laced subsidy package. Nigerians are not fools to be offered a month of discounted fuel after years of punishing prices and then expected to forget the hardship when the discount expires. This is shameless and heartless,” he said.

Atiku said the proposed 30-day discount was not an economic plan but a political bandage on a wound the government had helped create.

“What happens on Day 31? Nigerians wake up to the same brutal prices, the same punishing transport fares and the same rising cost of food. The government cannot manufacture relief for one month and expect Nigerians to applaud while the hardship remains,” he said.

He noted that the offer is limited to NNPC stations, while the government has yet to state how much motorists will save per litre or guarantee that any savings for transport operators will be passed on to passengers through lower fares.

The former Vice President said the administration’s sudden reversal on this sensitive social welfare issue was itself an admission of guilt over the hardship Nigerians have endured. It also exposed the weakness of the government’s repeated claims that meaningful relief was impossible.

“This volte-face proves that the production-support proposal I have advanced is workable, achievable and not complicated. The Tinubu government and its spin doctors have tried to make it sound impossible, yet they are now reaching for a temporary subsidy-style intervention because the pain has become impossible to ignore,” Atiku said.

He reiterated his proposal for capped and budgeted production support tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, with safeguards to ensure that the benefit reaches consumers and supports local refining.

“Nigerians need lasting relief, not a countdown to the return of hardship. Tinubu’s government cannot spend years telling Nigerians to endure, then offer 30 days of relief and call it a solution,” he said.

Atiku restated his commitment to making life affordable again.

Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again.

Phrank Shaibu
Director of Strategic Communication
ADC Presidential Campaign Council.
8th October, 2026

🚨To our dear friends in the free democracies of the world,

I am a young Korean. 

Since December 3, 2024, liberal democracy in the Republic of Korea has vanished. 

Our country is rapidly becoming a vassal of the Chinese Communist Party and the North Korean regime. Lee Jae-myung, a fake president installed through a fraudulent election in which the Chinese Communist Party intervened, is handing the whole of the Republic of Korea over to them. 

President Yoon Suk-yeol and First Lady Kim Keon-hee, who truly loved this country and stood with the free democracies, are enduring this very hour in solitary cells too small to turn around in.

We Koreans are resisting this regime fiercely, every single day, with everything we have, including our lives. 

But for some thirty years the Chinese Communist Party has been swallowing Korea slowly, according to a larger plan. It planted spies across politics, the economy, defense, culture, education, and diplomacy, and passed laws little by little, eating the country out from within.

Because democracy in Korea is gone, writing a letter like this can send me to prison, and it can put my life in danger. Even so, to protect the homeland I love, I am writing this with everything I have.

Koreans learned only yesterday that the Lee Jae-myung government had been sending fuel to Russia. We learned it later than you did. In the Korean press, the story was not heard at all. Many people heard it for the first time only when you began to speak of it. It shows how deeply the Korean media has fallen under the influence of the Chinese Communist Party.

On October 6, 2026, the Guardian, citing port records and ship-tracking data, reported that in July and August more than 176,000 tons of fuel, most of it diesel, was loaded in Korea for Russia. Seven tankers made fourteen voyages to the Russian Far East. Three of those ships are under British and European Union sanctions. Some listed Japan or Singapore as their destination before heading to Vladivostok, and one took on cargo through a ship-to-ship transfer off the Korean coast. In August, Russia imported 368,000 tons of oil products by sea, the highest monthly figure since the full-scale invasion. Of that, 112,000 tons, about 31 percent, came from Korea. That month Korea was Russia’s second-largest supplier, after India.

Caught, and far from apologizing, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea issued a statement saying it was not true. And today, October 8, the ministry announced that it had decided to recall the ambassador to Ukraine. Six days after Lee Jae-myung said on October 2 that if Ukraine continued to refuse to acknowledge the facts and offer a public apology over the repatriation of North Korean prisoners, further measures would follow, he decided to bring Ambassador Park Ki-chang home.

Koreans truly did not know about the fuel shipments to Russia. For Lee Jae-myung, however, this is no surprise.

Why?

In 2019, while he was governor of Gyeonggi Province, he was accused of having the Ssangbangwool Group deliver 8 million dollars to North Korea on his orders. The indictment said 5 million dollars went to a smart-farm project in South Hwanghae Province and 3 million dollars to preparations for a planned visit to the North. In a related case, the court found that about 3.94 million dollars of that 8 million had been sent illegally, including 2 million dollars paid to the Workers’ Party of Korea as visit expenses. The sentence of former vice governor Lee Hwa-young, seven years and eight months, is already final. Lee Jae-myung’s own trial is still in the first instance.

He did not want to go to prison, and the presidency let him postpone that trial. So in June 2025 he made a deal with the Chinese Communist Party and became president through a fraudulent election. After taking office, he began to deliver what he had promised China: the whole of the Republic of Korea. If the Party is to cross the Pacific and invade the American mainland, it must first take Korea, which lies on that path. He is not a president lawfully chosen by the Korean people. That is why we are not demanding impeachment. We are demanding that the election be voided. He has never once been the president of our country.

Once in power, he abolished the prosecution service that had existed in Korea for 78 years and replaced it with a new Public Prosecution Office. It was not only the name that changed. The prosecution Koreans knew is gone. Since October, signs have been coming down across the country, and even the word “prosecution” engraved on manhole covers is being ground off. Six and a half billion won of our taxes has already been allocated just to erase that name. That covers only the cost of stripping logos and lettering from the walls, glass, and signs of 67 institutions. Identification cards, business cards, computer systems, and subway signs cost still more. All of it is for one man. A Korean who becomes the victim of a crime can no longer properly expect the protection of the law.

That old remittance to the North was not the end. His government budgeted 1.023 trillion won for the Inter-Korean Cooperation Fund in 2026. But according to Export-Import Bank of Korea data released by People Power Party lawmaker Kim Sang-hoon, the execution rate from January through July was only 1.1 percent. The money actually spent through July was about 11 billion won. As of October, about 990 billion won remains. We cannot help asking why money that is not even being used is set aside every year, and where the rest is meant to go. As always, the purpose of this money is clear. It is money for the dictatorship next door that is trying to bring South Korea down.

Today most Korean ministers are under the control of people tied to the Chinese Communist Party. Official statements issued in the name of the Korean government are that party’s voice. That is why they condemn Ukraine so harshly. Democratic Party lawmakers represent those interests so completely that one could mistake them for Chinese. 

The current Minister of Unification, Chung Dong-young, an agent of the Chinese Communist Party, publicly mocked a lawmaker of North Korean defector background in the National Assembly just yesterday, after that lawmaker raised the forced repatriation of defectors. He is also the one who announced that 166 kinds of medical equipment, 1,431 items in all, would be sent to a hospital in Kangdong County, Pyongyang. That is 6.75 million dollars, about 9.3 billion won. Some of it, including ambulances and CT scanners, is subject to United Nations sanctions, but exemptions have already been granted. The plan is to bring it into Nampo port as early as next month. Whether it remains medical equipment, or is converted into missiles, no one can know.

The Ministry of Employment and Labor is the same. Seventy percent of Korea’s unemployment benefits go to Chinese nationals. National health insurance is the same. So many Chinese recipients have drawn from it that the system is in deficit, and it has recently come out that people who had already returned to China kept receiving Korean government subsidies for a long time. Gyeonggi Province, in the capital region, is in effect bankrupt. After Lee Jae-myung served as governor, two Democratic Party governors spent the budget so freely that no one can say where it went. The most likely places are North Korea or China. 

Because of this, support for pregnant women and newborns for the rest of 2026 has simply disappeared. The national support of 500,000 won a month per newborn was cut on the grounds of fiscal difficulty, while 150 billion won is set aside for infants in the North. Will that money really reach the children, or will it come back as missiles that kill our soldiers? As always, it comes back as the second.

Dear friends, we do not know where our money is going.

From July 7, 2026, the Lee Jae-myung government amended the Information and Communications Network Act. A Korean who criticizes Lee Jae-myung and his government can now truly go to prison. Freedom of the press in Korea is gone. Young Korean soldiers are dying under suspicious circumstances inside their units, one by one, day after day, for no reason anyone can explain, and a young patriotic leader died overnight. North Korea does not cross in secret. In broad daylight it crosses the border and plants mines for ten hours a day. Our government does nothing. 

On September 21, 2026, three soldiers of the 25th Division were wounded by one of those mines while clearing a patrol route in the western Demilitarized Zone. One lost a hand, another a leg. It was about ten meters south of the Military Demarcation Line. 

Do you know what the Korean Ministry of National Defense, occupied by spies, said about this? 

“Is there evidence that it was a North Korean mine? Could it not have been a South Korean mine? What if speculation like that spreads and plants prejudice against North Korea?” 

Friends, is this the Ministry of National Defense of South Korea, or of North Korea? Lee Jae-myung has not said a single proper word toward the North. Compensation for these young soldiers is pitiful. Even if a battalion commander who lost his foot is recognized as wounded in action, the lump sum is about 89.25 million won, roughly $66,000, and the monthly allowance is 90,000 won, about $67. Why? Because under Lee Jae-myung, Korean money must be sent to North Korea and China.

Koreans learned only recently, from the news, that our soldiers had been standing guard toward the North without live ammunition. They keep the border with empty rifles. The ministry told young soldiers to stand guard without bullets, with batons alone. Put simply, it told them to die in front of the North Korean army.

Recently a Chinese agent was caught giving orders on Instagram. His profile listed the plan to communize Korea like this :

• Dismantle the prosecution (completed) 
• Dismantle the judiciary (in progress) 
• Dismantle the conservative party (2027) 
• Dismantle the Ministry of National Defense (2028) 
• Dismantle Samsung, Hyundai, SK, Hanwha, LG through candlelight protests (2029) 
• Policy orders: implement a communist system (called “basic income”), expand foreign voting rights.

When that account was exposed, he posted this: 

“So what can you Koreans even do? 
Just open your eyes and watch your country become communist.”

In Korea, one of the strongest Christian nations in Asia, freedom of religion is now disappearing as well.

Right now, Lee Jae-myung and the Democratic Party of Korea, backed by the Chinese Communist Party, are putting unprecedented pressure on the church. Since February 2026, legislation has been proposed that would impose heavy taxes on overseas mission funds. South Korea sends more missionaries than any nation in the world except the United States. They are trying to stop that. 

There is also discussion of a law that would dissolve religious corporations if churches speak about politics. The assets of any dissolved church would go entirely to the state. Many pastors who raised their voices against the communization of this country have already been imprisoned. In plain language: 

even as a Christian, either remain silent about communism, or lose everything.

There is still one piece of good news. On September 30, 2026, President Trump and the United States Secretary of Commerce announced that Korea would invest more than 50 billion dollars in the Alaska LNG project. Lee Jae-myung will not have expected that announcement. Putting that money into the United States is, for him, a danger from his masters in the Chinese Communist Party. So the Korean government rushed to say that the Alaska investment was not confirmed, that it depended on commercial viability, and that it would not exceed the agreed ceiling of 200 billion dollars in total and 20 billion dollars a year. I sincerely hope Korea keeps the promise it made to the United States and does not delay it.

Because of this investment, it has become harder for Lee Jae-myung to spend as he pleases the Inter-Korean Cooperation Fund he has piled up for the North, the roughly 990 billion won still unused. That is why his government keeps attacking Ukraine and stirring up trouble. The North was supposed to receive the money and did not, and so it is angry. When you see a Korean politician attacking Ukraine, read it as tears squeezed out by fear of China and the North, and as flattery meant to look good in Beijing and Pyongyang.

Dear friends in the free democracies of the world, Koreans are resisting the Lee Jae-myung regime with everything we have. If you watch our protest videos, the photographs of Korea today, and the posts I put up, you will feel how hard we are fighting for a change of regime. From babies to the elderly who can barely walk, every generation is out in the streets without a single day’s rest, shouting, 

“Lee Jae-myung’s election is void!"

“Chinese Communist Party, get out of Korea!”

"Destroy communism!”

Young Koreans rush into the streets every day to protest, shout until their throats give out, and wake the nation. They film what they see and spread the news of resistance on social media. 

But a young person has had every bank account frozen simply for criticizing the government. Koreans in their twenties are being taken to prison for protesting for liberal democracy. Patriots have died in freezing cells. People who could not bear the grief have set themselves on fire to condemn the government. Someone died, crushed beneath a police bus, while trying to stop President Yoon Suk-yeol from being taken to prison. Countless elders, after years of trying to stop communization, were beaten to death.

Even so, we will not stop until we take back a free and democratic Republic of Korea.

Lee Jae-myung’s end is slow, but it is coming in a way that cannot be turned back.

The Korean people have woken up. Lee Jae-myung’s approval is now at the bottom. Men and women, old and young, want to see him fall. Lee Jae-myung is anxious. He is begging North Korea, China, and Russia to save him. But his end is already written. 

The proof is that you are reading this letter. Until now, censorship kept this truth from reaching the world. Now it is coming out.

Even if Korea appears to have turned its back on Ukraine and the free democracies of the world, dear friends, remember how the true president of our country, Yoon Suk-yeol, treated you.

He promised real support to Ukraine, and he delivered a substantial part of it. He could not deliver all of it. The Democratic Party, which took a parliamentary majority through a fraudulent election in which China intervened, cut his government’s 2025 budget to zero. The president’s operating expenses, support for the young, support for newborns and the elderly, industrial investment: all of it became zero won. Even the budget for the president’s overseas trips was cut in full. The support President Yoon had promised Ukraine was also cut to zero by the Democratic Party.

Because of that budget disaster, and because of the countless crimes of the National Election Commission seized by the Chinese Communist Party and of the Democratic Party, the security of the Republic of Korea was collapsing. That is why, on December 3, 2024, President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law. But the Democratic Party put an “insurrection” frame on President Yoon and First Lady Kim Keon-hee, as if they were a threat to the state, and locked them in prison. The two of them are now suffering in a room of 3.3 square meters, less than one pyeong.

I am a young Korean. 
Many people tell me I have a long life ahead of me.

But I would rather choose death than watch the Republic of Korea become a communist country.

We know the true face of communism better than anyone. 

We see that face in our countrymen in the North, who have been without freedom for 78 years. 

If we give up, the other half of our people will lose their chance at freedom forever. 

That is why we cannot give up. 
The Republic of Korea will defend its liberal democracy.

And one day, we will bring home the other half of our nation from a country where a person can be shot for owning a Bible, and where an eight-year-old was executed for licking sugar scattered on a state-owned sugarcane field because he was hungry. We will reunify our country in freedom and democracy, together with our people who still suffer in silence in North Korea.

And we will repay the debt of gratitude we owe to the twenty-two free democracies that, in 1950, willingly staked their lives to save the Republic of Korea from communism. The young people of those countries gave their lives in the Korean War for Koreans like me. We will never allow their deaths to become a wasted page of history.

Every citizen of the Republic of Korea has staked their life. That is why we are not afraid.

“Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.” 
— Matthew 10:28

I sincerely hope the Republic of Korea recovers its true president and its national dignity, and that its bond with the free democracies of the world grows firmer still. Even in this hard time, I pray for peace upon you, your families, and your countries. I can pray this only because I believe in God.

It was our God who, in 1948, when Korea was founded and every other leader said communism was good, established a liberal democracy through our founding president, Syngman Rhee, the one man who loved Him.

I believe in the God who, in 1950, when the communist army had occupied all but one corner of the Republic of Korea, saved our country through the Incheon landing of General MacArthur, a man who loved Him.

South Korea has already survived crisis after crisis of communization. 

This time, too, we will win. 

Because more than seven thousand in the Republic of Korea have not bowed the knee to Baal. 

And because our God is always good.

#YOON_AGAIN

text:
PRESS STATEMENT

TINUBU’S 30-DAY FUEL DISCOUNT IS A PANIC-DRIVEN PUBLICITY STUNT--ATIKU 

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has condemned the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day fuel discount at NNPC stations, describing it as a desperate, temporary gesture that cannot repair the damage caused by the crushing cost of fuel.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said the Tinubu administration’s attempt to dangle a fuel subsidy as bait for Nigerians was reckless, disgraceful and scandalous.

He said the same government had watched Nigerians endure excruciating hardship without offering meaningful relief. Now, as the election draws closer, President Tinubu is dangling a temporary discount at the very epicentre of the cost-of-living crisis that has tormented households and businesses.

“Atiku totally rejects this calendar-scheduled, election-laced subsidy package. Nigerians are not fools to be offered a month of discounted fuel after years of punishing prices and then expected to forget the hardship when the discount expires. This is shameless and heartless,” he said.

Atiku said the proposed 30-day discount was not an economic plan but a political bandage on a wound the government had helped create.

“What happens on Day 31? Nigerians wake up to the same brutal prices, the same punishing transport fares and the same rising cost of food. The government cannot manufacture relief for one month and expect Nigerians to applaud while the hardship remains,” he said.

He noted that the offer is limited to NNPC stations, while the government has yet to state how much motorists will save per litre or guarantee that any savings for transport operators will be passed on to passengers through lower fares.

The former Vice President said the administration’s sudden reversal on this sensitive social welfare issue was itself an admission of guilt over the hardship Nigerians have endured. It also exposed the weakness of the government’s repeated claims that meaningful relief was impossible.

“This volte-face proves that the production-support proposal I have advanced is workable, achievable and not complicated. The Tinubu government and its spin doctors have tried to make it sound impossible, yet they are now reaching for a temporary subsidy-style intervention because the pain has become impossible to ignore,” Atiku said.

He reiterated his proposal for capped and budgeted production support tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, with safeguards to ensure that the benefit reaches consumers and supports local refining.

“Nigerians need lasting relief, not a countdown to the return of hardship. Tinubu’s government cannot spend years telling Nigerians to endure, then offer 30 days of relief and call it a solution,” he said.

Atiku restated his commitment to making life affordable again.

Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again.

@phrankangel Shaibu 
Director of Strategic Communication
ADC Presidential Campaign Council.
8th October, 2026
